# hqc — technical specification

Version 0.262, 2026-11-25. Status: the architecture agreed after six reviews and a survey of
similar systems (§22), before implementation started. Changes are in §23, old versions in
`SPEC-CHANGELOG.md`. Marks: **[decision]** — decided, needs confirmation;
**[verify]** — needs checking on a real build.

Terms: **turn** — one cycle "input → agent work → final answer"; it starts with a
`user.message` or a `peer.message` with `mode=ask` and ends with an
`agent.message` with `final: true`. **Bare model** — an LLM with no access to the file
system. **Takeover** — continuing (resuming) a session somewhere else: from VS Code to hqc
or back. **Hermes** — Hermes Agent by Nous Research; on llm-server it runs as a
daemon (messaging gateway) and can also be started as a separate process acting as an
ACP server (`hermes acp`). **ACP** — Agent Client Protocol (Zed), JSON-RPC over stdio
between a client and an agent: `initialize`, `session/new`, `session/prompt`,
`session/update`, `session/request_permission`, `session/cancel`, `session/load`.
**Worker owner** — the user who enrolled the machine. **Session
owner** — the user who created the session.

## 1. Goals and scope

hqc is a single interface for running projects with LLM agents from any device.
The agents physically run on different machines and operating systems; the user talks to them
through a Discord-like web client: projects, sessions inside projects, an agent in a session.

What hqc does:

- keeps projects, sessions and the full event history in one place;
- starts and drives agents on the machine where the code lives and the hardware is attached;
- shows sessions started in VS Code and lets you take them over from a phone;
- gives agents tools to exchange messages, artifacts and requests with each other;
- lets colleagues in as separate users with explicit sharing.

What hqc does not do:

- it does not implement the agent loop for Claude Code and ACP agents: the loop lives in the
  runtime. For a bare model the hub runs a minimal loop "model ↔ hqc MCP tools" (§8.3);
- it does not duplicate what Hermes offers (agent task cron, kanban, memory, Telegram);
- it is not an IDE: no file editor, diffs only as artifacts;
- it gives no hard isolation between sessions on one machine without a container or a
  separate OS user (§14).

## 2. Topology

**Hub** — one always-available service. Keeps state, routes events, serves the
API to clients and workers. Runs only bare models (§8.3).

**Worker** — a daemon on every machine where agents should run. Connects to the hub
outbound only, over WebSocket. Inside: a native Claude Code adapter, a generic ACP adapter
for Hermes and any agent from the ACP registry, the hqc MCP server, the VS Code session mirror,
workspace operations, a local config with restrictions and environments.

**Client** — a web app, later Tauri and mobile. Talks only to the hub.

Deployment: the hub sits in the home DMZ behind Cloudflare Tunnel. People sign in through
Cloudflare Access (SSO), workers through a separate route with their own tokens (§6, §20).

### 2.1 Threat model

- The worker does not trust the hub for `allowed_roots`, environments, bindings and
  `allow_foreign_sessions`; the user's identity and answers to permission requests come from
  the hub and are trusted **[decision]**. The hub is the root of trust for conversations and
  permissions: whoever controls the hub can answer `allow` to any `approval.request`, write to
  any session and pass any session off as the worker owner's (`owner_is_worker_owner`). Nor
  for `session_secrets` (since 0.147, §14): the worker takes secrets only when its own
  `worker.toml` says so; the hub passes a secret through and keeps it nowhere, but it sees it in
  memory while it does, so whoever controls the hub sees the secrets given while they do (and
  could put a key of theirs into a workspace's keys, which gives the agent nothing but access to
  where that key opens).
- Consequences of a hub compromise: remote code execution on every connected
  worker as its owner, within `allowed_roots` and whatever the agent's tools allow
  (Bash can leave the workspace) — the hub starts a session, sends input and answers `once`
  to the permission request itself; plus reading all conversations, the transcripts
  in events and the push subscriptions. The protection is the hub itself: Access, tunnel only
  (in OIDC mode since 0.68: the provider's sign-in, only the reverse proxy reaches the hub), no
  open ports (§20). Signing input and answers with device keys registered on the worker
  locally is iteration 3+.
- The hub **cannot**: go outside the worker's `allowed_roots` (also not through an agent's
  `hqc_attach` or the `files` of `hqc_send`/`hqc_ask`: the worker resolves and reads the path
  itself, §7; files that reach a worker from the hub are written only into its own
  `.hqc/inbox`, §5.3, §12; a clone goes only into a new folder the worker checks itself, from
  `https`/`ssh` or a `file` URL inside `allowed_roots`, and only a folder the worker created
  and listed itself is ever deleted, never one because the hub named it, §5.3, §13; since 0.58,
  T45; a worktree only of a git workspace the worker knows, into a new folder checked the same
  way, and it is removed only by `git worktree remove` in the origin the worker recorded, since
  0.60, T46; a moved session's transcript goes only to the place of a folder the worker accepts
  for `session.start`, only from where Claude Code wrote it inside `allowed_roots`, and never
  over another file, §8.1, since 0.75), pick an environment or a
  Hermes profile for a path the worker owner has not bound locally, hand a session an ssh key
  (since 0.57 only an environment's `ssh_keys` give a process an ssh-agent, and without them it
  gets none, not even the user's), or enable
  the machine's MCP servers. These are set only by the worker's local config (§14): since 0.56
  (T43) `session.start` carries no environment, the worker resolves it from the canonical
  workspace path on every start, and what the hub shows about environments is a display. Nor
  can it run a
  session in the `auto` permission mode on a worker with `[permissions] allow_auto = false`
  (since 0.42, T38), or in `allow_all` on a worker without `[permissions] allow_all = true`
  (since 0.129, off by default): the worker runs the highest mode it allows and reports it.
  Where they are allowed, a hub that switches a session to one gains nothing it did not have
  (it can answer `once` itself); the worker's `deny` stays in force in every mode. The same holds for hqc's allow rules of a folder
  (since 0.52, T48): standing answers the worker applies after its `deny`, never over it. In an
  environment with `project_settings` (since 0.83, §14) a repository's own hooks run outside the
  worker's `deny` and without an approval request, so a hub that clones a repository of its
  choice into one of that environment's folders runs that repository's code there.
- The promise about local MCP servers holds for Claude Code (`--strict-mcp-config`)
  and Hermes (`HERMES_ACP_SKIP_CONFIGURED_MCP=1`, the worker always sets it). For other
  ACP agents there is no general way: in the local config each `acp_agent` declares
  `isolation: verified | none`; an agent with `none` is not allowed into foreign sessions
  (§11.1) and the promise does not extend to it.
- A worker is remote code execution on the owner's machine. Anyone who can write
  to a session on this worker runs code as the owner within the owner's policy.
- Between sessions of one worker the boundary is soft (§14): the processes run as the same
  OS user and can read each other's environment and files. Since 0.39 (T36) the hqc tools are
  not part of that softness: the session token is on the agent's command line, readable by the
  other sessions' agents, but the worker's MCP socket accepts a session's token only from a
  process that descends from the agent process the worker started for that session (§7.2).
  What stays soft: files, the environment, and anything an agent can do through another
  session's own processes (ptrace where the OS allows it to the same user; macOS restricts it,
  Linux with `ptrace_scope` 1 limits it to descendants).
- An agent acts with its owner's rights (§7), so a prompt-injected or compromised agent can do
  whatever the owner's hqc tools allow on the owner's sessions, and no more: every tool
  resolves its targets among the owner's projects and sessions only (`not_found` otherwise).
  What it can spend is capped (since 0.39, T36; §20): `mcp.call` per session and per worker,
  open asks, peer messages per session and minute and per chain, spawned sessions, schedules
  and their runs, searches, the bytes a worker uploads. Chains (§7.1) bound loops between
  agents; a schedule an agent creates continues its chain, so an agent cannot keep itself
  running by scheduling its own next turn. A message cannot raise permissions (since 0.43,
  T39; §7.1): a turn an agent starts in another session (a peer message, the prompt of
  `hqc_spawn`, a run of its schedule) runs at most in the lowest mode of that session and
  every session up the chain (`ask` < `auto` < `allow_all`, since 0.129), so a session in
  `ask` gets no turn run without asking through one in `auto` or `allow_all`, nor one in
  `auto` without the classifier through one in `allow_all`; since 0.44 (T40) neither through
  a buffered send nor through a schedule made while it ran in a higher mode. What such a turn
  leaves running (a background subagent or command, a wake-up) goes on in the session's own
  mode after it (§7.1). The hub computes the cap and the worker applies it; a compromised hub could
  lift it, as it can answer requests itself (above). On a worker with `allow_subagent_messages`
  (§8.1, since 0.84) an agent can also start a turn in another Claude session that accepts
  messages from other sessions (a local one of the same machine; per §8.1 **[verify]** also the
  account's cloud and Remote Control sessions), past the hub and these limits.
- A worker is trusted for its own sessions only (§5.2, §20): it writes their agent events and
  mirrored records, but no event that only the hub writes, nothing in another worker's
  sessions, and no `chain` or `delivery` (since 0.39: the hub drops them from a worker's
  events and keeps a mirrored record's `delivery` only as `delivered` on a typed prompt), so
  it can neither reset the chain limits of its sessions' turns nor queue input. A worker of the
  same owner can still use the owner's hqc tools through its sessions' tokens, within the caps.
- A publication (since 0.209, `hqc_publish`, §7, §12) is public: anyone who has its link opens
  it, without Access or the sign-in, until its owner unpublishes it or deletes the session (or
  the project) that published it. Only the session owner's `once` on the card of the session's
  request (in its chat, the Requests list or the feed of a session or room waiting on it)
  publishes, whatever the session's mode and `auto_approve`; a compromised hub can
  answer that card itself, as any request. The worker packs only files whose canonical paths
  lie inside the folder and `allowed_roots` (a link pointing out is refused by its name). The
  hub trusts the archive no more than that: it opens it with limits (§20) and serves it only on
  the publication domain (`HQC_PUBLISH_BASE`), a host apart from the hub's and the artifact
  domain that answers nothing but published files and `/health`, under a sandbox CSP: the page
  has no origin of its own, sees no cookies, reaches no API of the hub and loads only its own
  files. The link is a random id, not derived from the content: it cannot be found from the
  files or from another publication.
- A colleague with access to a shared project is limited by grants (§11) and by the worker
  owner's confirmations (§10).

## 3. Data model

Every entity has `id` (uuid v7), `created_at`, `updated_at`. `owner_id` exists on Worker,
Project, Workspace, Session, Artifact, Grant, ScheduledMessage. An Event has no owner;
it has `author`.

### User
`email` (from the verified Cloudflare Access JWT, in OIDC mode the provider's ID token, §6),
`oidc_sub` (since 0.68, OIDC mode only: the provider's `sub` the user is bound to on the first
OIDC sign-in, §6; hub migration `0031_oidc_subject`), `display_name`, `api_keys`
(OpenRouter, Anthropic API; encrypted with the hub's master key, which lives in the hub's
env/file, not in the database), `timezone`, `personal_project_id` (the implicit personal
project, created on first sign-in; the personal assistant session lives in it), `theme`,
`look`, `project_sort`, `new_session_project_id`, `quick_messages`.

`theme` (since 0.51, T49) — the client's base palette: three dark ones, `warm` (default) |
`graphite` | `contrast`, and since 0.88 their light counterparts `warm_light` |
`graphite_light` | `contrast_light`; one for the whole app and the same on every device of the
user (`PATCH /api/me`, §6). The client applies it at start (until `/api/me` answers, the one
last applied on this device, kept in the browser's storage as `hqc.theme`; without it `warm`)
and after a change.

`look` (since 0.114, hub migration `0039_user_look`) — how dense the client draws everything:
`compact` | `spacious` (default), the same on every device of the user (`PATCH /api/me`, §6).
Compact is the feed across the whole chat column in one column, as the VS Code tab draws it,
the platform's UI font instead of Inter, each project's full name on the project bar and a line
per session in the session list; Spacious has none of that (§6 client layout). The client
applies it as `theme`: until `/api/me` answers, the look last applied on this device
(`hqc.lookName`), without it `spacious`.

`project_sort` (since 0.114, hub migration `0040_project_sort`) — the order of the project
bar: `custom` (default; the user's own, `PUT /api/me/project_order`, §6) | `name` (by the shown
name) | `recent` (by the latest activity of the project's sessions), the favorite projects
first in each; the same on every device of the user (`PATCH /api/me`). The hub stores it and
keeps `GET /api/projects` in the user's own order; the client sorts by it, and until
`/api/me` answers uses the one last shown on this device (`hqc.projectSort`), without it
`custom`.

`new_session_project_id` (since 0.188, hub migration `0053_new_session_project`) — the project a
quick-started new session opens in: a foreign key to the user's own `projects` row, null until
the user picks one in Settings and again when that project is deleted (`ON DELETE SET NULL`);
the same on every device of the user (`PATCH /api/me`, §6). The hub stores it; the client uses
it only while the project is on the bar, else the user's personal project, so there is always
a target and no "none" choice (§6 client layout, the phone and Settings).

`quick_messages` (since 0.255, hub migration `0061_user_quick_messages`) — the user's own quick
messages: texts (`text[]`, empty by default) that every project's chat offers before the
project's own (§3 Project `quick_messages`, §6 client layout), in the order the user keeps them,
the same on every device (`PATCH /api/me`, §6). The same rules as a project's list: each at least
one character other than whitespace and at most 10 000 characters, at most 100.

`timezone` (since 0.38, T35) — an IANA name, `UTC` until set; the default zone of new
schedules (§16). The client sets it to the browser's zone (`PATCH /api/me`, §6) when it starts
and the two differ.

### Worker
`owner_id`, `name`, `os`, `token_hash`, `status` (online/offline), `last_seen`,
`protocol_version`, `boot_id` (from the last `hello`, §5.2), `capabilities` (`claude_code: {version, sessions_registry?, moves?, login?}`, `acp_agents[{name,
version, load_session, resume, image, isolation}]` — the result of each agent's `initialize`
when the worker starts), `local_models[]`, `share_local_models`, `allowed_roots[]`,
`environments[]` (since 0.56 `{name, allow_local_mcp?, mcp_servers? (0.262), permissions {unblock?, allow?, deny?, remote_unblock? (0.246)}}`,
never the values of `env`; `default` is implied), `env_bindings[]` (`{path, environment}`; the
Hermes profile in iteration 10),
`allow_foreign_sessions`, `idle_timeout`, `system_session_id` (§10.2), `machine_hash` (since 0.23:
the machine fingerprint from enrollment and the last `hello`, §5.1; not part of the API worker object),
`session_secrets` (since 0.147, hub migration `0044`: its `worker.toml` has `session_secrets = true`,
§14; from the last `hello`), `browser` (since 0.148, hub migration `0045`: its `worker.toml` has
`browser = true`, §14; from the last `hello`).

`system_session_id` — the worker's service session (§10.2). It is created together with the
worker when enrollment is confirmed (`POST /api/workers/enroll/confirm`); for workers older than
0.17 by hub migration `0006`, and if it is still missing, on `hello`. The hub tells the worker in
`hello.ack` (`system_session_id`); `GET /api/workers` returns it in the worker object. Revoking
the worker does not delete the session but archives it (the history stays, §10.2); enrollment
with replacement (§5.1) unarchives it; deleting a revoked worker (§6) deletes it together with
the worker.

Enrollment with replacement (§5.1) keeps the worker's `id`: `name`, `os` and `token_hash` come
from the new enrollment, `revoked_at` and `boot_id` are reset; sessions, workspaces and the
service session stay on this `id`.

The fields `allowed_roots`, `environments`, `env_bindings`, `allow_foreign_sessions`,
`share_local_models`, `acp_agents` — **the source of truth is the worker's local config**;
the hub keeps a copy from `hello` for display and early validation.

### Project
`owner_id`, `name` (1–100 characters), `slug` (unique per owner, does not change on
rename), `description`, `default_workspace_id` (nullable),
`session_template` (§13.3), `is_personal`, `color`, `icon`, `archived_at`, `quick_messages`. A project's first
workspace becomes its `default_workspace_id`; when the default workspace is deleted, the
earliest of the remaining ones takes its place. The personal project (`is_personal`) cannot be deleted or renamed (`409
personal_project`); its other fields can change; any number of new projects can be created.
Deleting a project deletes its workspace records and sessions (with events, as in §17.4); agent
processes get `session.kill`; folders and transcripts on the workers are left untouched.

`color` and `icon` (since 0.51, T49) — the project's appearance in the client; the personal
project has them too. `color` is one of `teal`, `plum`, `blue`, `rose`, `moss`, `coral`, `cyan`,
`slate` (the client's `theme.ts`; no yellows, amber means "waiting for you"); not set, the API
gives the one at index FNV-1a-32(the id's 16 bytes) mod 8 of that list, so it is stable.
`icon` is `{kind: emoji, value}` (1–8 characters, at most 32 bytes), `{kind: letters, value}`
(1–2 characters, kept in upper case) or `{kind: image, url}`; absent, the client shows the first
letters of the name. The image is stored on the hub in its own table (not an artifact: it
belongs to no session, the artifact cleanup does not touch it, it goes with the project), one
per project; `url` is `/api/projects/{id}/icon?v=<first 16 hex of its sha256>`. Setting an emoji
or letters drops a stored image. Limits: §12.

`archived_at` (since 0.110, hub migration `0038_project_archive`) — since when the project is
archived, null while it is not: put away from the project bar (`GET /api/projects` leaves it
out, `?archived=1` lists it, §6) and nothing else. Its sessions, workspaces, favorites and
order stay as they are: its sessions are not archived and stay in `GET /api/sessions`, an agent
of it keeps working, and it opens, takes new sessions and is changed like any project. Archiving
it again keeps the first time; the personal project is not archived (`409 personal_project`).

`quick_messages` (since 0.167, hub migration `0049_project_quick_messages`) — the project's quick
messages: texts (`text[]`, empty by default) the chat's quick-message button sends to the agent
with one press, in the order the user keeps them, always in the project object. Each is one
message as typed: at least one character other than whitespace, at most 10 000 characters; a
project keeps at most 100. The personal project has them too.

### Provider
Since 0.144 (iteration 5): a model provider of a user, an Anthropic-compatible endpoint
(`<base_url>/v1/messages`) with one model behind it: a local model behind a proxy such as
gpu-arbiter, a GLM at z.ai, an Anthropic API key. `owner_id`, `name` (letters, digits, `-` and
`_`, unique per owner; the `[providers.<name>]` a worker allows, §14), `label` (shown in the model
menus), `base_url` (`http://` or `https://`, stored without a trailing `/`), `model` (every model
name of the runtime goes to it), `context_tokens?` (the model's window, for the runtime's
compaction; absent — the runtime's own assumption), `created_at`, `updated_at`; hub migration
`0043`. Nothing in it is secret: a key, if the endpoint needs one, is only in the worker's
`worker.toml`. A session's `provider_id` (nullable) names the provider its agent runs on; null —
the runtime's own endpoint and `model`. The hub keeps a provider in use (`409 provider_in_use`
on delete) and hands its description to the worker in `session.start.provider` (§5.3); the
worker runs it only if its `worker.toml` allows the name with the same `base_url` (§14), since an
endpoint sees the agent's whole context and decides its tool calls. The worker's `providers[]`
from `hello` (§5.4) are the names it allows.

### Workspace
`project_id`, `worker_id`, `path`, `label`, `environment` (a name; a display of the binding
from the worker's local config: since 0.56 the hub sets it from the worker's `env_bindings` when
the workspace is created and on every `hello`, by the rule of §14; the worker never reads it), `ephemeral`, `created_by_hqc`, `kind`
(dir/clone/worktree), `origin_workspace_id` and `branch` (since 0.60, T46; hub migration `0029`),
`mirror_enabled` (since 0.23 `true` by default: the
Claude Code session mirror is on for every workspace; the switch is `PATCH`, §6, §9.2), hqc's allow
rules, `state` and `error` (since 0.58, T45; hub migration `0028`).

`state` — `ready` (the folder exists; every workspace before 0.58), or for a folder hqc makes
(`kind: clone` or `worktree`, `created_by_hqc: true`) `creating` while the worker clones or adds
the worktree and `failed` when it
could not, with the worker's reason in `error`; only the record is left then (the worker removed
what it had created). Only a `ready` workspace takes sessions (`409 workspace_not_ready`) and gets
`mirror.set` and `workspace.rules`; a `creating` one is not deleted (`409 workspace_creating`).

`origin_workspace_id` (since 0.60, T46) — for `kind: worktree`, the workspace it is a git worktree
of: a `ready` workspace of the same project and worker that is not a worktree itself (decided for
T46: one level, so the tree in the client is two levels and deleting goes worktrees first). While
any worktree record names it, the origin is not deleted (`409 workspace_in_use`, §6). `branch` —
the worktree's branch, or the branch a clone was asked for (T45's `clone_branch`, renamed by
`0029`).

`ephemeral` (since 0.61, T47) — a worktree `hqc_spawn` made with `isolation: "worktree"` for the
session it started (§7); otherwise like any worktree (sessions can be started there, the same
deletion). It is **never deleted automatically**. `marked_for_deletion` — not stored: the hub
computes it when serving, true for an `ephemeral`, `ready` workspace without a session that is
not archived. So archiving its last session marks it, unarchiving (or a new session there) clears
the mark, and a worktree whose spawn gave up before the session was created (§7) is marked from
the start. The client shows a marked workspace for deletion (§6), and deleting it goes through
the dialog of §13.2.

hqc's allow rules (since 0.52, T48; decided 2026-10-31: per folder, not per project or worker) —
standing answers of the workspace owner (the worker owner in iteration 4) to the permission
requests of every session in the folder, stored on the hub (table `workspace_rules`, migration
`0025`) and applied by the worker in `can_use_tool` after its `deny` (§8.1, §14). A rule is a
strict subset of Claude Code's syntax, so the worker's matcher reads every rule exactly: `Tool`
(a whole tool, `mcp__server` or `mcp__server__tool`; never `Bash` or another tool that runs
commands), `Bash(<words>)` (exactly that command), `Bash(<words> *)` or `Bash(<words>:*)` (the
command with any arguments); `<words>` are words of letters, digits and `-_./=+,@%:~` separated by
single spaces, without quotes, shell operators or a `*` other than the final one
(`hqc_proto::rules`). Limits: §20. The rules never go into `--settings`, so a change needs no
restart and reaches running sessions at their next request. The rules screen (§6) shows them with
the rules the worker reads for the folder (`worker.toml`, `~/.claude/settings.json`, in an
environment with `project_settings` (§14) the folder's `.claude/settings.json`,
`.claude/settings.local.json`); the hub keeps no copy of those.
A workspace is a **logical** boundary: all hqc operations (session cwd, inbox, mirror,
deletion) are confined to its path. It gives no enforced file system isolation.
A workspace is a hub object **[decision]**: all the worker knows about it is that its path lies
inside `allowed_roots` (checked on `fs.stat` and on every `session.start`, §5.3), and since 0.58
whether it created the folder itself (`created_workspaces.json`, §14).
`path` — the canonical path the worker returned for `fs.stat` (symlinks resolved).
A folder belongs to exactly one project: on one worker workspace paths are unique and not
nested in each other (compared by path components: `/a/b` and `/a/bc` do not overlap);
a new path that equals an existing workspace, lies inside it or contains it gets
`409 workspace_conflict` (§6). On different workers the same path means different folders.

### Session
`project_id`, `owner_id`, `workspace_id` (nullable; since 0.16 required on creation —
sessions without a workspace (§8.4) cannot be created through the API yet; only the worker's
service session has no workspace, §10.2), `worker_id` (the workspace's worker;
required for Claude Code without a workspace; null for a bare model; ACP agents without a
workspace are not allowed, §8.4), `cwd` (a relative path inside the workspace, `.` by default),
`title`, `title_source` (`default` | `runtime` | `user` — who set the title), `slug`
(unique in the project, does not change on rename; a move to another project keeps it when it
is free there and appends `-2`, `-3`… otherwise), `agent` (since 0.148 with `browser`: the owner
gave the agent their Chrome on the worker's machine, §14; hub migration `0045`),
`auto_approve`, `wake_on_send` (true by default since 0.55, T52, and on every session made before it, hub migration `0027`; false before), `locked_by` (none/hqc/vscode),
`last_seq`, `archived`, `archived_at` (nullable; since 0.53, T50: when it was archived, cleared
on unarchive; null for sessions archived before hub migration `0026`, the client then shows no
time; in the API session object as `archived_at?`), `vscode_active_at` (nullable; when the hub last received a mirror
event with `recent` — a write to the file within the last 30 s; it is how quiet is measured for
a takeover without registry data, §9.3; not part of the API session object), `held_by` (nullable
`{entrypoint, status}`: a live Claude Code process outside hqc that has the session's transcript
open, according to the live sessions registry on the worker, §9.3; in the API session object and
in `session.summary` it is the field `held_by?`), `vscode_held_at` (nullable; since when the
transcript has been held; not part of the API session object), `system` (bool: the worker's
service session, §10.2; the API session object carries only `system: true`), `spawned_by`
(nullable; since 0.37, T34: the session whose agent created this one with `hqc_spawn`, §7, and
since 0.172 a room's agent's room, or the session whose agent made a room with `hqc_room`;
cleared when that session is deleted) and `spawn_chain_id` (nullable: the chain of that call,
§7.1, kept for the spawn limits of §20; not part of the API session object),
`permission_mode` (nullable `ask` | `auto` | `allow_all`; since 0.42, T38, `allow_all` since
0.129, migration `0042`: the mode hqc asks the worker to run the agent in, chosen on creation
and switched with `PATCH`; null — the worker's `[permissions] mode`, §14) and
`effective_permission_mode` (nullable, the same values: the mode the worker last reported the
agent runs in, `session.state.permission_mode`, §5.4; what the client shows),
`permission_capped_by` (nullable; since 0.43, T39: while the worker runs the current turn
below the session's own mode under its input's cap, §7.1, the address of the session up the
chain whose mode set it, from `session.state.capped_input`, §5.4), `subagents` (since 0.70: the subagents the agent
runs now, from `session.state.subagents`, §5.4; 0 after a worker restart),
`background_tasks` (since 0.104: the background tasks the runtime lists for the agent now,
from `session.state.background_tasks`, §5.4; 0 after a worker restart), `output_per_s` (since
0.122: the session's latest `tokens.rate`, §4; absent — 0, also after its worker disconnects),
`paused_at` (nullable; since 0.160, migration `0050`: when the session was paused, then, once the
hub itself stops its agent for the pause, when it did; a process that ends another way keeps the
time of the pause; cleared on resume, §17.3), `pause_cut_turn` (since 0.191, migration `0054`:
the pause stopped a turn that was running; false while the session is not paused, §17.3),
`room_mode` (nullable `conversation` | `council`;
since 0.172, migration `0051`: set only on a room, a session with no workspace, no worker and no
agent whose agents are sessions of their own, §7.1.1) and `room_id` (nullable; since 0.172: on
an agent's session, the room it belongs to, §7.1.1; the session is deleted with the room).
In `ask` a tool call outside the worker's rules is asked about (§10.1); in `auto` Claude Code's
classifier decides and never asks (§8.1); in `allow_all` Claude Code runs it without the
classifier and asks only about a call an `ask` rule of its settings files matches and where
it asks in every mode, its own safety checks and tools that need a person (§8.1); the
worker's `deny` stops a call in every mode. `state` and
`queue_len` (§17.1) are **not stored**; the hub computes them when serving. In the first version
a session has exactly one agent; people's access to a session is determined by Grant only.

Title: creating without `title` gives "Session N" (N — the session's ordinal number in the
project, archived ones included; `slug` — `session-N`) with `title_source: default`; `title` on
creation, `PATCH title` and an agent's `hqc_rename` (§7) set `user`. The hub applies a title from the runtime
(`session.state.title`, §5.4; for Claude Code — `ai-title`, §8.1) and sets `runtime` only if
`title_source` is not `user`: the runtime does not rename a session the user has renamed.

Title from the worker (since 0.23, T21; since 0.25, T24 — on the worker's Claude Code
subscription; the hub has no model providers of its own). After the first final `agent.message`
of a session with `title_source: default` (from the worker or from the mirror: an imported
session likewise, by the first `user.message` records and the final `agent.message`) the hub
sends the session's worker a `title.request` in the background (§5.3) with the first message and
the first answer, each cut to 2000 characters. The worker runs Claude Code once outside the
session (§8.1) and answers with a title of up to 60 characters in the user's language. The hub
waits 30 s for the answer; worker offline, `error`, an empty title or a timeout go only to the
log, and the title becomes the first non-empty line of the first prompt without Markdown markup,
cut at a word boundary to 60 characters with "…". The hub folds the worker's answer to one line
of up to 60 characters. The title is set with `title_source: runtime` and only over `default`
(checked at write time): a user's or runtime (`ai-title`) title that arrived earlier or while
the worker was thinking is not overwritten; an `ai-title` that arrives later replaces it by the
general rule. One `title.request` per session per hub process.

Mirror (§9): `locked_by` — who drives the session: `hqc` — the worker's process (from a takeover
or the first input until it stops), `vscode` — a foreign holder or writer of the transcript
(VS Code, `claude` in a terminal), `none` — nobody. A session created by the mirror gets
`runtime_session_id` = the file's uuid, `cwd` from the record relative to the workspace, the
title from `ai-title` (`title_source: runtime`) or "Session N", `locked_by` per §9.1. It is
looked up by the pair (`worker_id`, `runtime_session_id`).

Move (since 0.75): a Claude Code session continues in another folder of its worker, usually in
another project, as the same conversation (`POST /api/sessions/{id}/move`, §6; the agent itself
with `hqc_move`, §7, since 0.76). Its `project_id`, `workspace_id`, `cwd` (`.`) and possibly
`slug` change, so its address `<project-slug>/<session-slug>` (§7) changes too; the old
project's saved list order forgets it (a move to another folder of the same project keeps its
place there). Its `runtime_session_id` stays: the worker moves the transcript to the new folder
(§8.1). Not to another worker.

### Agent (embedded in Session)
`runtime` (claude_code / acp / bare / none; `none` — only for the worker's service session
and, since 0.172, a room: there is no agent and no process starts, §10.2, §7.1.1), `acp_agent`
(the agent's name from the worker's local config, for `acp`), `model` (since 0.74 also switched
with `PATCH`, §6),
`runtime_session_id` (a string: the jsonl uuid for
Claude Code, an arbitrary id for ACP agents), `process_state`
(stopped/starting/running/stopping), `system_prompt` (since 0.172 set on creation for a room's
agent, §7.1.1; it goes in `session.start`, §5.3), `disallowed_tools[]`,
`restricted` (§8.4), `start_failures` (a counter, §5.2). Changing the runtime between turns
means **a new runtime session with an empty context**: `runtime_session_id`
is reset, the hqc history stays, and the user is offered a recap of the
last N messages as the starting prompt.

### Event
`session_id`, `event_id` (uuid; for events produced from Claude Code jsonl records —
by the adapter, the mirror and the import alike — it is a uuid v5 of the record's `uuid`, so
the same fact from two sources yields one `event_id`; if a record has several content
blocks, block 0 gets v5 of `uuid` and block `i > 0` gets v5 of the string `"<uuid>/<i>"`
in the same namespace; the rule is mandatory for all three sources (§9.2); since 0.98 the
question card the mirror builds from block `i` gets v5 of `"<uuid>/<i>/clarify.request"` and
`"<uuid>/<i>/clarify.response"` (§9.1);
for everything else — v7 from the sender), `seq` (assigned by the hub, monotonic within the
session), `ts`, `author` (`{kind: user|agent, id}` or `{kind: system}` without `id`; for an
agent `id` = its `session_id`), `type`, `payload`, `chain` (`{chain_id, depth, hops,
permission_cap?, capped_by?}` for agent→agent chains, otherwise null; the cap since 0.43, §7.1), `client_op_id` (echoed back to the client), `delivery` and
`delivered_at` — two flat event fields, only on `user.message` and `peer.message`:
`delivery` ∈ `pending | delivered | failed | withdrawn`, `delivered_at` — the delivery time;
`withdrawn` (since 0.219) is a message its owner took back before the agent took it (§17.2): it is
delivered to nobody. The hub's reads for a client (the pages of `GET .../events`, the backlog of a
subscription) still return it with `delivery: withdrawn`, so that a device that missed the `delivery`
frame learns of it, and a client's timeline shows no such message; every read for the agent or a
search (`hqc_read`, a fork's copy, the search, the title, the turn marks) leaves it out. A
`user.message` also has a column of the hub's own, not in the event JSON: `handed_at` (since 0.219, migration
`0055`) — when the hub
first sent the input to a worker (set before the `session.input` goes, and kept); an input that was
ever handed over may be held by the worker across a reconnect, so the hub alone withdraws only one with
no `handed_at` (§6). Since 0.112
the hub also sets `payload.joined: true` on a person's `user.message`, since 0.172 on a
room's input to its agent (§7.1.1) and since 0.174 on a `peer.message` of mode `send`, when it
is delivered into the turn already running (§17.2), with `delivery`; no other field of a stored
payload changes.

### ReadCursor
`user_id`, `session_id`, `last_read_seq`. The source of "unread" (the rule is in §6).

### Favorite
Since 0.74: `user_id`, `session_id` | `project_id`, `created_at` — a session or a project the
user starred; two tables, a row goes with its user, session or project (hub migration
`0033`). Favorites are the user's own: another user's star on the same object is never shown,
and starring does not touch the session's `updated_at`. The session object, `session.summary`
and the project object carry `favorite_at?` (the row's `created_at`) for the requesting user.

### Artifact
`owner_id`, `session_id` (the first session whose input carried the artifact; null until then),
`kind` (file/image/diff/html/text; since 0.209 site — the zip of a page or a file that
`hqc_publish` uploads, §7), `mime`, `size`, `sha256`, `name` (the last path component
without control characters, up to 255 bytes), `storage_key` (= `sha256`: the content on
disk is shared by all records with the same hash). A record is unique by `(owner_id, sha256,
name)`: the same file from the same user under the same name is the same record; since 0.128
an upload of it that names a `kind` gives the record that kind. A `site` is not (since 0.209):
every `hqc_publish` uploads a record of its own, so two publications of the same files are
unpublished apart. A `site` is published while `published_at` is set, with `public_id` — 128
random bits as 32 lowercase hex characters, unique — the first segment of its link (§12);
unpublishing clears both (migration `0052`). A published `site`'s `session_id` is the
publishing session, set when it is published; deleting that session, or its project, sets it to
null and takes the publication down (§12). The hub
separately remembers which sessions received the artifact in their input: their workers may
download it (§5.3, §12). Events refer only to `artifact_id`; download links are issued at render
time (§12). Unused artifacts are removed by the hub's cleanup (since 0.23, §12); `updated_at` is
the last upload of the same file or the last input with it.

### Grant
`owner_id` (who granted), `resource_type` (project/session), `resource_id`, `user_id`,
`level` (view/write/manage).

### PendingRequest
Open requests that survive a hub restart: `kind`
(approval/clarify/ask/worker_approval/move/secret/follow/publish/mcp_call), `session_id`,
`request_id`, `payload`, `expires_at`, `from_session_id`, `from_event_id`, `worker_id`
(for ask and mcp_call: whom to give the result to), `result` (filled in when the answer has
been received but not yet delivered to the worker).

A row is one per `(session_id, kind, request_id)`, and since 0.225 an open row's `request_id` is
the session's alone: the hub opens no request whose `request_id` an open request of another
kind of the session has. An answer (`POST /api/sessions/{id}/requests/{request_id}`, §6) names
its request by the id alone, so a worker's card under the id of a publication or a move the
owner is asked about would have the owner's Allow land on that one. A worker's `approval.request`
or `clarify.request` opens its row before the event is stored; one refused this way is not
stored (`ack` without `seq`, §5.2) and shows no card. Since 0.239 an agent's call whose
request the hub would open this way (`hqc_publish`, `hqc_move`, `hqc_secret`, `hqc_ask`) is
answered at once with `unavailable` ("the request id of this call is held by another open request
of this session") instead of waiting as for a repeat; an `hqc_ask` is checked before its message is
stored, so the target gets nothing. A worker's own request (§10.2) refused this way is refused to
the worker. A follow, whose `request_id` the hub derives itself, shows no card. A repeat of a
request of the same kind is as before.

An `ask` (since 0.35, T32) is a row of the **asking** session: `session_id` — the asking
session, `request_id` — the `mcp.call`'s, `worker_id` — the asking session's worker,
`payload` — `{target_session_id, event_id, to}` (`event_id` — the `peer.message` it put
into the target, `to` — the target's address; since 0.47, T42, `joined?` — the `event_id`s of
the target's `hqc_send`s to the asker that go with the reply, §7.1), `expires_at` — the ask's
timeout, `result` —
the `mcp.result` frame once it is answered, timed out or closed by a worker restart (§7.1).
`from_session_id`/`from_event_id` stay unused; `mcp_call` is not used: `hqc_send` keeps no
row of its own (§5.2).

A `move` (since 0.76) is a row of the session whose agent's `hqc_move` waits for the owner's
answer (§7, §10.1): `request_id` — the `mcp.call`'s, `worker_id` — the session's worker,
`payload` — the hub's `approval.request` in the session's feed plus `move: {path, project,
turn}` (the folder, the call's `project`, the chain of the call's turn, §7.1), no `expires_at`
(the call itself ends at the runtime's tool timeout, `ask_timeout_s` plus a minute, §7.2, and its
`mcp.cancel` closes the row),
`result` — the `mcp.result` frame once the move was carried out or refused, the owner denied it
or the hub cancelled the request. An allowed move closes the row first, without a `result`, and
fills it in when the move is done. On start, before it serves anything, the hub finds every
such row closed without a `result` that carries the owner's mark (the previous process stopped
while it carried the move out; the owner's `once` closes the row and puts `allowed_by`, the
owner's id, into its `payload`, and a row a cancellation closed without a frame has no mark; the
session's feed is not consulted, a worker's own approval may reuse the request id), keeps them
in memory by the row's `worker_id`, and carries each out once that worker sends `hello`, when
the move can be done; rows of this process are never among them. A hub that failed to store the
result carries the move out again at once. Either way a move already done answers as a repeat,
and the input after it is stored once (§7).

A `follow` (since 0.95) is a row of the session whose transcript is continued in a workspace of
another environment, waiting for the owner's answer (§9.2, §10.1): `request_id` — derived from
the session, the workspace it is in now (a fixed marker for none) and the target workspace, so
one per move from here to there, no `worker_id`, `payload` — the hub's `approval.request` in the
session's feed plus `follow: {workspace_id, cwd}` (the target, the record's `cwd` relative to
it), no `expires_at`, no `result`: no call waits for it. At most one is open per session. Only
the owner's answer closes it, and is used once: an allowed move is made by the answer, and a
closed row means records ask nothing more about that move.

A `secret` (since 0.147) is a row of the session whose agent's `hqc_secret` waits for the owner
(§7, §10.1): `request_id` — the `mcp.call`'s, `worker_id` — the session's worker, `payload` —
the hub's `approval.request` in the session's feed (`tool: hqc_secret`, `description` — the
agent's purpose, `secret: {name, kind, vault?, vault_field?, reads_vault?}` — `vault` (since
0.216) the Vaultwarden entry the agent named, kept only when the session's worker reads
Vaultwarden (§14); `vault_field` (since 0.243) the field of it the agent named and `reads_vault:
true` (since 0.243), with an entry or without, only when that worker also reads fields
(`vault_fields`, §5.4) — the one option
`deny`), no `expires_at` (the call ends
at the runtime's tool timeout, as a move's), `result` — the `mcp.result` frame once the owner
gave it (`POST /api/sessions/{id}/secrets` with `request_id`, §6: the worker's note, the path or
the key's fingerprint) or declined it. The runtime's `mcp.cancel` and a worker restart close the
row without a frame. Nothing of the secret is in it.

A `publish` (since 0.209) is a row of the session whose agent's `hqc_publish` waits for the
owner's answer (§7, §10.1), as a `move` is: `request_id` — the `mcp.call`'s, `worker_id` — the
session's worker, `payload` — the hub's `approval.request` plus `publish: {artifact_id, caption,
entry}` (`entry` — the name of the one file of an archive of a file, else null), no
`expires_at`, `result` — the `mcp.result` frame. An allowed publication closes the row first,
without a `result`, and fills it in once published. On start, before it serves anything, the
hub carries out at once every such row closed without a `result` that carries the owner's mark
`allowed_by`, as a `move` does (a publication needs no worker); the result goes to the worker
when it is connected, or after its `hello`. A publication done before the stop answers from its
`attachment` with the link the artifact has then.

### ScheduledMessage
`owner_id`, `session_id` or (`project_id`, `workspace_id`, template), `cron` or `at`,
`timezone`, `message`, `enabled`, `last_run`, `catch_up`.

Since 0.38 (T35; table `scheduled_messages`, migration `0018`): `session_id` only — the
project-template variant waits for session templates (backlog); exactly one of `cron` (5
fields) and `at` (a time); `timezone` — an IANA name, the owner's `timezone` when not given;
`next_run` — when it is due next (UTC), null once it will not run again (an `at` that ran or
was skipped); `catch_up` false by default. Deleting the session deletes its schedules.
Since 0.44 (T40, migration `0023`): `created_by` — the session whose agent made the schedule
(`hqc_schedule`), not part of the API object; null for a person's schedule, and once that
session is deleted (the schedule stays). Its runs are capped by that session's mode (§16).

## 4. Event schema

One schema for all runtimes. The adapter translates the runtime's stream into these events;
the client renders only them. The "source" column is the component that produces the event;
`author` is set per §3. `?` marks an optional field: it is absent when there is no value
(`null` reads the same).

| type | payload | source |
|---|---|---|
| `user.message` | `text` (since 0.69 the client shows it as typed, line breaks kept, without Markdown), `artifact_ids[]`, `quiet?` (since 0.231: `true` once the worker wrote the message into the agent's history without a turn at the owner's Stop, set by the hub on `ack {quiet: true}`, §5.2, §17.2; absent when false; the feed stands it behind its `joined_after`, where Claude Code recorded it, §6), `schedule_id?` (since 0.38: sent by the hub cron for that `ScheduledMessage`, §16; the client marks it "scheduled"), `during_text?` (since 0.108, set by the hub: the agent's text or (since 0.208) its thinking was being written when the input came; absent when false; §6), `joined?` (since 0.112: `true` once the runtime took the message into the turn already running, written by the hub on the worker's `ack {joined: true}`, §5.2, §17.2; absent when false; the client marks it "joined the turn"), `joined_after?` (since 0.221, with `joined` or (since 0.231) `quiet`, set by the hub in the same write: the `seq` of the last event of the session that is no `user.message` or `peer.message`, stored before the hub took the ack, when it is past the message's own; absent when there is none and on a message joined before 0.221; §6), `resume?` (since 0.160: `true` on the note of a resume, §17.3; absent otherwise), `restart?` (since 0.256: `true` on the hub's note after a worker restart, §17.3; absent otherwise), `human?` (since 0.219: `true` on a message the owner typed in `POST /api/sessions/{id}/input` (§6), written there and nowhere else, so it is absent on a hub's own note (a resume, `hqc_move`, subagent leftovers, long runs), a run of a schedule, a room's post to its agent and a message from the Claude Code transcript; it is what Take back and Send now require (§6, §17.2) and what the worker writes Claude Code's `origin: human` for (§5.3, §8.1)) | client; hub cron (§16, authored by the owner; since 0.39 the run of an agent's schedule has its `chain`, §7.1); hub after `hqc_move` (§7, since 0.76: authored by the owner, with the call's chain); hub on a resume (§17.3, since 0.160: authored by the user who resumed); hub on `session.subagent_leftovers` (§8.1, since 0.203: authored by the session's owner, no chain); hub on `session.long_runs` (§8.1, since 0.244: authored by the session's owner, no chain); hub after a worker restart (§17.3, since 0.256: authored by the session's owner, no chain); mirror — prompts from the Claude Code transcript (§9.1) |
| `agent.delta` | `text`, `reset?` (since 0.161: `true` when the runtime abandoned the attempt that wrote the text so far, which the hub and the client drop, and (since 0.208) the thinking being written with it, §6, §8.1; `text` is then empty; absent when false), `thinking?` (since 0.208: `true` for a piece of the agent's thinking being written, not of its answer; absent when false; §6, §8.1) | adapter; transport only, not written to the database |
| `subagents.live` | `agents[{task_id, description, activity?, total_tokens?, tool_uses?, duration_ms, call_id?, kind?, stoppable?, due_in_ms?, retry?}]` | adapter (since 0.113); transport only, not written to the database: the subagents the agent runs now (those of `session.state.subagents`, §5.4), the whole list each time, in the order they started, then (since 0.127) the main agent's background shell commands and (since 0.169) Monitor watchers, in the order they became rows, then (since 0.169) the wakeup the agent armed and its cron jobs, empty when none (§8.1); since 0.181 a task the CLI marks `ambient` is no row, and the commands and subagents it starts are rows as the agent's own (§8.1). `description` is the subagent's task, `activity` what it does now (absent before any progress), `total_tokens` and `tool_uses` its counts so far, `duration_ms` how long it has run when the list was sent, `call_id` (since 0.135) the `call_id` of the `tool.call` that started it (absent before the runtime names it; the client finds a subagent's card in the feed by it, §6), `stoppable` (since 0.161; absent when false) that the runtime stops it alone on `session.stop_task` (§5.3), which a subagent's row, a command's and (since 0.169) a Monitor's say, `retry` (since 0.179) `{attempt, max_retries, retry_delay_ms, error_status?}` while its request to the model API failed and waits to be retried (`error_status` absent: the attempt got no response; §8.1), `kind` (since 0.141; absent from an older worker, an unknown value reads as "unknown") `agent` for a subagent's row, `command` for a command's and, since 0.169, `monitor` for a Monitor's, `wakeup` for the agent's wakeup and `cron` for one of its cron jobs; a command's or a Monitor's row carries only `task_id`, `description` (its Bash call's description, or the command; the Monitor's description), `duration_ms`, `call_id?`, `kind` and `stoppable`; a wakeup's and a job's row also `due_in_ms` (since 0.169), the milliseconds until it fires when the list was sent, by the worker's clock, 0 once due, absent on a job whose next fire is not known |
| `tokens.rate` | `output_per_s` | adapter (since 0.122); transport only, not written to the database: the output tokens per second (text, thinking and tool input; reading context does not count) the agent and its subagents spent over the last 20 s (a subagent's response counts when it ends), sent when it changes, 0 once no turn and no subagent runs and when the agent's process stops, and (since 0.179) again, unchanged, at each heartbeat of a long call of the main agent (§8.1, §17.3) |
| `schedules.live` | `schedules[{schedule_id, message, due_in_ms, cron?, at?, timezone}]` | hub (since 0.169); transport only, not written to the database: the session's enabled schedules (§16) that have a next run, the whole list each time, the next one first, empty when none. `due_in_ms` is the milliseconds until the next run when the list was sent, by the hub's clock, 0 when due; `cron` is the pattern of a recurring schedule and `at` the time of a one-off, `timezone` the zone of the schedule. A worker sending one is refused (`error invalid_frame`, §5.2) |
| `agent.message` | `text`, `final`, `in_reply_to?` (event_id of the input that started the turn), `runtime?` (since 0.69: `true` for a reply the runtime wrote itself instead of the model — an API error, "Credit balance is too low"; absent when false), `interrupted?` (since 0.161: `true` for a reply an interrupt cut off before the runtime finished it — Stop, "No" to a permission request, §8.1; absent when false; the client shows it muted with " · interrupted" after its time), `refusal?` (since 0.168: `true` for the runtime's reply to a model refusal, Claude Code's with `stop_reason: "refusal"`; absent when false) | adapter. `final: true` — end of the turn; `final: false` — text between tool calls. A `runtime` message is held and ended like any other text (§8.1), so it is the turn's final message when it ends the turn; the client shows it as a service line, not as the agent's text. Under a `refusal` one, while no message of the user stands after it in the feed, the session is not archived and VS Code does not hold it (`locked_vscode`, whose chat has no input), a small "Switch model" opens a model menu: the families, each with its versions in a submenu, "Another model…" and the providers the session's worker allows (§6), the session's model checked, without Claude Code's default, which a running agent is not switched to (it takes it at its next start, §5.3 `session.model`). The checked entry itself (an alias, or the version in its family's submenu) only closes the menu; a family checked for one of its versions switches to its alias, and any other choice switches the session as the header's model pill does, and once the hub took it the line says "Switched to <model>. Send the message again." in the button's place, until a `system model_not_switched` after the choice (§8.1) brings the button back. Since 0.54 (T51) the final message that answered an `hqc_ask` carries, from the hub to clients only, `reply_delivered_at` beside `delivered_at` once the asking worker acknowledged the reply (§6, §7.1) |
| `agent.thinking` | `text` | adapter, if the runtime provides it |
| `tool.call` | `call_id`, `tool`, `args_preview` | adapter |
| `tool.result` | `call_id`, `result_preview`, `error` (bool), `error_text?` (short error text; since 0.194 an opened call row in the client shows it only when it is not the start of `result_preview`, which the Claude Code adapter cuts from the same text), `duration_ms?`, `artifact_id?` (a diff or a large result, §12; since 0.180 the Claude Code adapter's whole text of a result longer than `result_preview`, its first 2 MiB, kind `text`, §8.1), `artifact_ids[]?` (since 0.180: the result's images, kind `image`, in order; absent when none, §8.1) | adapter |
| `approval.request` | `request_id`, `tool`, `description`, `args_preview?`, `options[{id, label, canonical, grant?}]`, `expires_at?`, `policy_hint?` (allow/deny), `rule_suggestions?[{part, rule?}]`, `secret?{name, kind, vault?, vault_field?, reads_vault?}`, `subagent?{task_id, description}` (since 0.181: the subagent that asks, §10.1; absent for the agent itself and a subagent the adapter does not know) | adapter; `options` are **the agent's real options**, `canonical` ∈ once/session/always/deny/deny_always for the client's buttons (since 0.213 also the option ids `server_session` and `server_always`, canonical `session` and `always`, on an MCP tool's card, §10.1); `args_preview` (since 0.207) — the call's arguments as `tool.call.args_preview` carries them (the same limit and form), so a card that does not stand right after its call (a subagent's, another session's, one in the Requests list) shows the whole command and every argument; absent from an older worker; `grant` of an option (since 0.207) — what choosing it grants besides this call: `{place, rules?[], exact?}`, `place` ∈ `session` (the worker's session rules, until the process ends) / `local_settings` (Claude Code writes the rules to `.claude/settings.local.json` at the root of the git repository containing the session's cwd, §8.1), `rules` — as Claude Code writes a rule, `toolName` or `toolName(ruleContent)`, at most 10, each at most 256 bytes (a rule cut there ends with `…`; past 10 the tenth item is `… N more`, the count of the rules not listed, which the option grants as well), `exact` — the exact call is allowed too; no field — the option grants nothing more (`once`, `deny`) or the worker does not say; `policy_hint` — the call matches an `allow` or `deny` rule of the worker's `[permissions]` block (§14); no field — it matches neither; the client labels the card with it; `rule_suggestions` (since 0.52, T48) — the hqc rules the worker suggests for "Allow in this folder" (§10.1): one per simple part of a Bash command (`rule` absent when it has none for that part), the tool name for another tool; absent for a session without a workspace and for a command the worker's matcher cannot split; since 0.180 `reason?` — why the runtime asks (Claude Code: `decision_reason`, at most 1024 bytes; since 0.217, for a call an ask rule caught, the rule's tool and settings file, §8.1), `display_name?` — the runtime's name of the tool (at most 256 bytes), both absent when blank, and `human_only?` — `true` when only a person may answer it (§8.1): its `options` are `once` and `deny`, it has no `rule_suggestions`, and the hub's `auto_approve` leaves it to the owner (§10.1); absent when false. The client shows `reason` under the card's title and names the tool by `display_name` when there is one, an MCP server's tool as `<tool> (<server>)` (the runtime's `display_name` of one drops the server); `secret` (since 0.147) — only in the hub's card of an `hqc_secret` (`tool: hqc_secret`, `author {kind: system}`, §7): the name and kind (`secret`, `ssh_key`) asked for and, since 0.216, the Vaultwarden entry the agent named and, since 0.243, the field of it the agent named (`vault_field`) and `reads_vault` (§7); the hub drops it from a worker's event |
| `approval.response` | `request_id`, `option_id`, `by` (user id or `auto`), `message?` (the user's text instead of the call, only with a `deny`/`deny_always` option, §10.1) | client, or the hub with `auto_approve` |
| `approval.cancel` | `request_id`, `reason` (timeout/stopped/worker_restart/archived, since 0.180 withdrawn — the runtime withdrew its request, §8.1; the client says "withdrawn") | adapter, worker or hub. An answer from another device is not a cancellation: the first answer closes the request, the second gets `409 request_closed` (§10.1) |
| `clarify.request` | `request_id`, `questions[{id, text, header?, options?: [string], option_descriptions?: [string], option_previews?: [string], multi?: bool, required?: bool, input?: "integer" \| "number"}]`, `subagent?{task_id, description}` (since 0.181, as on `approval.request`) | Claude Code adapter: the `AskUserQuestion` tool arrives as `can_use_tool`, the answer goes into `updatedInput.answers` (verified on 2.1.307 with `--permission-prompt-tool stdio`, §8.1). Since 0.69 `header` is the question's short label and `option_descriptions` what each option means, in the order and number of `options`, `""` for an option without one; each is absent when empty. Since 0.199 `option_previews` is each option's mockup (an ASCII sketch, code, a config) by the same rule, cut by the worker to 8 KiB with `\n… (truncated)` after it. The client shows `header` above the question, each description under its option, and an "Other" field: its text is the answer (with `multi`, an item of the array beside the checked labels); "Other" chosen with nothing typed is sent as `"Other"`, as the VS Code tab does. As in the tab, "Answer" stays disabled until every question has an answer: an option picked, a text typed (not only spaces) or "Other" chosen. A question with a preview shows it as plain text in `<pre>`, never rendered as markdown or HTML, not wrapped and scrolling sideways: on a desktop in a column beside the options, the preview of the option last under the pointer while the pointer is over the question (the "Other" row lets it go) or of the option with the keyboard focus (kept while the focus is in the preview), else of the first chosen one, else the first one that has a preview, the column as tall as the tallest preview of the question; on a phone under each chosen option that has one. ACP agents have no source for it. Since 0.180 also an MCP server's request for input (Claude Code: `elicitation`, §8.1), with `server?` — the server that asks, `message?` — its text, `url?` — the page it sends the person to, then with no `questions`; a question of its form carries `required: true` for a field the server requires and `input` (`integer`, `number`) for a free-text field whose answer must read as one, both absent otherwise and in the agent's questions; the client heads the card "<server> asks", shows the text above the questions, "required" beside a required question's header, the link (only an http, https or mailto one as a link, labelled with the address it opens, a host in its punycode form), no "Other", the submit button ("Done" for a link, the card then saying "Done"; unlike the agent's questions it waits only for what the form's schema says, which a server on the MCP SDK checks the answer against, refusing one that does not match (§8.1): every `required` question answered, an `integer` answer an optional minus and digits, at most 2^53 − 1 in size, a `number` one written in decimal (an optional minus, digits with an optional point, an optional exponent) that JavaScript's `Number()` reads as a finite number; a field neither required nor answered may stay empty) and "Decline" |
| `clarify.response` | `request_id`, `answers` (`{<question id>: string \| [string]}`), `action?` (since 0.180, only for a request with `server`: `accept` — the answers, also none, are the input; `decline` — the person declined, `answers` empty; the client shows "Declined"). Since 0.246 the event of an answer to a request with `server` keeps `answers: {}`: a server's form may ask for a token, so its answers go to the worker in the frame only, and the hub's copy of the frame forgets them once the worker acknowledges it; the card says that the answers go to the server only, and "Answers sent to <server>" | client |
| `clarify.cancel` | `request_id`, `reason` (the same set as for `approval.cancel`) | adapter, worker or hub |
| `attachment` | `artifact_id`, `kind`, `name`, `caption?` | the agent via `hqc_attach` (since 0.34, T31): the hub writes it, `author: {kind: agent, id: <session id>}`, `kind` and `name` of the artifact; since 0.181 also the worker after a background task's end, the task's output file (§8.1), with the same `author`, `kind: text`; since 0.209 also a publication the owner allowed (`hqc_publish`, §7), with `kind: site` (`event.attachment.site.json`); the user's files go into `user.message.artifact_ids` (rule below) |
| `peer.message` | `from_session_id`, `from?` (the sender's address `<project-slug>/<session-slug>` when it sent, since 0.35), `text`, `mode` (send/ask), `request_id?` (for ask: the `mcp.call`'s), `artifact_ids[]?` (since 0.46, T41: the files the sender gave with `files`, artifacts of the owner; absent when none; the target's worker downloads them like a user's attachments, §5.3, §12), `during_text?` (since 0.108, set by the hub: the agent's text or (since 0.208) its thinking was being written when the message came; absent when false; §6), `room?` (since 0.172: `{session_id, seq}`, on an input from a room to its agent, the room and the `seq` there of the message it carries, §7.1.1), `joined?` (since 0.172, on such an input, and since 0.174 on a message of mode `send`: as on a `user.message`, §17.2), `joined_after?` (since 0.221, with `joined` or (since 0.231) `quiet`: as on a `user.message`), `quiet?` (since 0.231: as on a `user.message`), `aside?` (since 0.172, on an agent's post in a room: `true` for the final message of a turn the CLI started itself, which moves no circle, §7.1.1; absent when false), `notice_seq?` (since 0.172, on a room's notice to a session that wrote in it: the room's last `seq` when the round ended, §7.1.1) | the hub on `hqc_send`/`hqc_ask`/`hqc_spawn` (since 0.37, the new session's first input) and, since 0.172, for a room (§7.1.1: the owner's message and a post to its agents, an agent's post in the room, a message of a session that is not one of its agents — `hqc_room`'s first message, an `hqc_send` to the room — and the room's notice to such a session when a round ends); `author` is `{kind: agent, id: <the sending session>}` (for the owner's message in a room, the room), `chain` is set (§7.1); `delivery: pending` in the input queue, none while in the send buffer (§7.1) or (since 0.47, T42) when it goes with the reply to the target's ask instead (§7.1); since 0.54 (T51) a buffered one gets `delivered_at` (still without `delivery`) when the input that carried it is acknowledged |
| `usage` | `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read?`, `cache_write?`, `cost_usd?`, `session_cost_usd?`, `session_tokens?`, `model?`, `context_tokens?`, `context_limit?`, `cache_ttl_s?` | Claude Code adapter on `result` (since 0.69 not on one with `num_turns: 0`, no tokens and no cost; since 0.115 one with `num_turns: 0` and no tokens, since 0.161 any with no tokens, unless a compaction came in it, carries no tokens, no `cost_usd` and the grown `session_cost_usd`, and the feed draws no line for it, §8.1; since 0.170 the `usage` of a compaction carries the growth of `modelUsage` as its tokens); for ACP agents optional and without `cost_usd` (ACP v1 has no standard usage). Since 0.28 (T27): `cost_usd` is the cost of this turn (since 0.115 with what background subagents spent after the previous `usage` with a `cost_usd` of the same process, since 0.161 also with what a turn with no tokens before it cost, §8.1); `session_cost_usd` is the runtime's own running total of the whole runtime session after the turn (Claude Code: `result.total_cost_usd`, carried over `--resume`), absent if the runtime has none (§8.1). The client's header shows the latest `session_cost_usd`, else the sum of `cost_usd`; since 0.162 plus the last `session_cost_usd` before each `system conversation_cleared` (after `/clear` the runtime counts from 0 again, §8.1), so it shows the whole session's cost. Since 0.229 `session_tokens` is the runtime's cumulative tokens of the whole runtime session after the turn — input, output, cache reads and cache writes summed (Claude Code: `result.modelUsage` summed over its models), on every `usage` the adapter sends (the turn's, the compaction's and the total-only one) whose `result` has a `modelUsage`, absent otherwise; the client's header shows the latest one plus the last one before each `system conversation_cleared`, as it does the cost, but with no fallback to summing turns (§6). Since 0.222 a `usage` that carries tokens (not the one with the total only) also says how full the main agent's context is and how long its prompt cache lives: `context_tokens` is the context after the turn's last API response of the main agent (§8.1), `context_limit` the tokens it may hold before the runtime compacts it by itself, `cache_ttl_s` the seconds the session's cache has left when the turn ends, counted from the request of the response (3600 or 300, less the seconds since the response started, 0 at the least); each is absent when the runtime does not say it. `context_limit` is the threshold of the model's window; an override of the auto-compaction window or a disabled auto-compaction is not seen in the stream (§8.1). The client's header shows them (§6) |
| `tasks` | `items[{subject, status, active_form?}]` | Claude Code adapter (since 0.223), stored: the agent's task list after a change, the whole list each time, empty when it has none. `status` is `pending`, `in_progress` or `completed` (another value reads as "unknown", shown as pending); `subject` and `active_form` are at most 512 bytes and the list at most 200 tasks; `active_form` is what the agent is doing while the task is in progress, as the runtime names it (Claude Code: `activeForm`), absent when it names none. The latest one is the list, the client shows it as a row above the input (§6), never as a feed item; the adapter sends one only when the list changed (§8.1) |
| `status` | `state` (§17.1), `detail?`, `in_reply_to?` (since 0.69: on the `idle` that ends a turn, the event_id of the turn's input once the runtime echoed it (§8.1; in 0.69 the input the adapter sent last once echoed), as on `agent.message`; a turn the runtime starts by itself after a background task carries the input before it; absent on other statuses and from older workers; the hub fails an `hqc_ask` by it, §7.1) | worker or hub; the Claude Code adapter sends `idle` with `in_reply_to` on `result` (§8.1; since 0.161 without `detail`: why a turn ended early is a `system` line, `turn_interrupted` or `turn_ended_early`, below), and since 0.121 `running` on the `system/init` of a turn the CLI starts by itself (§8.1) |
| `system` | `text`, `code`, `level?` (`warn` \| `error`, only on `worker_log`), `call_id?`, `status?`, `task_id?` (since 0.135, only on `task_notification`), `usage?{total_tokens, tool_uses, duration_ms}` (since 0.181, only on `task_notification`), `from_session_id?` (since 0.172, only on `room_passed`: the agent that passed), `trigger?`, `pre_tokens?`, `post_tokens?` (since 0.179, only on `context_compacted`), `model?` (since 0.179, only on `model_not_switched`) | hub or worker; codes below |
| `retraction` | `event_ids[]` | adapter (since 0.179): events of the session the runtime took back — Claude Code's answer of a model that refused, replaced by another model's answer (§8.1). The hub keeps of `event_ids` only the session's own `agent.message`, `agent.thinking`, `tool.call` and `tool.result` of the agent, at most 1024, and stores it with those; nothing is deleted: clients do not show the events it names, also ones loaded after it, nor the retraction itself; search (§15) still finds them |
| `side.question` | `text`, `during_text?` (set by the hub as on a `user.message`: the agent's text or thinking was being written when it was asked; absent when false; §6) | hub only (since 0.232): a side question the owner asked the session's agent with `POST /api/sessions/{id}/side_question` (§6, §17.5), authored by the owner, stored and sent to clients like any event; it has no `delivery`, and the agent is given neither it nor its answer as input. The feed shows it with its answer as one block |
| `side.answer` | `question` (the `event_id` of its `side.question`), `text?`, `error?` | adapter (since 0.232): the runtime's answer to that question, stored when it comes, authored by the session's agent; exactly one of `text` (the answer, as Markdown) and `error` (why there is none) is set. A question has one answer: the hub stores a worker's `side.answer` only when `question` is a `side.question` of the same session that has no answer yet (an answer sent again after a lost `ack` gets its `seq`), and acknowledges any other without a `seq`, as it does an event for a session that is not the worker's; a client shows the answer with the lowest `seq`. It stands outside the agent's turn: it opens none and closes none (§17.5) |

`system` codes (the list is open; the client shows an unknown code as text):

| code | source | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `session_created` | hub | the session was created (for one created by the mirror: "Session imported from Claude Code", §9.1) |
| `turn_lost` | hub | the turn was lost: the agent process stopped mid-turn, the worker restarted, or there have been no turn events from the worker for a long time (watchdog, "no events for N s"; §17.3) |
| `agent_exited` | worker | the agent process exited on its own with an error or mid-turn (§17.3) |
| `policy_denied` | worker | a tool call was rejected by a `deny` rule from the worker's `[permissions]`, without asking the owner (§8.1, §14); the client shows "Blocked by worker policy" |
| `task_notification` | worker (adapter; mirror) | since 0.69: a background task of the agent (a shell command, a subagent) finished or stopped; `text` is the runtime's summary of it (§8.1, §9.1). It comes when the task ends, before the answer of the turn the runtime then starts by itself. Since 0.135 `call_id` is the `call_id` of the `tool.call` that started the task, `status` how it ended as the runtime says it (Claude Code: `completed`, `failed`, `stopped`) and `task_id` the runtime's id of the task (Claude Code: a subagent's `agentId`), each absent when the runtime does not say; the card of a subagent's `Agent` call takes its end from it, and a subagent's notification (by `call_id` or by the `agentId` of its background launch, with a `status` that ends it) stands in the feed as the subagent's end card (§6). Since 0.181 `usage` is what the task spent (Claude Code: the notification's `usage`), absent when the runtime does not say, the end card shows it (§6), and the task's output file follows the notification as an `attachment` (§8.1) (adapter only: a mirrored session's notification has neither `usage` nor the attachment). The client folds any other into a "Background task ·" line ("Background task failed ·" for `status` `failed`, "Background task stopped ·" for `stopped`, since 0.181) with the whole text on one line, without its Markdown marks, dimmed in italics like the start of a thinking, cut with an ellipsis where the line ends, and (since 0.181) with `usage` at its right end as `· <tokens> tokens · <n> tools · <run time>`, as the row above the input has it (§6; since 0.205 on a phone `· <tokens> · <run time>`); opened, it shows all of it as Markdown. Since 0.186 the output file the notification is followed by (an `attachment` of kind `text`, named `<task_id>.output` after the notification of that `task_id`) is drawn inside the line, under its text once the line is opened, not as a block of its own; one in a turn that answers a question stays with that turn's attachments in its "Reply to" block (§6), and one whose line is not loaded is a card |
| `context_compacted` | worker (adapter; since 0.162 mirror) | since 0.69: the runtime compacted the session's context (`/compact`); since 0.118 `text` is the summary the runtime wrote, "Context compacted" without one (§8.1); since 0.162 the mirror gives the same line from the transcript's `compact_boundary` and its summary (§9.1); the client folds the summary into a "Context compacted" line that opens to all of it as Markdown, and draws one with the fixed text as a divider. Since 0.179 the adapter's carries, when the runtime said, `trigger` (`auto` \| `manual`), `pre_tokens` (the context's tokens before) and `post_tokens` (after; absent when the runtime did not count them) — the mirror's carries none of them —, and the client's line reads "Context compacted · auto · 153k tokens freed", leaving out what is absent |
| `compaction_failed` | worker (adapter) | since 0.179: a compaction the runtime started failed; `text` is "Compaction failed: " and the runtime's error, "Compaction failed" without one (§8.1) |
| `transcript_not_saved` | worker (adapter) | since 0.201: the CLI reported `system/session_writes_lost` with the session's transcript among what it could not write (`error_code` `ENOSPC`: "the disk is full", `EDQUOT`: "the disk quota is used up", another or no code: "a write to the worker's disk failed", the code named in the brackets when there is one, the fix "Check the worker's disk"); `text` "Transcript not saved: the disk is full (ENOSPC); resuming this session may miss part of its conversation. Free up space on the worker's disk", the quota's fix being "Free up space or raise the quota on the worker's disk"; the worker is not named, the chat header shows it. The client shows it as any other text line. The CLI sends the frame only when it exits with status 0 (§8.1, `close`), so a process that is killed reports nothing; a frame that lost only the global config is written to the worker's log, with no line (§8.1) |
| `conversation_cleared` | worker (adapter) | since 0.162: `/clear` started a new conversation in the same agent process, with a new transcript (Claude Code: `conversation_reset`, §8.1); `text` "Conversation cleared"; the session goes on in the new transcript, and the agent no longer has what was before the line in its context |
| `command_output` | worker (mirror; since 0.218 adapter) | since 0.162: what a slash command printed (`/context`, `/cost` and the like), from the transcript (Claude Code: `<local-command-stdout>` and `<local-command-stderr>`, §9.1); since 0.218 also from the adapter, the CLI's `<synthetic>` reply with `local_command_source` (§8.1); `text` is the output, at most 4096 bytes |
| `goal` | worker (adapter, mirror) | since 0.218: a record of the runtime's goal (Claude Code's `/goal`, §8.1); `goal` is `{condition, state, reason?, checks?, duration_ms?, tokens?}`, `state` one of `set`, `unmet` (a check found it not met yet; `reason` says why), `met`, `failed` (the check found it impossible), `cleared`; `checks`, `duration_ms` and `tokens` with `met` and `failed`: how many checks ran, how long and how many tokens it took since it was set or, after a `--resume`, since the CLI set it again; condition and reason at most 4096 bytes each; `text` as Claude Code's own UI says it: "Goal set: <condition>", "Goal not yet met… continuing", "Goal achieved", "Goal could not be achieved", "Goal cleared: <condition>". The client draws `met`, `unmet` and `failed` as lines, `set` and `cleared` as none (the command's own output says it), and while the last of them since the last `conversation_cleared` is `set` or `unmet`, the goal row above the input (§6) |
| `runtime_notice` | worker (adapter) | since 0.179: a message of the runtime or of one of its hooks ("Stop hook says: …", a setting applied in part); `text` is the message as is (§8.1) |
| `model_fallback` | worker (adapter) | since 0.179: the runtime went on with another model (unavailable, overloaded, or with the user's consent); `text` "<model> → <other model>" and the runtime's words after a colon (§8.1) |
| `model_refusal_fallback` | worker (adapter) | since 0.179: the model refused and another model answered; `text` as for `model_fallback`; the refused answer is taken back by a `retraction` (§8.1) |
| `model_refusal` | worker (adapter) | since 0.179: the model refused and no other model answered; `text` is the runtime's, or "<model> refused to answer" and the API's explanation (§8.1) |
| `model_not_switched` | worker (adapter) | since 0.179: the runtime refused a switch to the model the user chose (since 0.195 also the model it was started with, Claude Code's `model_restriction`, §8.1); `text` gives its reason and the model it kept, `model` that model, which the hub makes the session's model (`agent.model`) when it is a name hqc takes from the user (§6, §8.1) |
