  Code live sessions registry and reports holders (§9.3); `moves: true` (since 0.75) — the worker
  moves a moved session's transcript (§8.1), reported only when Claude Code's config folder
  (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude`) exists at the worker's start, where the transcripts
  are; the hub moves only sessions of such a worker (§6). `vault: true` (since 0.216) — its
  `worker.toml` has both `session_secrets` and `vault` (§14): `secret.put` may name a Vaultwarden
  entry instead of the value (§5.3); the hub keeps it with the rest of `capabilities`.
  `vault_fields: true` (since 0.243), sent with `vault` — the worker reads a field of the entry
  (`secret.put.vault_field`): an older worker ignores the field and would give the password, so
  the hub offers the field, and `reads_vault` on a card, only to a worker that sends it.
  `environments` (since 0.56, T43) — the environments of the local config (§14) as `{name,
  allow_local_mcp?, mcp_servers?, permissions {unblock?, allow?, deny?, remote_unblock?}}`, without `default` and never with the
  values (or the names) of `env`; `mcp_servers` (since 0.262) the names of its local MCP
  servers (§14), never a command, URL, header or value, absent when none; a plain string, as workers before 0.56 send, reads as an
  environment without rules. `env_bindings` — `{path, environment}`, the path canonical when it
  existed at the worker's start (`worker.hello.json`). The hub keeps both on the worker and sets
  each workspace's `environment` from the bindings (§3 Workspace).
  The worker does not report workspaces (since 0.16; the hub no longer reads the iteration 1
  field `capabilities.workspace_path`): workspaces are created in the hub (§3, §6) and checked by
  the worker against `allowed_roots`.
- `event` {event} → `ack` (`session_id` is inside the event)
- `session.state` {session_id, process_state, runtime_session_id?, locked_by, title?, held_by?, commands?,
  command_info?, permission_mode?}
  — `title`: the title the runtime gave the session (§8.1); the worker repeats the last one in
  every following `session.state`, the hub applies it by the `title_source` rule (§3 Session),
  folding it to one line of up to 200 characters. `held_by` — the transcript's holder (§9.3): no
  field — the worker has no registry data, `null` — nobody, `{entrypoint, status}` — a live foreign
  process. The session's `updated_at`, by which the session lists are ordered (§6), does not
  move on every `session.state` (since 0.145): `process_state`, `runtime_session_id` and
  `locked_by` move it only when they change what the hub keeps (`locked_by` after §9.3), a new
  `title` or holder as before; the `session.state` the worker sends again for every session
  after `hello` repeats them and keeps it, unless something changed while the worker was away.
  **Holder report** — a `session.state` with a nil `session_id`, the transcript's
  `runtime_session_id` and `held_by` (`process_state: stopped`, `locked_by: none` — the hub does
  not read them): the hub looks the session up by worker and `runtime_session_id` (none — only
  `ack`) and applies `held_by` per §9.3. Reports go through the outbox in the same order as
  `mirror.event`; the answer is `ack {}`.
  `commands` (since 0.28, T27) — the slash commands the runtime offers, names without `/`
  (Claude Code: from its answer to `initialize`, `commands_changed` and `system/init`, §8.1).
  Absent — not known yet; like `title`, the worker repeats the last list in every following
  `session.state`. The hub stores it on the session (only when it changed) and shows it in the
  session object (§6): names are trimmed, a leading `/` dropped, names with whitespace or
  control characters or longer than 100 characters dropped, duplicates removed, at most 500
  kept. `command_info` (since 0.162) — the same commands in the same order as `[{name,
  description?, argument_hint?}]`, what the runtime says of each (Claude Code: the first line of
  its description and its argument hint, §8.1), sent with `commands` (example
  `worker.session.state.json`); the hub takes it instead of `commands` and keeps the names by
  the rules above, each description and argument hint in one line (runs of whitespace one
  space) of at most 200 characters, an empty one absent. An older hub ignores it; from an older
  worker the hub keeps the names alone.
  `permission_mode` (since 0.42, T38) — `ask` | `auto` | `allow_all` (since 0.129), the mode
  the agent runs in: the one the worker started or switched it with, then what the runtime reports (Claude Code:
  `permissionMode` of `system/init` and `system/status`, §8.1); absent — not known yet;
  repeated in every following `session.state` like `title`. The hub stores it as the session's
  `effective_permission_mode` (§3).
  `capped_input` (since 0.43, T39) — the `event_id` of the input whose cap the current turn
  runs under while the cap is below the session's own mode (`permission_mode` is the cap's
  mode meanwhile: `ask` under an `ask` cap, `auto` under an `auto` cap of a session in
  `allow_all`); absent — no cap holds the session down now. Unlike `title`, absence means none:
  every report says it. The hub stores the `capped_by` of that input's cap (its chain's, or
  the send buffer's when that one is lower, T40) as the session's `permission_capped_by` (§3)
  and clears it on a report without the field and on a worker restart.
  `subagents` (since 0.70) — how many subagents the agent runs now (Claude Code: §8.1), 0 when
  it is stopped; absent — 0, and like `capped_input` every report says it. The hub stores it as
  the session's `subagents` and sets 0 on a worker restart.
  `background_tasks` (since 0.104) — how many background tasks the runtime lists for the agent
  now: its own background commands and monitors, its background subagents and their commands
  (Claude Code: the list of `background_tasks_changed`, since 0.166 without the tasks marked
  `ambient`, since 0.200 nor those marked `off_host`, §8.1), 0 when it is stopped; absent —
  0, and like `subagents` every report says it. The hub stores it as the session's
  `background_tasks` and sets 0 on a worker restart.
  `foreground_calls` (since 0.125) — the `call_id`s of the calls of the agent itself that the
  runtime runs in the foreground now and can move to the background (`session.background`,
  §5.3; Claude Code: §8.1), empty when it is stopped; absent — none, and like `subagents`
  every report says it. The hub keeps the list in memory, not in the database, as the
  session's `foreground_calls` (§6), and drops it when the agent stops, its worker restarts or
  the session is deleted; it keeps at most 64 unique ids of 1 to 128 bytes without whitespace
  or control characters, in the worker's order, and drops the rest (§20).
  `activity` (since 0.179) — what the agent waits on now, while no output of the model comes
  (Claude Code: §8.1): `{kind: retrying, attempt, max_retries, retry_delay_ms, error_status?}`
  — a request to the model API failed and is retried after `retry_delay_ms` (`error_status`
  absent: the attempt got no response); `{kind: compacting}` — the runtime compacts the
  context; `{kind: thinking, estimated_tokens}` — the model thinks, about that many tokens into
  its thinking block; a kind the hub does not know reads as none (a newer worker's), and the
  rest of the frame still reads. Absent — none, and like `subagents` every report says it; the worker
  sends a `session.state` whenever it changes, a new thinking estimate at most once per 2 s.
  The hub keeps it in memory, not in the database, as the session's `activity` (§6), and drops
  it when an event ends the turn, the turn times out or is lost (§17.3), the agent stops, its
  worker disconnects or says `hello` again, and when the session or its project is deleted.
- `mirror.event` {workspace_path, runtime_session_id, cwd, event, title?, recent, held_by?} — events
  from the mirror (§9.1, §9.2), through the outbox; the answer is `ack {event_id, seq}` as for
  `event` (a duplicate — the `seq` of the stored one; a folder not mirrored by this worker, a `cwd`
  outside it and the other refusals of §20 — without `seq`); a record of a new transcript over the
  daily limit gets `error mirror_quota`, `retryable: true` (since 0.24, §9.1).
  `workspace_path` — the path from `mirror.set`, `cwd` — the transcript's folder by the rule of
  §9 (an absolute path),
  `title` — the file's last `custom-title`, else its last `ai-title` (since 0.162; before, the
  last `ai-title`), `recent` — the file was modified less than 30 s before the worker read the
  record, `held_by` — the transcript's holder at the time of reading, as in
  `session.state`. The hub looks the session up by worker and `runtime_session_id` and creates it
  for an unknown one; it ignores `event.session_id` (the worker sets the nil uuid) and `author.id`
  and fills them in itself (for `system` — `{kind: system}`).
- `worker.approval.request` {request_id, kind, description, expires_at} → `ack {}` — an owner
  confirmation outside a session (`kind`: `workspace.use`, later `workspace.create`,
  `workspace.delete`; the list is open). The hub writes an `approval.request` to the worker's
  service session; a repeat with the same `request_id` after a reconnect writes no new event
  (§10.2).
- `mcp.call` {request_id, session_token, tool, args} → `mcp.result` (fast tools) or `ack {}`
  (deferred, §5.2); through the outbox without the token (since 0.33, T30)
- `mcp.cancel` {request_id, reason} → `ack {}` — a call that died on the worker's side
  (§5.2, §7.2); also a relay request below, which the hub then stops
- `mcp.upstream` {request_id, session_token, server, method, params} → `mcp.result` (since
  0.235) — a request of the relay of the owner's remote MCP server `server` (§5.3
  `mcp_servers`), `method` one of `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `params` as the CLI
  sent them (at most 64 KiB). Sent directly, never through the outbox, and only while connected:
  a call to a remote service is not made late; a lost connection fails the open ones on the
  worker ("may still have been carried out"). The relay asks only for a server its agent was
  started with. The hub checks the token as for `mcp.call` (the session must be this worker's),
  that the server is the session owner's and its project's, and answers `result` `{upstream:
  <the server's JSON-RPC result>}` or, for one over 512 KiB, `{upstream_artifact: {id, size,
  sha256}}`: an artifact of the owner linked to the session, which the worker downloads with
  `GET /worker/artifacts/{id}` and checks, removed after an hour; over 64 MiB, and every failure,
  is `error` `mcp_unavailable` (unreachable, an error of the server, a URL into a private
  address), `mcp_sign_in` (`401`/`403`: set the credentials again), `mcp_timeout` (the server's
  timeout; "the call may still have been carried out on the server: check before retrying") or
  `mcp_too_large`, which the relay gives the CLI as a tool error. `initialize` answers the
  server's `serverInfo` and `instructions` (cached per server for an hour), which the relay hands
  the CLI, so the server's instructions reach the agent's context; `tools/list` the server's
  tools (cached the same way, all pages); `tools/call` goes to the server in the MCP session of
  this session and server (below). The relay answers `ping` itself.
- `worker.limits` {five_hour?, seven_day?, status?, rate_limit_type?, resets_at?} → `ack {}`
  (since 0.81) — the usage limits of the account the worker's agents run on, each window
  `{utilization (0..1), resets_at (Unix seconds)}`: the 5-hour window ("Current session" of
  Claude Code's `/usage`) and the 7-day window of all models; since 0.179 the limit the account
  is nearest to: `status` (`allowed`, `allowed_warning`, `rejected`), which limit it is
  (`rate_limit_type`: `five_hour`, `seven_day`, `seven_day_opus`, …) and when it resets
  (`resets_at`). Sent whenever the runtime reports them (Claude Code: every
  `rate_limit_event`, §8.1). The hub keeps the latest per worker in memory, with when it came,
  and shows it in `GET /api/workers`; after a hub restart there is none until the next turn.
- `session.subagent_leftovers` {session_id, subagent, ended_s, commands[{task_id, description,
  running_s}]} → `ack {}` (since 0.203) — a subagent of the session's agent ended a while ago and
  commands it started still run (Claude Code: §8.1): `subagent` is its task, `ended_s` how many
  seconds ago it ended, each command its `task_id` in the runtime, its `description` and how many
  seconds it has run. Sent directly, once per such end, while the agent runs.
  The hub gives the agent a note as the owner's pending input (§8.1), unless the session is a
  room's or paused, or is not on this worker; it acks the frame either way.
- `session.long_runs` {session_id, tasks[{task_id, kind, description, running_s}]} → `ack {}`
  (since 0.244) — background commands or subagents of the session's agent that have each run for
  another `long_run_note` of the worker (§14; 55 minutes unless set; Claude Code: §8.1): `kind`
  is `command` or `agent` (a subagent), `task_id` the task's id in the runtime, `description` its
  description there, `running_s` the seconds it has run. Sent directly, one frame for all the
  tasks that reached their mark on one tick, while the agent runs. The hub gives the agent a note
  as the owner's pending input (§8.1), unless the session is a room's or paused, or is not on this
  worker; it acks the frame either way. A hub older than 0.244 answers it with `error
  invalid_frame`, so the hub is updated before the workers.
- `workspace.created` {request_id, canonical | error} → `ack {}` (since 0.58, T45) — the outcome
  of `workspace.create`: the folder is ready at `canonical`, or it was not made (`error`, a
  message for the user; nothing is left on disk). Sent directly when the clone (or since 0.60 the
  `git worktree add`) ends and again
  for every repeated `workspace.create`; the hub makes the workspace `ready` at `canonical` (and
  sends `mirror.set` when it is mirrored) or `failed` with the error (up to 2000 characters), and
  ignores an outcome for a workspace that is not `creating` any more.
- `result` {request_id, ...} / `error` to the hub's requests (`fs.stat`, `fs.list_dirs`,
  `workspace.list_candidates`, `title.request`, `permissions.inspect`, `workspace.inspect`,
  `workspace.delete`, §5.3), with the request's `id`.
- Artifact upload: HTTP PUT `/worker/artifacts` with the worker's token, not over WebSocket.
  Artifact limit **100 MB**, no chunking. Since 0.34 (T31), for `hqc_attach` (§7, §12): the
  body is the file, streamed, with `Content-Length`; `x-hqc-session-id` — the session it is
  for, which must be one the hub has on this worker (else `404`; the service session too);
  `x-hqc-artifact-name` — the name, percent-encoded as in the download; `x-hqc-artifact-kind?`
  and `Content-Type` as in `POST /api/artifacts`. The answer is the artifact (§6), `201`, or
  `200` for the same content under the same name. A bad token `401`, over the limit `413
  too_large`, an unknown `kind` `400`. Since 0.180 also a tool result's whole text and its
  images (§8.1), with their `Content-Type`. Since 0.209, for `hqc_publish` (§7):
  `x-hqc-artifact-kind: site` with the zip the worker packed, stored as `application/zip`; a
  `site` is always a new record (`201`).

## 6. Client ↔ Hub protocol

Authentication: the hub verifies the signature of the `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` JWT against
Cloudflare's JWKS (issuer and audience from the config) and takes the email from the token. An
email header without a JWT is not accepted. The worker route `/worker/*` is excluded from Access
and accepts only worker tokens; the human route `/api/*` accepts only Access JWTs (in OIDC mode,
below, the provider's ID tokens). The hub listens only on the tunnel interface (in OIDC mode,
only the reverse proxy reaches it).

OIDC mode (since 0.68), for a hub behind a reverse proxy that signs people in with an OIDC
provider instead of Cloudflare Access (Traefik forwardAuth with oauth2-proxy and Keycloak, for
example): `HQC_OIDC_ISSUER`, `HQC_OIDC_AUD`, `HQC_OIDC_JWKS_URL` and `HQC_OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS`,
all four, and `HQC_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` (§20). `/api/*`, the `/api/ws` WebSocket included, then
takes the provider's ID token from `Authorization: Bearer` and checks it the same way: an RS256
signature by a key of that JWKS, exactly that `iss`, the `aud`, `exp` and `nbf` (60 s of
leeway; `nbf` in Access mode too), and the email from the `email` claim;
`Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` is not read. On top of that the email counts only with
`email_verified: true` (Keycloak puts it in the ID token with the `email` scope), otherwise
`403`: the provider may let every account set its own email, and an account that set the
owner's would become the owner's hub user, with their workers. A token with a `typ` other than
`ID` gets `401` (Keycloak's access tokens are `Bearer`; other providers may leave `typ` out,
which passes), and so does one whose `aud` is an array without `azp` equal to `HQC_OIDC_AUD`
(OIDC Core 3.1.3.7). Only the emails of `HQC_OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS` (comma-separated, compared
case-insensitively) get in; another one gets the same `401` as an invalid token, before the hub
looks up or creates a user: any account of the realm with an ID token for the client, through
the proxy's sign-in or past the proxy, would otherwise become a hub user that enrolls workers of
its own. The hub user is keyed on the token's `sub` (§3 User `oidc_sub`); the issuer is fixed by
`HQC_OIDC_ISSUER`, so `sub` alone is the key. The user bound to that `sub` signs in; else the
user of the email is bound to it on this first OIDC sign-in (one from Access mode too), or is
created with it; if the user of the email is bound to another `sub`, the token gets the same
`401`. So an account whose email changes at the provider keeps its hub user (when the new email
is on the allow-list too), and another account that gets the same email verified does not take it
over. The proxy puts the token there (oauth2-proxy
`--set-authorization-header`) and lets `/worker/*` through without its sign-in. It must also renew the token before it expires: the hub refuses an
expired one with `401`, and oauth2-proxy keeps handing over the token it got at sign-in unless
`--cookie-refresh` is shorter than the token's lifetime (in Keycloak the Access Token Lifespan,
5 minutes by default). Only some of the four variables, an empty allow-list, no
`HQC_CLIENT_IP_HEADER`, an issuer or JWKS URL that is not `https://` (`http://` only to a
loopback host, the rule of `HQC_PUBLIC_ORIGINS`), or the variables together with `HQC_ACCESS_*`
or `HQC_DEV=1`, and the hub does not start.

Dev mode (local development without Access): `HQC_DEV=1` together with `HQC_DEV_USER=<email>`;
all `/api/*` requests come from that user. The hub refuses to start if `HQC_ACCESS_*` or
`HQC_OIDC_*` is also set or `HQC_HUB_LISTEN` is not loopback (`127.0.0.0/8`, `[::1]`, `localhost`); on start it
logs a loud warning (§20).

REST bodies and `/api/ws` frames are typed in `hqc-proto` (`api`, `client_frame`); the
contract examples are `examples/wire/api.*.json` and `client.*.json`; the hub and client tests
read them. Unknown fields are ignored in both directions.

HTTP API (iteration 1 and projects with workspaces from iteration 2; the list is not complete,
the rest is marked "later"):

- `GET /api/me` → `{id, email, display_name, timezone, personal_project_id, theme, look,
  project_sort, new_session_project_id, quick_messages, limit_notice_percent}` (`api.me.json`;
  `limit_notice_percent` since 0.190: the hub's `HQC_LIMIT_NOTICE_PERCENT`, the limit bar's
  threshold below, 70 from a hub before it); `PATCH /api/me` {timezone?, theme?, look?,
  project_sort?, new_session_project_id?, quick_messages?} (since 0.38, `api.me.patch.request.json`; an unknown
  zone: `400`; `theme` since 0.51, `look` and `project_sort` since 0.114, §3 User, another value:
  `422`; `new_session_project_id` since 0.188: a project that is not the user's or does not
  exist: `404`, nothing stored; `quick_messages` since 0.255: the whole list, replacing the stored
  one, a blank message, one over 10 000 characters or more than 100: `400`, nothing stored,
  not even another field of the request) → the same object;
  later keys; `PUT /api/me/project_order` {project_ids} (since 0.64,
  `api.project_order.request.json`) → `{projects[]}` in that order: the user's own order of the
  project bar, kept per user (`users.project_order`); ids that are not the user's projects and
  repeats are dropped. The bar has no archived projects (§3 Project), so since 0.110 an archived
  project the list leaves out keeps its place: right after the project before it in the order
  stored so far (the projects missing from it after it), when that one is in the list, else at
  its old index; restored, it comes back where it was. The reply has the projects that are not
  archived
- `GET /api/projects` → `{projects[]}` in the user's order, the projects missing from it last,
  oldest first (since 0.64; before it oldest first), without the archived ones (since 0.110);
  `?archived=1` gives the archived ones instead, in the same order
  (`api.projects.archived.json`), `POST /api/projects` {name, description?} → `201`
  and the project, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/projects/{id}` (`PATCH` {name?, description?,
  default_workspace_id?, color?, icon?, quick_messages?} — `default_workspace_id` a workspace
  of this project, otherwise `400`; `quick_messages` (since 0.167) a list that replaces the whole
  stored one (absent: unchanged, `[]`: none), a blank message, one over 10 000 characters or
  more than 100 messages is `400 bad_request` and changes nothing (§3 Project); `color` one of the 8 names and `icon` an emoji or letters within the limits
  of §3 Project, otherwise `422` (`{kind: image}` too: an image comes only by `PUT .../icon`);
  the personal project: `409 personal_project` on rename and delete, its `color` and `icon`
  change; `DELETE` → `204`, §3 Project).
  `POST /api/projects/{id}/archive` and `POST /api/projects/{id}/unarchive` (since 0.110, §3
  Project) → the project object: archived since now (again: the first time stays), or back on
  the bar in its place of the user's order; the personal project: `409 personal_project` on
  archive; another user's or a nonexistent project: `404`.
  The project object is `{id, owner_id, name, slug, description, default_workspace_id?,
  is_personal, color, icon?, created_at, updated_at, favorite_at?, archived_at?}`
  (`api.project.json`; `color` and `icon` since 0.51, `favorite_at` since 0.74, §3 Favorite,
  `archived_at` since 0.110, only on an archived project)
- `PUT /api/projects/{id}/icon` (since 0.51, T49; multipart: field `file`, like an attachment)
  → the project object with `icon: {kind: image, url}`: the image is checked as in §12
  ("Project icons"), anything else is `422 invalid_icon` with the reason in `message`; a body
  the multipart parser refuses: `400` with the parser's reason, `multipart: …` (since 0.109).
  `GET /api/projects/{id}/icon` → the image (§12). Another user's or a nonexistent project, or
  no image: `404`
- `GET /api/workspaces?project_id=` → `{workspaces[]}` (without `project_id`: all of the
  user's workspaces); `POST /api/workspaces` {project_id, worker_id, path, label?,
  mirror_enabled?, create?} → `201` and the workspace (`kind: dir`, §13.1): the hub sends the worker
  `fs.stat` (with `create` since 0.64: the worker makes a missing folder; it is an ordinary
  `dir`, `created_by_hqc: false`) and stores `canonical`; `mirror_enabled` (since 0.23 defaults to `true`; `false`
  means no mirror) controls the mirror and the import from Claude Code
  (`CreateWorkspaceImport`, §9.1): the hub sends the worker `mirror.set`, and when such a
  workspace is deleted, `mirror.set` with `enabled: false`. Worker not connected: `409
  worker_offline`, the workspace is not created; no reply within 10 s: `504
  worker_timeout`; path outside `allowed_roots`: `400 outside_allowed_roots`; no such path:
  `400 path_not_found`; not a directory: `400 not_a_directory`; the worker rejected the frame:
  `400 invalid_path`; the path equals a workspace of the same worker, lies inside one or
  contains one: `409 workspace_conflict` with body `{error, message, existing_workspace_id,
  existing_project_id, existing_path}` (`api.workspace.conflict.json`; the client says "this
  folder is already in project <name>" with a link). Since 0.58 (T45) `{kind: clone,
  project_id, worker_id, path, url, branch?, label?, mirror_enabled?}`
  (`api.workspace.clone.request.json`): `path` is the new folder; the hub checks `url` and
  `branch` as the worker does (`400 invalid_url`, `400 invalid_branch`), sends `fs.stat` of the
  parent (the codes above) and of the new path (`400 path_exists`), stores the canonical parent
  plus the name as `creating` with `kind: clone`, `created_by_hqc: true` (the same
  `workspace_conflict` check) and sends `workspace.create` (§5.3); `201` with the workspace
  `creating`, which the client reads again until it is `ready` or `failed`. Since 0.60 (T46)
  `{kind: worktree, project_id, worker_id, origin_workspace_id, branch, new_branch?, path?,
  label?, mirror_enabled?}` (`api.workspace.worktree.request.json`): the origin must be the
  user's `ready` workspace of this project and worker and not a worktree (`400 invalid_origin`,
  also without `origin_workspace_id`), `branch` passes `check_branch` (`400 invalid_branch`);
  without `path` the new folder is `<origin-parent>/<origin-name>-<branch>` with the branch's
  `/` as `-`. The path is checked as a clone's, the workspace stored `creating` with `kind:
  worktree`, `created_by_hqc: true`, `origin_workspace_id`, `branch`, and the hub sends the
  origin's `workspace.rules` and then `workspace.create` (also when it repeats it after
  `hello`); the worker's refusals (not a git repository, a branch checked out elsewhere, one
  that exists or does not) come back as `failed` with its reason. Another `kind`:
  `400`. `PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}` {label?,
  mirror_enabled?} → workspace (`api.workspace.patch*.request.json`): changing `mirror_enabled`
  is the "VS Code sessions" switch (since 0.23, §9.2); the hub sends the worker `mirror.set`
  (at once if connected, otherwise after `hello`); the same value sends nothing. `DELETE
  /api/workspaces/{id}?remove_folder=&force=` → `204`: the record, the folder is left alone
  (§13.2); while it has non-archived sessions: `409 workspace_in_use`, unless
  `archive_sessions=true` (since 0.64: the user confirmed it), which archives them first as
  `POST /archive` does (§17.4), before the folder is removed; archived ones lose
  `workspace_id` and cannot be unarchived (`409 no_workspace`); while it is `creating`: `409
  workspace_creating`; while worktree records name it as their origin (since 0.60, any state):
  `409 workspace_in_use` ("N worktree(s) of this workspace exist; delete them first"), checked
  before the worker is asked. `remove_folder=true` (since 0.58, T45) only for a `ready` workspace with
  `created_by_hqc` (else `400`): after the session check the hub sends `workspace.delete` (§5.3)
  and deletes the record once the worker answered; worker offline `409 worker_offline`, no
  answer in 60 s `504 worker_timeout`, refused by the worker `400 invalid_path` (also a worktree
  with uncommitted files without `force`) — the record stays in all three. `force=true` (since
  0.60, T46) goes into `workspace.delete` as `force`: the client sets it only when the dialog
  showed uncommitted files. `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/inspect` (since 0.58, T45) → the worker's
  `workspace.inspect` without `request_id` (`api.workspace.inspect.json`), only for a `ready`
  workspace with `created_by_hqc` (else `400`); offline `409 worker_offline`, no answer `504
  worker_timeout`. The workspace object is `{id, project_id, worker_id, path, label,
  environment, kind, origin_workspace_id?, branch?, ephemeral, marked_for_deletion,
  created_by_hqc, mirror_enabled, hqc_rules, state, error?, created_at, updated_at}`
  (`api.workspace.json`, `api.workspace.worktree.json`, `api.workspace.ephemeral.json`;
  `hqc_rules` since 0.52 — how many hqc rules
  the folder has; `state`, `error` since 0.58, §3 Workspace; a client reads a missing `state`
  as `ready`; `origin_workspace_id`, `branch` since 0.60; `marked_for_deletion` since 0.61, §3
  Workspace, a client reads a missing one as `false`). The client (project settings, `ProjectSettings.dc.html`): "Clone a repository"
  next to "Add a workspace" — the worker, the URL, the parent folder from the same folder tree
  (or typed), the folder name (the repository's by default) and an optional branch; a clone's
  row shows "Cloning…" (the list is read again every second meanwhile), then the workspace, or
  "Clone failed" with the worker's error and "Remove" (the record only). "Remove" on a ready
  folder hqc created opens a dialog with the worker's inspection — the uncommitted files ("and N
  more"), the branches with their commits on no remote, "not a git repository", or that nothing
  would be lost — and "Delete folder", "Remove from project only", "Cancel"; with the worker
  offline the check fails and only the record can be removed. Since 0.64 "Remove" on a
  workspace with non-archived sessions or worktrees opens the dialog too (for a folder hqc did
  not create: "Remove from project", "Cancel"): it lists the sessions, says they are archived
  with it and marks one with a turn on "running, will be stopped", and the removal sends
  `archive_sessions=true`; worktrees of it are listed to delete first, with the buttons off. Since 0.60 (T46): "New worktree"
  on a ready workspace that is not a worktree (the client cannot tell a git folder; the worker
  can, and the worktree fails otherwise) opens a form under its row — the branch, "New, from the
  current commit" or "Existing branch", and the folder, showing the hub's default until edited
  (sent only when edited). Worktrees are listed right under their origin, indented, with their
  branch; while the worker adds one the row says "Adding worktree…", then the workspace or
  "Worktree failed" with the reason. The deletion dialog of a worktree lists the worktree's own
  branch with its commits on no remote and says they stay (the branch stays in the origin, only
  the folder goes with `git worktree remove`; a clone's dialog says its unpushed commits go with
  the folder; each warning says what "Delete folder" does with what it lists, since 0.64), and
  deletes with `force=true` only when it listed uncommitted files.
  Since 0.61 (T47): an `ephemeral` worktree has the tag "spawned" on its row; a marked one also
  "for deletion", the line "Its sessions are archived. hqc keeps the worktree and its branch
  until you delete it." and "Delete" instead of "Remove", which opens the same dialog (it adds
  that hqc made the worktree for a session an agent started)
- hqc's allow rules of a workspace (since 0.52, T48; §3 Workspace), the workspace owner only
  (another user's: `404`): `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/rules` → `{rules[{id, rule, created_at}]}`,
  newest first (`api.workspace.rules.json`); `POST /api/workspaces/{id}/rules` {rules[]}
  (`api.workspace.rules.request.json`) → the same list: rules the folder has are kept as they are,
  an empty list is `400`, a rule that is not valid hqc syntax `422 invalid_rule` (nothing saved),
  more than 200 per folder `422 too_many_rules`; `DELETE /api/workspaces/{id}/rules/{rule_id}` →
  `204` (unknown: `404`). After a change the hub sends the worker `workspace.rules` (§5.3).
  `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/permissions?command=|tool=` → the worker's `permissions.inspect`
  result without `request_id` (`api.workspace.permissions.json`); worker offline `409
  worker_offline`, no answer `504 worker_timeout`, refused by the worker `400 invalid_path`, the
  check over 16 KiB `400`.
  The client: the rules screen `#/p/<project>/rules/<workspace>` (`?session=<id>` when opened
  from a session), from "Rules · N hqc" on the workspace's row in the project settings and
  "Folder rules" in the chat's "More" menu; it shows the worker, the path, the workspace's
  environment (since 0.56), the worker's default mode and the session's; "Check a command" (a
  command, or a tool name such as `Edit`; a multi-line field since 0.62, so a pasted script keeps
  the line breaks that separate its commands; the worker's verdict with the rule and its source, "Will
  ask" with "Allow…" and the suggested rule); then denied, allowed (hqc's rules first, with the
  date and a remove cross confirmed in the row; the files' rules read-only) and everything else
  (Ask, Auto or Allow all, the files' `ask` rules), each rule with its source. "Allow in this folder" adds a
  rule with a live format check (an error blocks saving), a duplicate is an error, and a deny that
  would win (checked on the worker) is a warning. Worker offline: hqc's rules only, editable, the
  check disabled. The permission card's "Allow in this folder": §10.1
- `GET /api/workers/{id}/dirs?path=` → `{entries[{name, path}]}`: an `fs.list_dirs` frame to
  the worker (§5.3); without `path`: `allowed_roots`; outside them: `400 invalid_path`;
  offline: `409 worker_offline`
- `GET /api/sessions` (since 0.89) → `{sessions: [<session>]}`: every session of every project
  of the user in one list, the objects of `GET /api/projects/{id}/sessions` (archived and
  service sessions included), the newest `updated_at` first. The client fetches its list with
  it and `GET /api/projects` (since 0.114 also `?archived=1`), not one request per project
- `GET/POST /api/projects/{id}/sessions` (list: `{sessions: [<session>]}`; create:
  {title?, workspace_id?, worker_id?, cwd?, model?, auto_approve?, permission_mode?,
  provider_id?} → `201` and
  the session object, `api.session.request.json`), `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` (§17.4).
  `permission_mode` (since 0.42, T38): `ask` | `auto` | `allow_all` (since 0.129; anything else:
  `422`, the body cannot be read); absent — the worker's default. `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` {title?, auto_approve?, permission_mode?, model?, provider_id?}:
  `provider_id` (since 0.144) — absent: unchanged, `null`: the runtime's own endpoint; a provider
  of the session's owner that the session's worker allows (its last `hello.providers`), else
  `400` (not the owner's) or `422 provider_not_allowed`, both on creation too; a change restarts a
  running agent (`session.kill`, then `session.start` with the new description, the transcript
  resumed), a stopped one starts on it; a session on a provider keeps the provider's model,
  `session.model` does not reach its runtime; `permission_mode: auto` for a session with a
  provider (the one it has or the one the same request gives) is `422 auto_needs_anthropic`
  (since 0.246, §5.3), and the client offers no Auto there. The session object's
  `agent.provider` is {id, label}. `GET/POST /api/providers` ({providers: [...]} and `201`), `PATCH/DELETE
  /api/providers/{id}` (§3 Provider; `PATCH` replaces every field; `409 provider_exists` for a
  name the owner has, `409 provider_in_use` on deleting one sessions run on): {name, label,
  base_url, model, context_tokens?} (`context_tokens` 1000 to 10 000 000); a provider object has
  `workers[]`, the owner's workers whose last `hello` allowed it.
  `POST /api/providers/probe {base_url, name?}` (since 0.236) → `{models[{id, context_tokens?}],
  error?, worker_id?}`: what the endpoint lists, as one of the owner's online workers reads it
  (`provider.probe`, §5.3), a worker that allows `name` first, then the others until one answers
  with models; `409 worker_offline` when none is online. The client's provider form starts with
  the base URL and fills from it the model (a list it can type over), the context window, the
  name and the label, each only while the owner has not edited it.
  Remote MCP servers (since 0.235, `docs/ITERATION-7.md`): `GET/POST /api/mcp/servers`
  ({servers: [...]} and `201`), `PATCH/DELETE /api/mcp/servers/{id}`, `POST
  /api/mcp/servers/{id}/test`, the owner's only. A server: {id, name, url, header_names[],
  timeout_s, all_projects, project_ids[], status (`ok` | `failing` | `unknown`), last_error?,
  tools[] (names, as last listed), instructions?}. `POST` takes {name, url, headers?[{name,
  value}], timeout_s?, all_projects?, project_ids?}; `PATCH` the fields given, `headers` replacing
  all of them. `name` as in `session.start.mcp_servers`, unique per owner (`409 name_taken`); `url`
  https (http only to a loopback host), without a user or password; at most 8 headers, a name of
  letters, digits, `-` and `_` and none the hub sets itself (`Host`, `Content-Type`, `Accept`,
  `Mcp-Session-Id`, `Mcp-Protocol-Version` …), a value of one line up to 4 KiB; `timeout_s` 30 to
  1800, 300 by default; `project_ids` the owner's; at most 50 servers (`409
  too_many_servers`). Header values are write-only: sealed with `HQC_MCP_KEY` (XChaCha20-Poly1305,
  the server's id as associated data), never sent back, logged or put into an event; without the
  key a server with headers is `422 mcp_key_missing`. `test` runs `initialize` and `tools/list` in
  an MCP session of its own, closed after, and returns the server with its status. A changed URL
  or headers drop the cache and the open MCP sessions. The hub speaks Streamable HTTP (`POST` with
  a JSON or an event-stream answer, `Mcp-Session-Id`, `Mcp-Protocol-Version`), one MCP session per
  hqc session and server, opened on the first request, opened again once when the server answers
  `404` for it, and closed (`DELETE`) when the agent's process stops or after an hour unused;
  redirects are not followed, and the address connected to is the one checked against private
  ranges (§20).
  `POST /api/mcp/probe {url}` (since 0.236) → `{name?, server_name?, auth, error?}`: the hub sends
  the server an `initialize` without credentials; `auth` is `none` (it answered; `server_name` is
  its `serverInfo.name`, and the session it opened is closed), `oauth` (`401` and it names an
  authorization server), `token` (`401` without one) or `unknown`; `name` is a valid server name
  from `serverInfo.name` (`github-mcp-server` → `github`) or the host (`mcp.linear.app` →
  `linear`). The client's form starts with the URL and fills the name and the way to sign in
  from it while the owner has not edited them; every field stays editable.
  OAuth (T65): a server with `auth: oauth` ({auth, oauth_client_id?, oauth_client_secret?,
  oauth_scope?} in `POST`/`PATCH`; the secret write-only; status `sign_in` until signed in, and
  `signed_in` in the server object) signs in through its authorization server, as MCP's
  authorization spec has it. `POST /api/mcp/servers/{id}/sign_in` → {url}: the hub discovers the
  server's protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728, named by its `401` or at the well-known path)
  and the authorization server's metadata (RFC 8414 or OpenID), registers itself (RFC 7591) when
  no client id is given and the server offers it (`422 client_id_needed` otherwise), and answers
  the authorization URL with PKCE (S256), a state bound to the owner for ten minutes, the
  `resource` (RFC 8707) and the scope given or the server's. The browser comes back to `GET
  /api/mcp/oauth/callback`, behind the hub's sign-in like `/api/*`, which exchanges the code and
  answers a plain page; the redirect URI is the first of `HQC_PUBLIC_ORIGINS`, else the request's
  host. Tokens and the client secret are sealed under `HQC_MCP_KEY`; the access token is refreshed
  a minute before it expires and once when the server refuses it (one refresh per server at a
  time, a rotated refresh token kept); a failed refresh sets `sign_in`, and the call's error says
  to sign in again. `DELETE /api/mcp/servers/{id}/sign_in` forgets the tokens. The client shows
  the section "MCP servers" in Settings (the list with status and tools, add and edit with
  headers or OAuth, Test, Sign in, Sign out, Delete) and the servers a project gets in its
  settings (T66).
  Since 0.262 (iteration 9) `GET /api/mcp/servers` also has `local[{name, worker_id,
  worker_name, environment}]`: the servers each of the owner's workers (not revoked) declares in
  `worker.toml` (§14 `mcp_servers`), from the environments of its last `hello`, sorted by name,
  worker and environment. They are read-only: the hub cannot add, change or start one, and
  routes nothing by them (a session runs where its workspace is). Settings → MCP servers lists
  them under "On machines" with a line on declaring one in `worker.toml`, and a project's
  settings show those of the workers its workspaces are on.
  Skills (since 0.245, `docs/ITERATION-8.md`): `GET /api/skills` ({skills: [...]}), `POST
  /api/skills`, `PATCH/DELETE /api/skills/{id}`, `GET /api/skills/{id}/files` ({files: [{path,
  size, executable?}]}), the owner's only. A skill: {id, name, description?, allowed_tools[],
  sha256, size (unpacked bytes), files, all_projects, project_ids[], updated_at}. `POST` is
  multipart: one `zip` part, or `file` parts whose file names are the paths inside the skill, and
  an optional `name`; `SKILL.md` at the top or under one top folder; `__MACOSX/`, `.git/` and
  `.DS_Store` dropped. The name is the frontmatter's `name`, else the top folder's, else `name`;
  a name the owner has already replaces that skill's content and keeps its projects (`200`), a
  new one is `201` for all projects. Limits: an upload of 8 MiB, 4 MiB and 500 files unpacked, a
  path of 200 bytes, 100 skills (`409 too_many_skills`); over the size `413`. A `SKILL.md` with
  `hooks` is `422 skill_hooks`; a path out of the skill, a link, a bad name or a frontmatter the
  hub cannot read for sure (§20) `400`. The hub keeps an archive it writes itself (paths sorted,
  fixed times, mode `0755` for an executable entry of a `.zip`, else `0644`), whose sha256 is the
  skill's hash: the same files give the same hash. `PATCH` takes {all_projects?, project_ids?}.
  The client shows the section "Skills" in Settings (upload a folder or a `.zip`, the list with
  each skill's description, size, files and `allowed-tools`, the projects, delete) and the skills
  a project gets in its settings.
  `POST /api/sessions/{id}/secrets` (since 0.147, §14) {kind, name, value?, vault?, vault_field?,
  passphrase?, remember?, request_id?} (unknown fields: `422`; one of `value` and `vault` exactly,
  else `400`; `vault` since 0.216 — a Vaultwarden entry the worker reads itself, §5.3, only on a
  worker whose `capabilities` have `vault`, else `409 unavailable`; `vault_field` since 0.243 — the field of
  that entry, only with `vault`, else `400`, and only on a worker that also has `vault_fields`,
  else `409 unavailable`): a secret (`kind: secret`) or an ssh private
  key (`kind: ssh_key`, with `passphrase` and `remember` for it only) for the session's running
  agent, from its owner, on a worker of theirs with `session_secrets` (else `409 unavailable`),
  not the service session, not archived. The hub passes it in `secret.put` (§5.3) and keeps it
  nowhere: in no event, row, log line or error. `200` is the worker's `{note, path?,
  fingerprint?, remembered?}`; the client puts `note` into the message being written, so the
  agent learns where the secret is with the user's next message. `409 worker_offline`, `422
  secret_refused` with the worker's reason (no running agent, a bad key, a wrong passphrase, a
  kept name the workspace has), `504 worker_timeout`. The feed gets `system secret_given` with the
  name and, for a key, its fingerprint ("Secret WIFI_PASS given", "ssh key pi-lab (SHA256:…)
  given, remembered for this workspace"), and the entry when the worker read it from
  Vaultwarden ("Secret WIFI_PASS given from Vaultwarden entry home-wifi", with a field "…, field
  username"; an `rbw` that stays locked is `422 secret_refused` too). `request_id` answers the session's open `hqc_secret`
  (§7): its `name` and `kind` must be the request's (`400`), a closed one is `409
  request_closed`; the request closes with the call's result and the feed gets `approval.response
  {option_id: give}`; a refused give leaves it open. "Decline" is the request's answer with
  `option_id: deny` (`POST /api/sessions/{id}/requests/{request_id}`); no other option is taken.
  `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/keys` ({keys: [{name, fingerprint}]}) and `DELETE
  /api/workspaces/{id}/keys/{name}` (`204`, `404` for a key the workspace has not): the keys the
  workspace's worker keeps for it (`workspace.keys`, `workspace.key_delete`, §5.3); the worker
  must be online (`409 worker_offline`). `GET /api/workers` has `session_secrets` in the worker
  object.
  The worker's own Claude Code (since 0.185, only the worker's owner, the worker online with
  `capabilities.claude_code.login`, else `409 worker_offline` or `422 unsupported`): `GET
  /api/workers/{id}/claude` (`claude.auth`, §5.3); `POST /api/workers/{id}/claude/login` →
  `{login_id, url}` (`409 login_running`; a page off claude.com and claude.ai is `422
  login_failed` and the hub cancels the sign-in); `POST /api/workers/{id}/claude/login/{login_id}
  {code}` → `{ok, message?, status}` (`404` for an unknown sign-in, waits up to 80 s); `DELETE
  /api/workers/{id}/claude/login/{login_id}` → `204`. The code passes through in memory only.
  Client: Settings → Workers shows under each such worker "Claude: <email> · <plan>" or "not
  signed in" and "Sign in": "Open the sign-in page" (only an Anthropic https page), a field for
  the code (cleared on send, kept in no draft or storage), "Send", "Cancel".
  `PATCH /api/sessions/{id} {browser}` (since 0.148, §14): `true` gives the session's agent the
  owner's Chrome on the worker's machine, only by the worker's owner for a session of theirs on
  a worker whose last `hello` had `browser` (else `422 browser_not_allowed`, another user `403`,
  the service session `409 system_session`); `false` takes it away. A change restarts a running
  agent as a change of provider does (`session.kill`, then `session.start` with `browser`, the
  transcript resumed); a stopped one starts with it. The session object's `agent.browser` is
  `true` while it is on; `GET /api/workers` has `browser` in the worker object.
  `model` (since 0.74) — absent: unchanged, `null`: the runtime's default; it is checked as on
  creation before anything is written, the service session answers `409 system_session`, and
  the hub sends the worker `session.model` (§5.3). It is not in `session.summary`: another
  device sees the change when it fetches the session object. A message typed as
  `/model <name>` (since 0.77; `POST /input`, the text being that command alone) does the same
  once stored: `default` stores `null`, a name outside the field limits (§20) is not stored and
  goes to the runtime only; the client fetches the session object after sending one, and (since
  0.179) after a `system model_not_switched` comes in an open chat (§4). The chat
  header names the model the last turn used, or the stored one when the session was switched to
  another model since (an alias `opus` matches `claude-opus-…`). `permission_mode` in `PATCH`:
  `permission_mode` switches the session's mode and sends the worker `session.permission_mode`
  (§5.3); `auto` and `allow_all` only by the worker owner (`403`, as for `auto_approve`), `ask`
  by whoever may manage the session; the service session: `409 system_session`. The reply carries the stored
  `permission_mode` and the `effective_permission_mode` the worker reported so far; its
  confirmation comes as `session.summary`. Since 0.172 `model`, `permission_mode` or `browser`
  in `PATCH` of a room answers `409 room`: a room has no agent, its agents' sessions have them
  (§7.1.1)
- `POST /api/projects/{id}/rooms` (since 0.172, §7.1.1) {title?, mode, workspace_id?, cwd?,
  permission_mode?, agents: [{name?, model?, provider_id?, system_prompt?}]} → `201` and the room's
  session object (`api.room.request.json`, `api.session.room.json`). `mode` is `conversation` |
  `council` (anything else: `422`); `agents` has at least one (`400` otherwise), and an agent's
  `system_prompt` is at most 32 KiB (`400` otherwise: the worker passes it to the CLI as one
  argument, and Linux refuses an argument over 128 KiB), a NUL in it replaced as in a title.
  Checked as `POST .../sessions` checks a session before anything is stored: the owner's
  project, each model, each provider (the owner's, else `400`; one the workspace's worker
  allows, else `422 provider_not_allowed`), the title and each agent's `name` (as a title), the workspace (`workspace_id`, else the project's default;
  ready, on a worker of the owner) and `cwd`. The room is a session with no workspace and no
  worker, `agent.runtime: none`, `room_mode`, titled `title` or "Room N" (N and the slug `room-N`
  as for "Session N", §3 Session), with `system session_created`. Then each agent gets a session
  of its own as `POST .../sessions` makes one, in that workspace and `cwd`, in
  `permission_mode`, with its `model` (absent or empty: the runtime's default), `provider_id`
  and `system_prompt`, `spawned_by` and `room_id` the room (`api.session.room.member.json`),
  titled by its `name` (trimmed, a NUL replaced as in a title; empty is none), else by its model
  as given, by the provider's `label` on a provider, "default" without either, a repeated one
  numbered among the agents without a name ("opus", "opus 2"), `title_source: user`. Its agent
  does not start with it: the first input from the room starts it
- `GET/PUT /api/projects/{id}/session_order` (since 0.53, T50): the order of the project's
  session list for the requesting user, one record per user and project → `{mode, session_ids}`
  (`api.session_order.json`). `mode` is `state` | `recent` | `custom` (the list's switch; it
  lived in the browser's `localStorage` before); `session_ids` are every unarchived session of
  the project except the service sessions, in the user's order: those not placed yet (a new
  session, a restored one) first, newest created first, then the stored order; archived and
  deleted ones are left out. No record: `state` and the sessions newest first. `PUT` {mode?,
  session_ids?} (`api.session_order.request.json`; either or both, a missing one keeps its
  stored value) stores the order as the reply gives it: ids that are not unarchived sessions of
  this project (another project's, another user's, archived, unknown, repeated) are ignored, the
  project's sessions missing from the list go first; an unknown `mode` is `422`. Another user's
  or a nonexistent project: `404`
- `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events?after_seq=&limit=` — pagination by `seq`, response
  `{events[], last_seq}`. Since 0.54 (T51) a final `agent.message` that answered an
  `hqc_ask` has `reply_delivered_at` when the asking worker acknowledged the reply (§7.1);
  the field is not stored, the hub adds it here and on `/api/ws`
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/input` {text, artifact_ids[], client_op_id} → `201 {event}`:
  the stored `user.message` with `client_op_id` and `delivery: pending`; a repeat with the same
  `client_op_id` (deduplicated by `(session_id, client_op_id)`) → `200 {event}` with the event
  stored the first time. Since 0.172 a room's `user.message` has no `delivery`: its agents get
  the message in their input queues, each of a `council`, one of a `conversation` (§7.1.1)
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/stop`, `/restart`, `/steer`, `/takeover`, `/archive`, `/unarchive`,
  `/retry` (§5.2). `/takeover` (§9.3) continues in hqc a session that VS Code was driving: `locked_by:
  hqc`, `system session_taken_over`, `session.start` with `mode: resume` to the worker; the
  response is the session object; with `locked_by: hqc` it does nothing. A live foreign process
  holds the transcript: `409 vscode_open` with `held_by`; no registry data and VS Code wrote
  less than 30 s ago: `409 vscode_active`; worker offline: `409 worker_offline`; archived:
  `409 archived`; service session: `409 system_session`. Since 0.172 `/stop` of a room stops its
  agents (§7.1.1): `system room_stopped` "Stopped" in the room first, then each agent that is
  not archived stopped as its own `/stop` does (its own requests cancelled with `stopped`, the
  runtime's left to a connected worker, §10.1, and `session.stop` to its worker);
  the agents' inputs are not failed (since 0.231 the worker of an agent whose turn runs at the
  Stop writes what waited into its history without a turn, §8.1, §17.2),
  and a turn on a message from before "Stopped" posts nothing unless a later one joined it
  (§7.1.1); `{sent}` is `true` when one went out. Since 0.130 `/restart` ends the agent's
  process and starts it again at once (`session.kill`, then `session.start` with `mode: resume`,
  §17.3) and answers `{sent}`, `false` with nothing sent while the worker is offline; archived:
  `409 archived`, driven from VS Code: `409 locked_vscode`, service session: `409 system_session`
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/pause`, `/resume` → the session object (since 0.160, `write` level,
  §17.3). `/pause` sets `paused_at` and, with no turn running, ends the agent's process at once
  (`session.kill`); with one running (since 0.191), it stops that turn as `/stop` does and ends the
  process when the turn has ended. `/resume` clears it and stores the note of the pause as a
  pending `user.message` (since 0.191 also when the process was not stopped yet); when it was, it
  starts the agent (`session.start` with `mode: resume`). A pause of a paused session and a resume
  of one that is not paused change nothing; archived: `409 archived`, driven from VS Code: `409
  locked_vscode`, service session: `409 system_session`; since 0.172 a room: `409 room` (it has no
  agent; its agents' sessions are paused one by one, §7.1.1)
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/background` {call_id} → `{sent}` (since 0.125; `write` level, as
  `/stop`): `session.background` to the worker (§5.3), `sent: false` when the worker is not
  connected; nothing comes back of what the runtime did, the call leaves the session's
  `foreground_calls` when the worker reports it moved. The `call_id` is not checked against
  `foreground_calls`: Claude Code moves a foreground call of the session by its id, a
  subagent's too, and the session is the user's own. A `call_id` that is empty, longer than
  128 bytes or has U+0000: `400 bad_request`; service session: `409 system_session`
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/inputs/{event_id}/withdraw` → `{withdrawn: true}` (since 0.219;
  `write` level, as `/input`): the owner takes back a message of theirs that waits for the agent
  (§17.2). The message becomes `delivery: withdrawn`, which the hub tells the open clients with a
  `delivery` frame and removes from `inflight`; the pages of the feed and the subscription backlog
  go on returning it as withdrawn (§3), `hqc_read`, a fork's copy and the search never do. What
  the hub does depends on whether a worker may hold the message. One the hub never handed to a
  worker (no `handed_at`, §3: the worker was away since it was typed, the session is paused or not
  started) is withdrawn on the hub alone. One that was handed is asked about at the worker with
  `session.withdraw` (§5.3) on the worker's connection, whatever the session's start state there
  (a `session.kill` clears the hub's `inflight` and the worker's queue, so the connection of a
  paused session holds nothing, and the worker says so): `withdrawn: true` withdraws it, `false`
  is `409 already_taken` and the message stays as it is. With no worker connection a handed
  message is not withdrawn (the worker may keep the input and give it to the agent): `409
  worker_offline`, "the worker holds this message; try again when it is connected", the message
  stays pending. While the request is outstanding the connection's state keeps the message in
  `withdrawing`, so the hub hands it to nobody and a second take-back of it is `409 withdrawing`,
  "this message is being taken back already"; the set is cleared when the request ends in any
  way (the answer, an error, the connection closed). The worker's answer is waited for 10 s, and
  settled also when the owner's request is gone meanwhile. One that is withdrawn already is `409
  withdrawn`, "this message was taken back already", and the client that asked puts its text and
  files back into the input, as on `withdrawn: true`. One the agent took already (`delivery: delivered`, or no longer pending) is `409
  already_taken`. The hub sends no input that is withdrawn (it marks
  `handed_at` and checks `delivery = pending` in one statement before each `session.input`). An
  event that is not a `user.message` of this session with `payload.human` (§4: an unknown id,
  another session's, a resume note, a hub's note, a run of a schedule): `404`; archived: `409
  archived`, driven from VS Code: `409 locked_vscode`, service session: `409 system_session`, a
  room: `409 room`; no answer from the worker `504 worker_timeout`, a worker that answers `error`
  (e.g. a runtime that does not answer the cancel): `502` with the worker's own `error` code and
  message, not `400 invalid_path`. Two limitations. A worker that answers after the 10 s: the
  owner has `504` and the hub drops the answer; when the worker had dropped the message, it stays
  queued and handed to nobody until the owner takes it back again (the worker holds nothing then
  and says so: the message is withdrawn and its text comes back), or until the worker connects
  again or the agent's process restarts, which hands it again and it runs. The owner's request is
  gone (the connection broke) or its `200` is lost: the hub withdraws the message all the same and
  the chat hides it, but its text does not come back into the input, unless the owner takes it
  back again before the client learns of it (`409 withdrawn`)
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/inputs/{event_id}/now` → `{sent_now}` (since 0.219; `write` level):
  the owner sends such a message into the running turn at once (§17.2): `session.input_now` to
  the worker connection that holds the message in `inflight` (§5.3), whose `sent_now` comes back as
  it is. `409 not_now` when the worker answers `not_now` (no turn runs, the turn waits for an
  answer to a card of the agent's, a move waits, the turn answers an `hqc_ask`), or when no started
  connection holds the message (the worker is offline, the session paused or not started, the
  message handed in an earlier connection); a worker's other `error` is `502` as for `/withdraw`,
  and the other refusals are those of `/withdraw`
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/side_question` {text} → `201 {event}` (since 0.232; `write` level;
  `api.side_question.request.json`, `api.side_question.json`): stores `side.question` (§4) and
  sends the worker `session.side_question` (§5.3) with the session's `history` of side
  questions, after sending `session.start` (with `no_wait`) when the session's agent is not
  started on this connection, so that a side question works for an unloaded agent (§17.5). `400` for a text
  that is empty or only blank; `409 room` (a room has no agent of its own), `409 archived`,
  `409 locked_vscode` (as `/input`), `409 paused` (a paused agent is not started), `409
  not_askable` (a runtime other than Claude Code), `409 worker_offline`, `409 system_session`;
  the hub also stores `side.answer {error}` at once when the worker goes away between its check
  and the send. A text with U+0000 is stored and sent with it replaced, as any text. The client sends it for a composer text `/btw
  <question>` or `/side <question>` (§6 client layout).
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/tasks/{task_id}/stop` → `{sent}` (since 0.161; `write` level, as
  `/stop`): `session.stop_task` to the worker (§5.3), `sent: false` when the worker is not
  connected; nothing comes back of what the runtime did, the task's row leaves
  `subagents.live` when the worker reports it ended. The `task_id` is not checked against
  `subagents.live`: Claude Code stops a task of the session by its id, and the session is the
  user's own. A `task_id` longer than 128 bytes or with U+0000: `400 bad_request`; service
  session: `409 system_session`
- `GET /api/sessions/{id}/subagents/{task_id}/history[?after=<event_id>]` → `{events[],
  truncated, continues?}` (since 0.181; `read` level, as `GET .../events`;
  `api.subagent_history.json`): the worker's `session.subagent_history` result without
  `request_id` (§5.3), `after` passed on to it, asked for each time and stored nowhere. A
  `task_id` that is not 1 to 64 bytes of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`: `400 bad_request`, an `after` that is
  not a UUID: `400`, the worker not asked; worker offline `409 worker_offline`, no answer
  `504 worker_timeout`, refused by the worker `400 invalid_path`
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork` {event_id} → `201` and the new session object (since 0.80;
  `manage` level): a new session in the same project, workspace, worker and `cwd`, with the
  source's model, `permission_mode` and `auto_approve`, titled "<title> (fork)", whose
  conversation is the source's before the user's message `event_id` (a `user.message` of a
  person in this session, else `404`); a session that is not Claude Code or has no workspace on
  a worker of its owner: `409 not_forkable`. The cut is the source's last `agent.message` events
  before the message (up to 20, newest first): they go as `session.start.fork` (§5.3) with the
  source's `runtime_session_id`; with none (the first message) the session starts with no
  conversation and no fork. Its feed gets the source's `user.message`, `agent.message`,
  `agent.thinking`, `tool.call`, `tool.result`, `attachment`, `peer.message` and `system` events
  before the message under new ids, at `seq` 1.., none of them an input to deliver (since 0.179
  without the events a `retraction` names), then `system forked_from`, all read by the owner;
  requests, statuses and usage stay with the source. Since
  0.156 the copies go in without their search words, which the hub writes as soon as the copy is in,
  without the answer waiting for them (§15). Since 0.82 a copy keeps its origin (`events.origin_id`,
  `origin_runtime`, not on the wire): the id the runtime's record gave the event and the transcript
  that record was first written in. The
  cut's events are each named by their origin, and the fork goes to the transcript of the newest
  one with only the events in it: a fork of a fork before a message of its copied history cuts
  in the transcript that history came from, which stays on the worker when the sessions between
  never ran (the CLI writes a fork's transcript at its first message) or were deleted (§17.4).
  Since 0.162 the events a session has when its runtime goes on in another transcript (`/clear`,
  §8.1) get the one they were written in as `origin_runtime`: a fork before a message of the
  conversation before `/clear` cuts that transcript, one after the first answer after it the new
  one (before, every fork cut the new one, and the worker did not find the cut there); the cut
  is only among the answers after the last `system conversation_cleared` (its own or copied)
  before the message, or before the place the client shows it at (below), so a fork before the
  first answer after `/clear` starts a new conversation, like one before the first message,
  without the source's events. Since 0.108 a fork before a message with `during_text` keeps the
  `agent.message` the client shows above it (below, the WebSocket paragraph) as the newest cut
  and the last copied event; an `agent.thinking` the client shows above it (since 0.208) is not
  kept. Since 0.221 a fork before a message with `joined_after` cuts at the last `agent.message` after
  the message and not past `joined_after`, or at the place of the turns it waited through (below)
  when that is later, and keeps the events up to it but the inputs; with neither it cuts before
  the message as for any other, and such a message has no `during_text` place. The calls and the
  thinking after that `agent.message`, which the feed shows above the message, are not kept, as a
  thinking above is not. A fork's copy of a message keeps `joined_after` in the copy's own `seq`:
  the last copied event that is no input and stood at or before it, none when that is not past
  the message (a fork leaves out `usage`, `status` and requests, so its `seq` are not the
  source's). Since 0.239 a `joined_after` that is not a non-negative JSON integer of at most 18
  digits (every `seq` is one; a worker's event is stored as sent) counts as none: the fork does
  not fail on it, and the copy has none.
  Since 0.161 a fork before a message the client shows after the
  turns it waited through (the same paragraph; one with `during_text` too) cuts after them: the
  newest cut is the last `agent.message` before the place the client shows the message at, and
  the feed also gets the events after the message and before that place but its inputs. The
  agent starts at once. The client puts the message's text into the new session's input as its
  draft and opens it. Since 0.134 the agent of a fork with copied history is told it is a copy:
  the first input after `system forked_from` goes with `session.input.text` beginning `[hqc
  fork] <the forked_from text>. The conversation above was copied from that session; this
  session is <its address>, separate from it from here on.` and an empty line, the address the
  session has at delivery; a slash command does not carry it (the next input does) and a failed
  input does not count; in a `peer.message` the note stands after the worker's sender header
  (§7.1). An input sent again before its `ack` carries it again. The feed keeps the text as
  typed. A fork before the first message has no copied history and no note.
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/move` {path, project?, create?} → the session object (since 0.75;
  `manage` level, §3 Grant): the session continues in folder `path` of its worker, in that
  folder's project (§3 Session). The hub checks the folder with `fs.stat` as `POST
  /api/workspaces` does, with the same codes (`create`: the worker makes a missing folder; the
  overlap and `ready` checks below run on the requested path before that, so a `409` leaves no folder,
  unless the path reaches a workspace through a symlink, which only the canonical path shows; `400
  path_not_found`, `outside_allowed_roots`, `not_a_directory`, `invalid_path`, `409
  worker_offline`, `504 worker_timeout`), and takes the canonical path. A workspace of the
  session's owner on that worker at exactly that path is taken with its project (`project`, when
  given, must be that one: `400` otherwise), unless it is not `ready` (§3 Workspace): `409
  workspace_not_ready`, as for a new session; one that lies inside the path or contains it, or
  another owner's, is `409 workspace_conflict` with the body of `POST /api/workspaces`.
  Otherwise the folder becomes a new `dir` workspace, mirrored (§9.2), of `project` (an id or
  slug of the owner's projects, `404` otherwise) or of a new project named after the folder's
  last component; a project's first workspace becomes its default. Then the session gets that
  project and workspace, `cwd: .` and its slug (§3 Session), the old project's saved order drops
  it (the same project's keeps it), the feed gets `system session_moved` (§4), the workspace's
  `mirror.set` goes out, and a running agent gets `session.start` with the new folder, which the
  worker applies between turns (§5.3). No input is queued (`hqc_move` queues one, §7): a stopped agent starts there with its
  next input. A session already in that workspace is answered as it is, nothing written and no
  second `session_moved`; the workspace's `mirror.set` and the `session.start` of a running agent
  go out again, as the first call may have ended between the move and them (the client went
  away, a database error). `409 archived`: an
  archived session, as for `/takeover`. `409 unavailable`: not a Claude Code session, the
  service session, no workspace, driven from VS Code (`locked_by: vscode`), held open by a live
  process outside hqc (`held_by`, §9.3), a session whose subagents still run (`subagents`, §5.4;
  a foreground one too, as the hub sees only the count: a background one would keep the agent in
  its old folder), a worker that is not the session owner's (as for `POST /api/workspaces`), or
  a worker that does not report
  `capabilities.claude_code.moves` (§5.4). These refusals are checked before `fs.stat` and again
  after it, on the session read anew: it may change meanwhile. The client offers it as "Move to
  project…" in the chat's "More" menu: the project (one of the user's, or a new one named after the folder), one
  of that project's folders on the session's worker, the folder tree or a typed path, and
  "Create the folder and move" after `path_not_found`, as when a workspace is added; after the
  move the session leaves the old project's list and opens in the new one, which joins the rail.
  A `session.summary` with another `project_id` (a move made elsewhere) does the same. A desktop
  row of the session list dragged onto another project on the bar moves the session there
  without the form when that project has exactly one `ready` folder on the session's worker;
  otherwise the form opens over the list with that project chosen.
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/requests/{request_id}` {option_id, message? | answers?, action?} →
  `{event_id, seq}`
  of the stored answer; closed request: `409 request_closed` (§10.1). The same call answers a
  request wherever the client shows it (its own feed, the feed of a session waiting on it, the
  "Requests" list, §10.1): `{id}` is always the request's own session. `message` is a text reply
  instead of the call (§10.1): only for an `approval` in a session and only with an option of
  `canonical: deny`/`deny_always`, non-empty, up to 16 KiB, otherwise `400`. A `clarify` takes
  non-empty `answers`; since 0.180 one with `server` (an MCP server's, §4) also takes `action`:
  `accept` with `answers` or without (a link's Done), `decline` without answers; `action` on
  another clarify, an unknown one, or `decline` with answers: `400`; only the worker owner
  answers one with `server`, anyone else gets `403` (§10.1, §11)
- `POST /api/artifacts` (multipart: field `file`, optional `kind`) → `201` and the artifact
  object `{id, kind, name, mime, size, sha256, created_at, public_url?}` (`api.artifact.json`);
  the same file under the same name again → `200` and the earlier object, with the `kind` given
  (since 0.128); over 100 MB: `413 too_large`; unknown `kind`, `kind: site` (since 0.209: only
  the worker's `hqc_publish` uploads one) or no `file`: `400`; a body the multipart parser
  refuses: `400` with the parser's reason, `multipart: …` (since 0.109). Without the field,
  `kind` is derived from the type and extension (§12). `GET /api/artifacts/{id}` → the artifact
  object, a published `site` with `public_url`, its link (since 0.209, `api.artifact.site.json`;
  absent while it is not published, and on a hub without `HQC_PUBLISH_BASE`); `DELETE
  /api/artifacts/{id}/publication` (since 0.209) → `204`: the owner unpublishes it,
  `published_at` and `public_id` are cleared and the link is `404` from then on; an artifact not
  published: `204`, nothing changes; `GET /api/artifacts/{id}/url` → `{url, expires_at}`
  (`api.artifact.url.json`), a signed link valid for 10 minutes (§12). Someone else's or a
  nonexistent artifact: `404`. An input (`POST .../input`) with `artifact_ids` of someone
  else's or nonexistent artifacts: `400 unknown_artifact`; more than 32: `400`. Download by link: `GET /artifacts/{id}?exp=&sig=`
  (outside `/api`, §12); for the worker: `GET /worker/artifacts/{id}` (§5.3)
- `GET /api/requests` → `{requests[]}` (`api.requests.json`, since 0.41, T37): every open
  request (`approval`, `clarify`, `worker_approval`, since 0.76 `move`, since 0.95 `follow`,
  since 0.209 `publish`) in the user's sessions that are not
  archived, oldest first, the workers' service sessions included. An item is `{session_id,
  request_id, kind, address, title, worker_id?, worker_name?, system?, event, waiting[]}`:
  `address` (`<project-slug>/<session-slug>`), `title` and the worker of the request's session,
  `system: true` for a worker's own request (§10.2), `event` — the `approval.request` /
  `clarify.request` as stored (§4), `waiting` — `{session_id, address, title}` of the user's
  sessions that wait on this one through open `hqc_ask`s (§7.1), directly or along a chain,
  the nearest first, so the last is the top of the chain (absent when nobody waits). Only the
  user's own sessions and asks count: another user's request, or another user's ask aimed at
  the user's session, is never listed. The same list comes over `/api/ws` as `requests` (below)
- `PUT /api/sessions/{id}/read_cursor` {last_read_seq}
- `PUT/DELETE /api/sessions/{id}/favorite`, `PUT/DELETE /api/projects/{id}/favorite` (since
  0.74, §3 Favorite): for whoever may read the session or the project, as `read_cursor`;
  `PUT` → `200 {favorite_at}` (again: the same time), `DELETE` → `204` (also when there was
  none). A session's change reaches the user's clients as `session.summary`; a project's has no
  frame, another device sees it at the next `GET /api/projects`. The client shows the open
  project's starred sessions as a Favorites group above its session groups, in the list's one
  scroll (since 0.211; before, a block pinned over the list with a scroll of its own), newest first,
  without the project's name in the row (since 0.114; before, the starred sessions of every
  project began every project's list); a starred session is listed there only, not again in its
  group (Reorder still lists every session), so a project whose sessions are all starred shows
  the block, not "No sessions yet". The starred projects come first on the project bar in each
  of its orders (§3 User `project_sort`), with a star on the tile's corner.
- `GET /api/workers` → `{workers[]}`: workers that are not revoked; `?include_revoked=1` adds
  the revoked ones (the "Settings" screen). The worker object is `{id, name, os, status: online
  | offline | revoked, revoked_at?, last_seen?, system_session_id, limits, ...}` (§3 Worker);
  `limits` (since 0.81) — `{five_hour?, seven_day?, status?, rate_limit_type?, resets_at?,
  reported_at}` of the latest `worker.limits` (§5.4; the three since 0.179), `null` while there
  is none. The menu of the chat header's model pill shows them for the session's worker under its
  items: a bar, the share used and when it resets. Since 0.179 the chat also reads them when it opens and
  whenever the session's state changes, and shows a bar above the input, worded as the VS Code
  tab words it; unlike the tab, which shows the share only once the status is `allowed_warning`,
  at 70 % of either window (since 0.190 `limit_notice_percent` of `/api/me`, the hub's
  `HQC_LIMIT_NOTICE_PERCENT`; at `0` the chat shows no bar at all, a hit limit included): "You've
  hit your 5-hour limit · resets 18:00" while `status` is `rejected` (the limit named by
  `rate_limit_type`, "usage limit" for one it does not know), else "You've used 82% of your
  weekly limit · resets Wed 18:00" for the fuller window at that share or more; nothing below, and
  nothing for a limit or a window whose reset time has passed (the hub
  keeps the last report, and a new one comes with the next turn), nor in a session on a provider
  (its model does not run on the subscription the limits are of).
  `GET /api/workers/enroll/{code}` → `{name, os, created_at, country?, replaceable?}`
  (`EnrollInfo`; `country` is `CF-IPCountry` of the `enroll` request, absent with
  `HQC_CLIENT_IP_HEADER`, §5.1; `replaceable`: §5.1, workers
  of the same machine first and with `same_machine: true`), `POST
  /api/workers/enroll/confirm` {code, name?, replace_worker_id?} → `{worker_id, name,
  replaced?}` (the client also opens the screen from the link `#/enroll?code=XXXX-XXXX`;
  replacement and `409 worker_online`: §5.1; examples `api.enroll.*.replace*.json`).
  `DELETE /api/workers/{id}` → `204`: revocation (§5.1), the service session is archived (§10.2);
  already revoked or someone else's: `404`.
  `DELETE /api/workers/{id}?purge=1` → `204`: deletes a **revoked** worker: the worker record,
  its service session (with events, as in §17.4) and its workspace records (folders are left
  alone, §13.2; a project's default workspace is replaced with the earliest remaining one). Not
  revoked: `409 worker_not_revoked`; while the worker has non-archived sessions (other than the
  service one): `409 worker_has_sessions` with body `{error, message, sessions_count}`; the client
  offers to move them by enrollment with replacement (§5.1) or to archive them. Archived sessions
  survive the deletion without `worker_id` and `workspace_id` (unarchiving: `409 no_workspace`).
  `GET /api/workers/{id}/candidates` → `{candidates[{path, sessions_count, last_active}]}`
  (`api.candidates.json`): a `workspace.list_candidates` frame to the worker (§5.3, §9.1); offline:
  `409 worker_offline`; no reply within 10 s: `504 worker_timeout`; a worker without a mirror
  refused: `400 invalid_path`
- `GET /api/search?q=&project=&session=&kind=&since=&order=&per_session=&fuzzy=&cursor=&limit=`
  → `{results[{session_id, address, title, archived, seq?, type?, ts, snippet, session_hits}],
  next_cursor?, also?, counts?}` (`api.search.json`, since 0.36, T33; §15): `q` 1–200
  characters after trimming; `project` an id or slug of the user's project (another user's or
  an unknown one: `404`); `fuzzy=1` (or `true`) needs at least 3 characters; `limit` 1–50, 20
  by default; `next_cursor` is opaque, passed back as `cursor` for the next page, absent on the
  last one. A hit without `seq` is a title hit. Since 0.111: `session` — a session id: only its
  hits (another user's or an unknown session has none); `kind` — `message` (`user.message`,
  `agent.message`, `peer.message`, `system`), `command` (`tool.call`), `output`
  (`tool.result`) or `answer` (`clarify.response`): only hits of that kind, so no title hit;
  `since` — an RFC 3339 time: only hits at or after it, a title hit counted at its session's
  creation; `order` — `best` (the default) or `newest`: newest first instead of best match
  first; `per_session` — at most that many hits of each session (held to 1–50), its first ones
  in the order. `session_hits` is the number of hits of the query with the same filters in
  the hit's session, before `per_session`; `also` — at most 8 words of this page's hits that the query
  found besides the words typed (their other forms, the similar words of a fuzzy query),
  lowercased, the word in the most hits first, absent when none; `counts` — on the first page
  only (no `cursor`) of a query without `session`: `{all, message, command, output, answer}`,
  each `{hits, sessions}`, the hits of the whole query in its project and since its `since`,
  whatever its `kind` and `per_session`, and how many sessions they are in; `all` counts title
  hits too. Refused queries (empty, too long, too short for fuzzy, a foreign cursor, a
  `session`, `kind`, `since` or `order` that cannot be read, over the time limit): `400
  bad_request` with the reason in `message`. The client opens a hit at
  `#/s/<session>?seq=<seq>` (a title hit at `#/s/<session>`)
- `GET/POST/DELETE /api/grants`
- `POST /api/push/subscribe` (body is `PushSubscription.toJSON()`: `{endpoint,
  expirationTime?, keys: {p256dh, auth}}`), `DELETE /api/push/subscribe {endpoint}`,
