  `GET /api/push/vapid` → `{public_key}` (base64url of the uncompressed P-256 point; `null` if
  push is not configured; the client then shows "notifications are off on the hub"). The push
  body itself: §16. `endpoint`: only `https://` on push service hosts (§20), otherwise `400`;
  at most 10 subscriptions per user (`409 push_limit`); someone else's `endpoint`: `409
  conflict`, not a takeover; a repeated request for one's own subscription updates it.
- `/api/schedules` (since 0.38, T35; §3 ScheduledMessage, §16): `GET
  /api/schedules?session_id=` → `{schedules[]}` (`api.schedules.json`; without `session_id`:
  all of the user's), the next due first, finished ones last; `POST /api/schedules`
  {session_id, cron? | at?, timezone?, message, catch_up?} → `201` and the schedule
  (`api.schedule.request.json`, `api.schedule.json`; the checks of §16 and §20 give `400`, an
  archived session `409 archived`, over the limit `409 schedule_limit`); `PATCH
  /api/schedules/{id}` {enabled?} → the schedule (pause and resume; a `cron` resumed runs next
  after now); `DELETE /api/schedules/{id}` → `204`. Another user's schedule or session: `404`.
  The schedule object is `{id, owner_id, session_id, cron?, at?, timezone, message, enabled,
  catch_up, next_run?, last_run?, created_at, updated_at}`. The client lists, pauses, resumes
  and deletes a session's schedules in the block above the input (§6), opened by a "Scheduled:"
  line there or by the session's "More" menu ("Schedules")
- later: `/api/projects/{id}/template`

Client layout (since 0.51, T49, `docs/design/redesign-2026-11-01`; since 0.114 the new screen):
a window 1080 px wide or more has the project bar, the session column and the main column; from
900 to 1079 px the bar and the main column, the session column sliding out over the chat
(below); below 900 px the phone layout, one screen at a time (below). The look (§3 User `look`,
"Settings" → "Look": Compact or Spacious, applied once the hub has stored it) sets how dense all
of it is, as classes on the document root: Spacious — the feed and the input at most 780 px
wide, the user's messages as bubbles on the right, Inter, a 72 px bar with a tile per project,
two lines per session; Compact — the feed, the input and the live subagents across the whole
chat column, in one column as the VS Code tab draws it (a mark in a gutter before each item: a
grey dot for the agent's text, the state of a run of tools, an arrow for a message between
sessions, a shield for a permission request, a question for the agent's questions, a clip for a
file, a chevron for what folds; the user's messages as plates from the feed's left edge, the
service lines across the feed), the platform's UI font (SF on a Mac) instead of Inter, a row
with each project's full name on the bar, a line per session. Since 0.73 the tab's icon keeps
two of the project bar's marks across all projects: an amber dot while a session waits, else a
light one while one has unread events. Since 0.64 a project opened on a desktop opens the
session last open in it on this device (kept in the browser's storage; none, archived or
deleted: the empty main column); a phone's project screen stays its session list. Since 0.78 a
message typed into a session and not sent stays its draft on this device (the browser's storage,
`hqc.drafts`): the input shows it again when the session is opened, and the session's row,
unless it is the one open, says "Draft"; sending the message or clearing the input drops it.
Since 0.89 the projects (since 0.114 the archived ones too), the sessions and the list orders
the hub gave on this page load are kept on this device as well (the browser's storage,
`hqc.list`, with the id of the personal project), written after each fetch of the list and when
the page is hidden or left, dropped when a write fails: on a reload the project bar and the list
(of the project of the open session or project, else the personal one) show them at once, and
the hub's answer replaces them; a kept list order is asked from the hub again once per page
load. The client fetches the list with `GET /api/projects`, `GET /api/projects?archived=1` and
`GET /api/sessions`; the archived projects stay as kept when their request fails. "offline" (the
workers line, a phone's list head, the chat's header) appears only once the socket's first
connect has ended. The theme is the user's `theme` plus the current project's `color`, as CSS
variables on the document root recomputed when either changes; status colors do not depend on
the project (amber waiting, green online, red danger, violet between sessions, since 0.114 blue
for the project bar's unread dot); since 0.88 the light themes have darker variants of them, and
there the project's color is darkened where it is text; since 0.114 the user's message bubble is
the theme's surface in every project, not tinted by the project's color. Since 0.88 the app
theme is picked on the Settings page (`#/settings`, the first section "Theme": a row of dark and
a row of light tiles, a click applies it at once). On a light theme the client switches
`apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style` from `black-translucent` (white status text) to
`default` (dark text) **[verify]**: whether an iPhone's Home Screen app picks the change up at
once, at its next start or only when added again. The Settings page (since 0.114) has a back
arrow to the address it was opened from (on a computer, from `#/`, the current project);
"New session" (since 0.188), after Look, picks from a select of the projects on the bar the
project the phone's floating button and a wrapper's shortcut (`window.hqc.newSessionInProject()`,
below) open a new session in (§3 User `new_session_project_id`), the same on every device; it
shows the project in use, the personal one while none is picked or the picked one has left the
bar, and a pick is stored at once, no "Save"; "Quick messages" (since 0.255), after it, the
user's own quick messages, offered in every project before the project's own (below), edited as
the project's (below): the intro line "Texts sent to the agent with one press from the button
beside the message field, in every project, before the project's own. The same on every
device.", the list, "Add a quick message"; "Web search" (since
0.142) picks where "Search in …" of selected text searches: Google (the default), DuckDuckGo,
Bing or Yandex, kept on this device (`localStorage`), not on the hub; "Keys" (since 0.242)
holds the key of every action below that has one: Quote and Search of selected text, the
project search, the session column, New session, Archive session, the previous and the next
session and project, Back and Forward. Each is recorded anew (a press with ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ held;
Ctrl or Alt off a Mac; Esc cancels), put back to its default or cleared (Delete), and a key given
to one action is taken off any other; kept on this device (`localStorage`), not on the hub;
"Models" (since 0.144)
lists the user's providers (§3 Provider), each with its model, `base_url` and the workers that
allow it, or the `[providers.<name>] base_url = "…"` line a `worker.toml` needs when none does,
with Edit and Delete, and "Add a provider"; the model menus of a session
(the new session's model chip and the chat header's model pill) list, below the Claude models
(Claude Code's default; since 0.206 a family each — Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, Fable — whose item picks
its alias and whose submenu holds its versions, the versions since 0.168; "Another model…"), the
providers its worker allows; picking one in a chat asks once ("The agent restarts on …"), and a
Claude model picked there leaves the provider in the same `PATCH`; a provider session's chat
header names the provider instead of the model and shows no cost, which the CLI computes at a
made-up rate for a model it does not know; "This device" (since 0.240) has "Forget this device",
which deletes the copies of chats and attachments this device keeps for the user (§6) and then
reads "Forgotten"; it is off while no user is known (before `/api/me` answers, with none stored on
the device); and
"Workers" lists a line per worker: its online dot, name, system (macOS, Linux, Windows), status
and "Revoke", or "Delete" for a revoked one. The project settings (`#/p/<id>/settings`, "Project
settings…" in the project's menu, below) have Appearance (the "Project appearance" dialog: the
name, icon as an emoji, letters or an image, the color, a live preview in the app theme; before
0.88 it also had the app theme; on a phone a full-screen sheet; "Delete project" next to the
button that opens it; since 0.64, before it a section "Project" had "Rename" and "Delete
project"; the personal project has neither the name field nor the delete), Quick messages (since
0.167, below) and Workspaces (the
workspace records with "VS Code sessions", "Make default", "Remove"; "Add a workspace", "Import
from Claude Code"; they are no longer in the sidebar).

The project bar (since 0.51; since 0.114 its marks, search, menu and orders): Spacious, 72 px, a
tile per project with its icon on its color at ~24 %, the current one more saturated with a pill
of its color at the left edge; Compact, a row per project with its icon on its color and its
full name, the bar as wide as the longest name, 200–320 px (a longer one ends in "…"), the hub's
name "HQC" by its mark, "+", the order menu, the settings and the avatar in one row at the
bottom, and the session column narrower so the chat keeps at least 300 px. A project's mark, on
the tile or on the row's icon: an amber count of its sessions that wait for the user ("needs
you"), else a stripe that runs around the icon while one of them works (the rule of a session
row's pulsing dot: `running`, `queued`, a subagent or a background task at work after its turn,
a busy VS Code; archived and service sessions do not count), under `prefers-reduced-motion` too,
since a still arc does not read as work: one lap in 18 s, faster the more output tokens per
second the project's working sessions report in `output_per_s` (§6, 0.122), the lap 18 s divided
by min(6, 1 + log2(1 + rate / 40)), changed without a jump; else (since 0.67) a blue dot while
one has unread events, the name bold in Compact; an idle project has none; a starred project
also has a star on the icon's bottom right corner. While one of its sessions works, by that
rule, the tile's tooltip names the project, the agents at work (each working session's agent and
its `subagents`) and the rate, "hqc · 3 agents · 120 tokens/s", also beside the amber count. "+"
asks for a name, makes the project and opens its settings. The order menu (⇅, with more than one
project) has Custom, Name and Recent (§3 User `project_sort`, `PATCH /api/me`, applied at once
and put back if the hub refuses): Custom is the hub's order (`PUT /api/me/project_order`), Name
the shown names, Recent the newest `updated_at` among the project's listed sessions (not
archived, not a service session) first, the projects without one after them, the newest project
first; the starred projects first in each. Its "Reorder…" (since 0.64) arranges the user's own
order whichever is shown: the tiles are dragged (or moved with ↑/↓ when focused) instead of
opened, ✓ stores the order with `PUT /api/me/project_order` and switches the bar to Custom, ✕
drops it. A right click on a project (or the menu key) opens the project's menu: Open in new tab,
Add to (Remove from) favorites, then the end it shares with "⋯" in the session column's head
(below): Project settings…, Archive project (Restore for an archived one) and Delete project…,
neither of the last two for the personal project. Archive project takes it off the bar at once, without a
question, the open one giving its place to the personal project (on a phone, back to the
projects screen), and shows "Archived «name» · find it with the search on the bar · Undo" for 5
s at the bottom of the bar (on a phone "Archived «name» · Undo" at the bottom of the projects
screen); Undo and Restore send `/unarchive`, and the project comes back in its place; a refusal
of the hub puts it back on the bar in the hub's order and says why. The project search — its
magnifier in the bar's head, or its key from anywhere (⌘K on a Mac, Ctrl+K elsewhere, unless
changed in Settings ▸ Keys) — finds projects by
their shown name, the archived ones too (marked "archived") once something is typed: in Compact
the field takes the place of "HQC" and the bar's list shrinks to the matches, with tiles a 290
px panel with the names opens over the session column; ↑/↓ select, Enter opens the match, Esc
(the focus back on the magnifier) or a press outside the bar closes it, "N of M" counts the
matches, and a match's right click opens its project's menu. An archived project opened from the
search, an address or one of its sessions shows its session list like any other; the bar has no
tile for it.

The session column (since 0.114): 280–310 px by default, narrowing with the window; its right
edge is dragged (or moved with ←/→ in 16 px steps when focused) between 240 and 560 px, the
width kept on this device (`hqc.look`), never so wide that the chat gets less than 300 px. Its
head is one row: the project's name, the magnifier (the search page, §15), "⋯" and "+" (a new
session, below). "⋯" (since 0.206) holds the list's order — State, Recent and Custom, the one
shown checked, none while Reorder runs — and "Reorder…"; then "New room…" (§7.1.1); then, on a
phone, whose project screen has no bar to right-click, Add to (Remove from) favorites, and the
end of the bar's menu above: Project settings…, Archive project (Restore) and Delete project….
Under the head the scrolling list: a new session's "Draft" while one is open (below), the
project's favorites (§3 Favorite) under the name "Favorites" and their count as any group's, then
the groups (below); another project's list opens at its top (since 0.211), not at the scroll the
previous one left. A row is a dot — amber
waiting, red error, the project color pulsing while it works, an empty ring idle, `</>` while it
is open in VS Code and not working there, (since 0.206) the pause sign, muted and titled
"Paused", for a paused session that neither works nor waits (one still ending its turn keeps its
pulsing dot) —
then the title, "Draft", the unread count, and in Spacious the state line under the title (the
state, "N queued", "N agents"); Compact puts the row on one line, "N agents" after the title and
the state in the dot alone (faded while the worker is offline). A desktop row has no time (its
group says how old it is) and no `worker · path`; a phone row shows its time in Recent. On a
desktop the mouse on a row shows two round buttons past the column's right edge, Archive and a
star (they stay 300 ms after the mouse leaves the row or them, for the way between them), and no
card or tooltip: Archive archives the row as its menu's Archive does; the star, filled on a
favorite, adds the session to the favorites or takes it out as its menu's item does. A right
click on a row (the menu key; on a phone a long press or a right click) opens its menu: Open in
new tab, Add to (Remove from) favorites, Rename, Move to project… (not for a room), Restart
session (not for an archived, a service, a VS Code-driven or a paused session, a room or one whose
worker is offline), (since 0.160) Pause session while the agent works, as in the chat's header
(below), or Resume session for a paused one, Archive, and Delete…, which asks in a second step of
the menu with the focus on Cancel. A folder's rules are in the chat's "More" (below). A desktop
row (not in Reorder) can also be dragged onto another project on the bar, whose tile or row is
ringed while the row is over it: dropped there, the session moves
(`POST /api/sessions/{id}/move`) into that project's one `ready` folder on the session's worker,
or, with none or several, "Move to project…" opens over the list with that project chosen; a
refusal is the list's notice. At the bottom of a desktop column: "Requests" while one is open (§10.1), then the
workers line — "N workers online", the open session's worker with "N running" (its sessions in
every project, by the rule of the list's Running group), "offline" while the socket is down —
whose click opens the "Workers" list above it (§10.2). A phone's project screen (`#/p/<id>`) has
the same column with one head row after "‹" back to the projects and no buttons past the column;
"Requests" and the workers line are on the phone's first screen (below).

The chat header (since 0.206): the title, then the meta row — the state, the permission mode and
the model as round pills beside it (below and §6 `permission_mode`; none for a room or the
service session, and an archived session's are the names alone, without a menu), then, on a
computer, "started by <address>", "on <worker>", the folder with its copy button, "Browser", the
cost and, since 0.222, the context. Since 0.229 the cost item names the session's tokens after
the cost ("$2.25 · 3.4M tokens this session"; a room's "this room" sums its agents'; the tokens
show also for a session on a provider, which has no cost shown; the hover gives the exact
number). On a phone the header is lines at even gaps, with even
padding above and below: "‹", the title and the header's buttons, centred on the title's line,
the title cut only at the first button; the state at its full text and "N agents" (a room's: the
state and its mode); the two
pills, each at its full text with its chevron, 22 px tall as on a computer (20 px in a phone's
Compact look), then "started by <address>", whose address gives way to an ellipsis first and a pill's text (a
provider's long label) only past it. The lines under the first are as wide as the header past
"‹". Without pills "started by" is that line alone, and without either there is no such line;
a room has no pills, and its agents' line stays right under its state's, above "started by" of
a room an agent made. "More" says where the session runs, "<worker> · <folder>" with the
folder's copy button (no worker while VS Code holds the session: the state pill names it), and
the cost with the tokens. The model pill names the provider (§3 Provider), else
the model (the one chosen, or the last usage's when none is or it is the chosen one's full
name), else "Default"; its menu is the model menu above, the session's model checked (a family
for its alias and for each of its versions, the version after the family's name, "Opus 4.8"):
the checked entry itself (the alias, or the version in the submenu) only closes the menu, a
family checked for one of its versions switches to its alias. "Another model…" asks for the name
in the menu (Enter sends it, an empty one nothing); the worker's usage limits stand under the
items (§6 `GET /api/workers`).

Since 0.222 the context item stands after the cost, behind a "/": "<n>% context" — the
`context_tokens` of the last `usage` that has them, as a share of its `context_limit` (rounded,
over 100 when the context is past the limit; the hover says "329k of 967k tokens before
auto-compaction") — and " · cache m:ss", the time left of the session's prompt cache, which ends
`cache_ttl_s` after that `usage`'s time (the worker has taken the time since the request off
it), counted down every second while there is time left, by a clock of the item alone, not of
the chat; after its end "cache expired"; the hover adds "Claude's cache of this session ends at
<time>; a message after that reads the whole context again". The cache part is shown only while
the session is not Running (a response in the work renews the cache) and not for a session on a
provider, whose endpoint has no such cache; a room has no item, and neither has a session VS
Code holds (its turns are not reported, the numbers would stand still); after VS Code lets the
session go, the item shows the last hqc turn's numbers until hqc's next turn. A later `usage`
with the total only leaves the item as it was (once the earlier `usage` is loaded, §6 below),
and a cache end the date cannot hold leaves the cache part out. A `system
conversation_cleared` after that `usage` empties it. On a phone the item is short, "34% · cache
41:12", and stands in the state's line after "N agents". It does not give way in the one-line
row, as the cost does not. The title is renamed in place:
on a computer a pencil after it, shown on hover, and on a phone a tap on the title turns it into
a field; Enter or leaving the field sends `PATCH /api/sessions/{id} {title}` with the name
trimmed (an empty or unchanged one sends nothing), Esc keeps the old one, a refusal is the
chat's notice "Not renamed: …"; not for an archived or a service session, a room and a room's
agent included. While the agent works (`running`, `waiting`, `queued`, and since 0.212 an `idle`
session whose subagents or background tasks still work after its turn, which the header shows
as Running; not an archived or a service session, a room or one paused already) "Pause" (§17.3;
on a phone an icon, "Pause session") stands right before Stop, or alone after the turn, where
Stop has no turn to stop and spares the background work (§8.1) that a pause ends with the
agent's process; a paused session that is not archived has "Resume" in its place, before Stop
while its turn still runs; their refusals are the chat's notice ("Not paused: …", "Not
resumed: …").
"More" (⋯) holds, as far as each applies: on a phone where the session runs and the cost (above),
and "Retry" for a failed one; Schedules (not for a room, §16), Move to project… (not for
an archived session or a room), "Folder rules" (a link to the rules screen of the session's
folder, §6), Restart session (as in the row's menu; a refusal "Not restarted: …"); with none of
them, and in the service session, there is no "More".

The client's menus (a row's, a project's, the head's, the header's pills, a new session's chips,
the feed's) close on Esc or a press outside, move with ↑/↓ and give the focus back to what had
it; while one, the workers list or the slid-out column is open, a permission card does not take
Enter and Esc (§10.1). Since 0.206 an item with a submenu (a model family's versions) shows a
chevron: on a computer the submenu is a flyout beside the item, to its right where it fits, else
to its left, opened by the mouse on the item or by →, which focuses its first entry; ↑/↓ move
within it, ← and Esc close it alone with the focus back on the item, and it goes 250 ms after the
mouse left both the item and it; on a phone the chevron is a button of its own beside the item
and unfolds the submenu under it, indented. A click on the item itself picks it.

The session list (since 0.53, T50): State / Recent / Custom of the column head's "⋯" (State groups Needs
you / Running and then the idle sessions by how long ago they were active, "Idle · Today", "Idle
· Yesterday", "Idle · Last 7 days", "Idle · This month", "Idle · Earlier"; Recent Today /
Yesterday / Last 7 days / This month / Earlier; Custom is one list in the saved order; empty
groups are left out, none is collapsed; since 0.102 an `idle` session whose subagents still work
after its turn ended, `subagents` > 0, and since 0.104 one whose background tasks still run,
`background_tasks` > 0, is under Running, and its row and the chat header say "Running") and its
"Reorder…"; Reorder shows "Reorder · Cancel · Done" under the head and gives each row a handle
(on the left on a desktop, on the right on a phone), dragged with pointer events (mouse and
finger) or moved with ↑/↓ while focused; Done stores the order with `mode: custom`, Cancel
restores the previous one. Both are `session_order` above. Archiving from a row (its menu or its
archive button) hides it at once and shows "Archived «title» · Undo" for 5 s; the `/archive`
call goes only when the toast ends, when another row is archived (the previous one is sent
first), before Reorder or archive mode opens, or when the page is hidden or left (`fetch` with
`keepalive`); Undo cancels it, so nothing reaches the hub and the row is back in its place. The
session header has no archive, restore or delete. "Archive N" under the list opens archive mode:
the sidebar without the project tint, a hatched header with a back arrow, "Archive", "<project>
· N sessions" and "Read-only…", a search, and rows with "Archived <when>" and "Restore" and
"Delete" always shown (delete confirmed in the row). An open archived session has an "Archived"
chip in the header, a hatched band "Archived <when> · read-only. Restore or delete it from the
list on the left." (the time from `archived_at`, none without it), the feed dimmed and no input.

A window 900–1079 px wide (since 0.114) has no session column in its layout: "Sessions" at the
left of the chat's header (with the amber count of the project's sessions that wait for the
user), or its key (⌘\, Ctrl+\ off a Mac, unless changed in Settings ▸ Keys), slides the column
out over the chat from the bar's edge, as
wide as on a desktop, with a scrim over the rest; a session, a new one, a project or a page
opened (from the column or elsewhere), Esc, a click on the scrim or leaving that width puts it
away. With no session open the main column says "Open Sessions to pick a session or start a new
one".

The phone (since 0.114): the first screen, `#/`, lists the projects — Favorites, Needs you (a
session waits for the user), Running (one works, none waits) and the other projects ("All
projects" while no other group has one) with "New project" last, each group in the bar's order
and each project in the first group that takes it (a favorite only under Favorites, a project
that waits and works only under Needs you) — or, picked from its title's menu, "Sessions": every
live session of the projects on the bar in the groups of State, each row with its project's name
before the state line and its tile at the end, without a menu, a working one's dot in that
project's color, its unread count blue and "Draft" in the secondary text. Its head is one row:
the title with that menu (kept while the page is open), "Requests" with the count (amber, as
what waits for the user), the search, the settings and the avatar; the workers line is at the
bottom, and a project archived from there shows its "Archived «name» · Undo" there. A project's
row has its tile (with the bar's stripe running around it, at the bar's speed, while one of its
sessions works and none waits), its name (bold with unread events; in Spacious "N waiting · N
running" under it), then a running mark in the project's own color with how many work, the amber
count of those that wait and the count of those with unread events. A project opens its own
screen, `#/p/<id>`, the session list; everything else replaces the screen as before. In both
views one round floating button (since 0.188), above the workers line at the right, opens the
new-session window of the project in use, `#/p/<id>/new` (§3 User `new_session_project_id`:
picked in Settings, the personal project until then), painted in that project's color as its
tile is; it is there once `/api/me` has answered and that project is known (from the lists, or
from the list kept from the last load), not while the Undo bar of an archived project stands in
its place, and the lists leave room for it under their last row. Both looks apply on a phone
too: in Compact its list heads, groups and rows are denser and a row is one line with the state
in the dot. Every back arrow ("‹" of a chat, a project's list, the requests, the search, the
settings pages and the worker enrollment) steps back through the tab's history
when the entry under the screen is the arrow's address, and otherwise opens that address in
place of the screen: the browser's or the phone's back gesture after an arrow never returns to
the screen the arrow closed. Each entry keeps in its `history.state` the address it was opened
from. A press on a button of the composer (send, attach, remove a file) leaves the focus in the
field: a phone keeps its keyboard, and the composer does not grow under the tap by the home
indicator's room before the click lands.

Keys to move around (since 0.242; before, the macOS app's own shortcuts did this by clicking
the page), each set in Settings ▸ Keys; the default on a Mac, then elsewhere: New session (⌘N,
Alt+N) opens the new-session window of the current project — a browser keeps ⌘N and Ctrl+N for a
new window of its own, so there it needs another key; Archive session (⌃⌘A, Ctrl+Alt+A) archives
the open session as its row's menu does, with Undo, where the session column shows it (nothing
where the column is not shown: the Undo is the column's); Previous and Next session (⌥⌘↑ and ⌥⌘↓,
Alt+↑ and Alt+↓) open the row above or below the current one in the session column, the last or
the first without one, nothing past either end or where the column is not shown; Previous and
Next project (⌃⌘↑ and ⌃⌘↓, Alt+Shift+↑ and Alt+Shift+↓) open the tile above or below the current
one on the project bar; Back and Forward (⌘[ and ⌘], Alt+← and Alt+→) step the page's history.
They work with the focus in the input too; a key a field or a menu has already taken (prevented)
is theirs.

The page has one function for a wrapper around it (since 0.188),
`window.hqc.newSessionInProject()`: it opens that same new-session window, `#/p/<id>/new` of
the project in use, and, called before `/api/me` has answered and that project is known, does it
as soon as they are. The macOS app hangs its global shortcut on it.

Quick messages (since 0.167, §3 Project; the user's own since 0.255, §3 User). A chat whose
project is known has a lightning-bolt button in the composer's row, right after the attach one (and
after the key button, when there is one). It opens a list above the field, in the look of the
command list: a row per message, the user's own in their order, then the project's in its stored
order, a text in both once at its place in the user's list (since 0.255); its first line on one
line ending in "…" when it does not fit, the
whole text as the row's title (each row a button, so Tab reaches it), and a last row "Edit quick
messages: all projects · this project", links to Settings (`#/settings`) and to the project's
settings (`#/p/<id>/settings`); with no messages the list says "No quick messages yet — add them
in Settings or in project settings", with the same two links. A press on a message sends it at once as the input of
the session, exactly as stored, and closes the list; what is typed in the field and the files
attached stay as they are, unsent. Esc and a press outside close the list, the field keeps the
focus; the list and the field's completion list are never open together. Opening the list asks
the hub for the project and for the user again (`GET /api/projects/{id}`, `GET /api/me`): the
lists kept on the client show at once, and what another device changed shows when the answers
come.
Each message in the list is a button. The opener has `aria-expanded` and, while the list is open,
`aria-controls`; Esc on a message of the list puts the focus back on the opener. The new session's
window has no such button.
A message the user typed, with text, has a lightning-bolt button "Add to quick messages" among
its buttons, right before fork (since 0.204); like fork, not while it waits for delivery or
when it was not delivered. A press reads the project from the hub, adds the
message's text exactly as typed at the end of that list and sends it whole in `PATCH
/api/projects/{id}`; a text the hub's list has already sends nothing. A text the project's list
has, or the user's own list has (since 0.255), is a check, "In quick messages", that cannot be
pressed; the hub's refusal is said in the chat's notice. The button always adds to the
project's list. The service session has no such button.
The project settings have a section "Quick messages" between Appearance and Workspaces: a line
saying what they are, the list in stored order (each message as written, kept to 3 lines, with
"Edit" and "Delete"), and "Add a quick message"; the form for a new or an edited message is a
text area with "Save" and "Cancel", an edit happens in place of the row of the message it started
from (found by its text; gone from the list meanwhile: at the end of the list), and while a form
is open the other buttons are disabled. Every change
first reads the project from the hub, applies itself to that list (an added message goes last; an
edit replaces the first message equal to the text it started from, or adds the new text when none
is; a delete removes the first message equal to its text, and sends nothing when none is), sends
the whole list in `PATCH /api/projects/{id}` and shows the hub's refusal under the list. The
Settings section (since 0.255) is the same editor over the user's list: it reads `GET /api/me`
and sends the whole list in `PATCH /api/me`.
The messages cannot be reordered and have no names.

Secrets (since 0.147, §14). The composer of a session whose worker has `session_secrets` has a
key button beside the attach one: a form above the composer with the kind (Password, SSH key), a
name and the value — a password field (`autocomplete="current-password"`, so a phone's password
manager fills it), a key a text area without spelling help, with an optional passphrase and
"Remember for this workspace". "Give" sends `POST /api/sessions/{id}/secrets`; on success the
answer's `note` goes on a line of its own into the message being written and the form closes; on
an error the form keeps what was typed and shows the reason. The value lives only in the form
while it is open: never in the draft, the feed, `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`. The hub's
`hqc_secret` card (`approval.request` with `tool: hqc_secret` and `secret`) shows "The agent
asks for a secret / an ssh key: <name>", the agent's purpose and the same fields, with "Give"
and "Decline"; it is answered once the hub's `approval.response` with `give` or `deny` comes,
and on the requests screen it has the same form. When the worker reads
Vaultwarden and its fields (`secret.reads_vault`, since 0.243) the card has "Vaultwarden | Type it": it opens on
Vaultwarden when the agent named an entry (`secret.vault`), on "Type it" otherwise. In
Vaultwarden mode the entry is in a field the owner may change, with a second, labelled field
"Field" (unmasked: a field's name is not secret, the worker logs it and the feed line names it;
placeholder "empty: password", for an `ssh_key` "empty: private key"; prefilled with
`secret.vault_field`, optional); "Give" sends `vault`,
and `vault_field` when the field is not empty, instead of a value — the worker reads it, and the
value reaches neither the client nor the hub; "Type it" gives the fields above. A card of a
worker that reads Vaultwarden but not fields (no `reads_vault`, an entry in `secret.vault`) has
the switch and opens on the entry, without "Field", as before 0.243. The
rules screen of a workspace whose worker has `session_secrets` lists the ssh keys kept for it
(name, fingerprint) with Delete after a confirmation; an offline worker gives a line saying so.

The browser (since 0.148, §14). The menu of the chat header's mode pill of a session whose worker
has `browser` has, under the switch, "Browser: off · Give the browser" or "Browser: on · Turn
off"; giving it asks once ("Give the
agent your browser? The agent restarts with your Chrome on <worker>: it opens its own tabs in
your profile, signed in as you, and sees the tabs you drag into its tab group. It can click and
type there; it cannot upload files. Watch what it does."), taking it away says the agent
restarts without it; both send `PATCH /api/sessions/{id} {browser}`. While it is on, the chat
header's meta row on a computer shows "Browser" after the folder, titled "The agent has your Chrome on
<worker>". Since 0.149 the lists mark it in the browser's own color (fuchsia, `--browser`, apart
from the amber of waiting, the blue of unread and the violet of messages between sessions): the
session's row has a ring of it and a globe after its title ("The agent has your browser"), and a
project with such a session that is not archived has a dashed ring of it around its tile on the
project bar and on a phone's list of projects, around the marks it has already.

A new session (since 0.114) opens at once as a chat window, `#/p/<project>/new`, with nothing on
the hub yet: the header says "New session", "Draft" and where it will run; the list shows it as
the group "Draft" on top, the current row "New session" with "Draft · <worker> · <path>"; the
feed says to write the first message (or, for a project without workspaces, that a session needs
one, with "Add a workspace"). Chips over the input choose the workspace (each of the project's
with its worker and path, the default marked, "Add a workspace…" under them), the folder inside
it (typed, `.` by default), the permissions (the worker's default, Ask, Auto, Auto after the
one-line confirmation below) and the model (Claude Code's default, an alias, since 0.168 a
version, or another name typed), the defaults already chosen: the project's
`default_workspace_id`, else its first workspace (§13.4). The first message creates the
session with those choices (`POST /api/projects/{id}/sessions`, no title) and goes in as its
first input; until the chat is there
the input sends nothing more ("Starting…") and the chips are off, while what is typed and
attached meanwhile stays; the draft row stands for the new session in the list. Once the chat's
first page is in, the address becomes `#/s/<session>` and the session's chat replaces the
window: the message in its feed, the text and files not sent in its input, the caret there. A
create the hub refuses keeps the window, the message back in the input with its files and the
reason above it. Left unsent, the draft is gone; left while the session is being created, the
session stays in the list with what was typed meanwhile as its draft, or, refused, the list says
"Not started: <reason> — your message was not sent".

The chat (since 0.114): its header has "‹" on a phone, "Sessions" in a 900–1079 px window, then
the title, the state pill and the meta line. A session VS Code has (`locked_vscode`) says "In VS
Code on <worker>" in the pill, marked `</>` ("In Claude Code…" when another program holds it, by
`held_by.entrypoint`), and in place of the input a bar: "Close the session in VS Code to write
from here." while it is held, else "VS Code was the last to run this session." with "Take over
here" (§9.3). "Retry" of a failed session is a filled button. In the feed a message's time
stands at the right end of its first line, inside the bubble or plate for the user's, after a
note on that line (since 0.178 an icon, its words the tooltip: "Joined the turn", §17.2; "Instead
of the request", §10.1) and before "· scheduled", "· awaiting delivery", "· queued" (since 0.161,
an input that came while a turn ran, see the WebSocket below), "· not delivered" or "· forking…";
its buttons are always shown, in the line's flow so that they cover no text: Copy
and, for the user's message, "Add to quick messages" (see quick messages above) and "Fork from
here", at the message's bottom right, on a computer and a phone alike (since 0.228; from 0.204
left of the time in its first line, see Copy and Quote below): at the right end of an agent
message's usage line and of the bottom line of "Reply to"; else floated right at the end of the
text's last line (inside the bubble or plate for the user's and the text answer's), so that a last
line with room keeps them and a full one puts them on a line of their own under it; after a text
that ends in a code block, a table, a rule, a quote or a formula, on a line of their own; a message
with no text (files only) has them left of its time. A user's text and a reasoning are shown without
their trailing line breaks, which would put the buttons lines below the text. Since
0.156, until the hub answers a fork (it copies the source's history first, seconds for a long
session) the message says "· forking…" and its "Fork from here" is disabled; the client asks for
no second fork before the same message meanwhile.
A run of tool calls is "N tool calls ·
time" and the call's line when it is one, else the tools it called, each once, in the order
first called ("(Bash, Read, chrome-devtools/take_screenshot)", an MCP tool as
`<server>/<tool>`); a Skill call's line names its skill, a SendMessage call's line (since 0.163)
says what it sent: its `summary`, else its plain-text `message` on one line; since 0.177 a call
with none of the keys a line reads (an MCP tool's) shows its arguments in the order of
`args_preview` (§4: the shortest value first), each field as Claude Code shows one of an MCP
tool's input, `name: "a", x: 90.7`, and a call's row and the header of a group of one call show
its result after its line and "→", on the same line: what the opened row shows, the error (without
the CLI's `<tool_use_error>` tags), else the result (nothing for a change that went through), a
JSON object as `key: value, …`, a lone `result` field as its value, any other text as written;
when both do not fit, the result keeps three parts of the width to the line's one, the shorter
leaving the rest to the other; a row's time runs from the call to its result (`duration_ms` when
given), a thinking line shows as much of its text as the line holds, not 60 characters, an
answered request's row names the tool and its argument as the call's row does ("Read src/a.rs",
"move (probe-bench) x: 90.7") and a request card names an MCP tool as `<tool> (<server>)`;
thinking and tool lines are fainter than the text, and an open thinking block is prose in the
feed's font. Since 0.180
an opened call's result has its `http` and `https` addresses as links (opened in a new tab, each
labelled with the address it opens, a look-alike host in its punycode form), its images
(`tool.result.artifact_ids`) as thumbnails under its text, each opening in the viewer over the chat
(§12), and "Full result" when `artifact_id` holds the whole text (it opens in a new tab); a run with
an `Artifact` call whose result names one page address (the result starts "Published ", "Created a
new Artifact at http", "An earlier attempt of this call already created the Artifact at http" or
"Opened the Artifact at http", and has one "at http(s)://…", as the VS Code tab reads it, extension
2.1.319) has that address as a link on a line of its own under the run, seen while the run is
folded. Since 0.135 a subagent has two cards in the project's colour, two lines each at any width,
which never wrap: a long text is cut
with an ellipsis. Its start: a call of `Agent` (`Task` in older Claude Code) is no row of a run: it
ends the run before it and is a card of its own (tinted background and border), its result inside
it. Its first line is a small agent icon, "Agent started:" dimmed (since 0.141; before it only the
card's label for a screen reader said "Subagent"), the call's `description`, the call's
`subagent_type` dimmed (since 0.141 not on a phone screen 480 px wide or less, where the label
leaves the task too little room; the type opens with the call's arguments) and a "background" chip
when its `run_in_background` is true (since 0.205 on a phone the label is "Agent:" and the chip is
left out, for the room of the task); its second the subagent's state: while the latest
`subagents.live` (§4) has a row with the call's `call_id`, a pulsing dot, what it does now, alone,
as the CLI's text often starts "Running …" itself ("Running" before any progress and, since 0.202,
while what it does now is the call's task itself) and, at the right, the row's `<tokens> tokens ·
<n> tools · <run time>` (since 0.205 on a phone `<tokens> · <run time>`, without the word "tokens"
and the tool calls), ticking every second as above the input; else
as the first `system task_notification` of the call says it ended — the first with its `call_id`,
else, after a background launch whose result names the subagent `agentId: <id>`, the first with that
`task_id` (after a restart the CLI reports a subagent cut off by it without the call's id; a later
one, that of a SendMessage which continued the subagent, is no end of the call, though the CLI
describes a later notification of a task as replacing the earlier one, §8.1): `completed` "Done ·
<run time>", `failed` "Failed", `stopped` "Stopped", the run time from the call to the notification;
any other `status`, or none, leaves it to the result —; else by the call's result: the CLI's answer
for a subagent the user stopped (an error that starts "[Request interrupted", whose notification is
no line, §8.1) is "Stopped", another error "Failed" with its `error_text`, a subagent sent or moved
to the background (`run_in_background`, or a result that starts "Async agent launched", the CLI's
answer then) "In background", without an end seen, any other "Done · <run time>", from the call to
the result (its `duration_ms` when the times say nothing); with none of them "Running" and the time
since the call. "Done" has a check mark, "Failed" a cross. A click on the head opens the call's
arguments and result as a call's row shows them. Its end, a lighter card of the same kind, stands
where the subagent ended: at a `system task_notification` with `status` `completed`, `failed` or
`stopped` whose `call_id` is an `Agent` or `Task` call's, or whose `task_id` is the `agentId` of
such a call's background launch, in place of the notification's "Background task ·" line (a
command's or a Monitor's notification keeps its line; since 0.186 the output file the worker
uploaded after it (§8.1) is drawn inside that line, under its text once the line is opened,
not as a card of its own); and at the result of a subagent that ran in
the foreground, any result of the call but a background launch's. Its first line is the state's mark
(a check, a cross, a square when stopped), "Agent finished:" dimmed (since 0.141; since 0.205
"Agent:" on a phone), the task, "done", "failed" or "stopped", since 0.181 the notification's
`usage` as `<tokens> tokens · <n> tools` (§4; since 0.205 on a phone `<tokens>`), and, on the
call's first end only, the run time from the call to the end (a later one, a SendMessage that
continued the subagent, would count from the call); its second the end's text, the notification's
or the result's (an error's `error_text`; a done one's without the CLI's trailer, from the last
`agentId: <id> (use SendMessage …)` line that the `<usage>` block follows), on one line without its
Markdown marks; a click on the head opens the whole text as Markdown. In the Compact look the
start's mark is a pulsing dot while it runs, a check when done, a cross when it failed or stopped
and a grey dot in the background; the end's a check when done, else a cross.
Copy (since 0.204, with Search and Quote until 0.233; a phone's "Quote" button is gone): the button
of an agent message, the user's message, a text answer, a message from another session and the reply
to it, what the session sent to another ("Sent to") and the reply it got ("Reply from"), a room post
and the agent's reasoning (at the right end of its summary line while folded, since 0.228 at the end
of its text while open; a click on it neither folds nor unfolds it), also in the history of a
subagent; tool output has none. It is always shown (see the message's time above) and puts the whole
text of its message into the clipboard, whatever is selected in it. A press on the strip's buttons
does not take the focus from the input. "Quote" (since 0.234; before it a button of every message,
which took the selection or, with none, the message's first two sentences) is one button over the
input, not on the messages: the word "Quote" in the input's row, over the right end of the field,
left of send, taking no room, so that the field, its wraps and the feed stay as they are while it
comes and goes (the end of the draft's last line fades under it). It is shown while the chat holds a
selection that starts in the feed or in a subagent's history, and where there is an input; a
selection that starts elsewhere (the header, the input) gives none. Following the selection is cheap
(whether it is there, not its text); the text is read when the button is pressed. A press puts the
selection into the input after the draft as `> ` lines, with the caret at its end, and clears the
selection. The selection is the browser's own text when the range lies inside one message; one
across messages is taken whole, by lines (paragraphs, list items and table rows on separate lines,
cells apart by a tab), without the messages' times and heads, their meta lines, the summary line of
a reasoning, the caption bar of a code block, the hidden text of folded blocks and the buttons; a
range that starts in the line a folded reasoning shows begins with its selected part of that line
(without "Thinking · "), one that only passes through it leaves the line out; a range that ends
outside the feed it starts in (a triple click on the last paragraph of the last message) is cut at
that feed's end, and one that ends at the start of the next block gives its message's own part. A
press on the button takes the text at once and keeps the button, though the press clears the
selection (a phone's tap does, before the click); the click, a press elsewhere or a press the
browser takes over lets go of it. The right-click menu below holds "Search in <the search picked in
Settings>" (since 0.142; the messages' buttons had it until 0.233) and Copy of the selection. On a
computer a right click on text selected in the feed or in a subagent's history opens the client's
menu of the same for that text (again since 0.228; from 0.204 the browser's): "Quote" where there is
an input, "Copy" and "Search in …"; it takes the text as Quote does, cut at the feed's end too
(since 0.234). A right click with nothing selected before it or outside the selection (a Mac's
browser answers it by selecting the word under the pointer), elsewhere in the chat and on a phone
gives the browser's own menu; one inside a selection that the browser cleared on the press (WebKit
off a Mac) selects it again. Firefox, which does not tell the text under the pointer, gives the
client's menu while the selection stays as it was and the browser's when the press cleared it.
Keys for the same (since 0.238; set in Settings ▸ Keys since 0.242), by default ⌘' and ⌘E on a
Mac, Ctrl+' and Ctrl+E elsewhere: the first quotes the selection as the button does (where there
is an input), the second searches it as "Search in …" does, in a new tab; they take a selection
that starts in the feed or in a subagent's history; without one the key is the browser's. The
button's tooltip and the menu's Quote and Search name the keys in use.
On a touch screen a finger that swipes a message of the chat's feed left quotes it, as Telegram
does (since 0.252): the agent's answer (one to another session's question too), the user's own
message, a message from another session or a room's post. The message follows the finger and a
quote mark comes out at its right at the finger's height; released past 60 px, the message's first
two sentences go into the input as Quote puts a selection there, with "…" when its text goes on
(the Markdown of an answer or of another session's message as its text, a list item or a table row
a line of its own; the user's message without its quote lines); released before, nothing. Where
there is no input a message does not move; a swipe on a code block or a table that scrolls
sideways scrolls it, and a touch held half a second before it moves is the browser's (a long press
selects text). A subagent's history has no swipe.
In the user's message a run of lines `> text` or a bare `>` (what Quote puts in) shows as a quote,
without the `>`, with a bar on its left (since 0.253; before it the lines showed as typed): those the
message starts with, blank lines between them too, stand above the time across the bubble, as in
Telegram, the time on the line of the text after them; one further on stands in the text, one line
break apart from it. A click on it
(not one that ends a selection), a tap (pressed on the finger's lift, as a button) or Enter or Space
on it takes the chat to the text it quotes, as Telegram does. The client looks for the quote's
letters and digits (lowercased, NFKC; in a source the feed renders as Markdown, its marks, link
targets, ordered-list numbers and fence lines left out) in the session's events before the message,
newest first: agent messages and reasoning, the user's messages, text answers to a request and side
questions without their own quote lines, messages from other sessions, side answers, the feed's
notes (a subagent's report, a background task's line, a compaction summary), the text of permission
and question cards, the arguments and
results of calls; the whole quote first, else its first paragraph (a quote taken across messages),
in the loaded events and then in each older page as it comes in, 1000 events a page, until it is
found; then in the events after the message (an answer quoted while it was being written is stored
after the quote). The feed renders from the block that draws the source (the block that starts at
it, else the one that holds it: a call shown on its permission card is that card's), as for a search
hit, lets go of the bottom, opens a folded reasoning the text is in, scrolls the text to the middle
and highlights exactly it for 2.4 s (the CSS Custom Highlight API). Where the text is not in the
page (a reasoning in a folded run of calls) or the browser has no custom highlights, the block is
marked as a search hit is. Found nowhere: "The quoted text is not in this chat"; an older page that
did not load: "Older history did not load".
The input is one row: the paperclip, the field growing with its lines up to 200 px, send; on a
computer its placeholder says "Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line". On a computer the input
takes the caret when the chat opens, once its newest page is in, unless a request waits for an
answer (an open approval in the feed, or the session `waiting`), another field has the focus, or a
menu or the slid-out column is open; on a phone only when the chat replaces a new session's window.
An open chat stays at its bottom while its images load: only a scroll up lets go of the bottom, and
a move up while the feed's scroll range changed is the browser's, not a scroll up (since 0.164),
unless it comes in the user's own scroll up (since 0.198).

than the text, and an open thinking block is prose in the feed's font. A call without a
`tool.result` is running (a pulsing dot) until its turn ends; since 0.161 one with an end of a
turn after it in `seq` order (the final `agent.message`, `status` `idle` or `error`, `system
turn_lost`) is not finished, marked with the cross of a failed call, as the VS Code tab marks a
call without a result once the session is not busy; a run is running while one of its calls
is, else it takes the mark of its last call.
Copy (since 0.204, with Search and Quote until 0.233; a phone's "Quote" button is gone): the button
of an agent message, the user's message, a text answer, a message from another session and the reply
to it, what the session sent to another ("Sent to") and the reply it got ("Reply from"), a room post

input, not on the messages: the word "Quote" in the input's row, over the right end of the field,

an input, "Copy" and "Search in …"; it takes the text as Quote does, cut at the feed's end too
(since 0.234). A right click with nothing selected before it or outside the selection (a Mac's

gives the browser's own menu; one inside a selection that the browser cleared on the press (WebKit

Keys for the same (since 0.238; set in Settings ▸ Keys since 0.242), by default ⌘' and ⌘E on a
Mac, Ctrl+' and Ctrl+E elsewhere: the first quotes the selection as the button does (where there

The input is one row: the paperclip, the field growing with its lines up to 200 px, send; on a
computer its placeholder says "Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line". On a computer the input
takes the caret when the chat opens, once its newest page is in, unless a request waits
for an answer (an open approval in the feed, or the session `waiting`), another field has the
focus, or a menu or the slid-out column is open; on a phone only when the chat replaces a new
session's window. An open chat stays at its bottom while its images load: only a scroll up lets
go of the bottom, and a move up while the feed's scroll range changed is the browser's, not a
scroll up (since 0.164), unless it comes in the user's own scroll up (since 0.198). The user's own
scroll of the feed is a wheel or trackpad, a finger, or the main button pressed on the feed's own
element (its scrollbar, its padding and the margins beside the column) while they are down, or a
scrolling key outside a field, and it goes on while scroll events follow within 400 ms of the last
of them (momentum, a bounce at an edge); it goes up or down as its last input did (the wheel's
sign, the finger's way, the key; the pressed button counts as up). While it goes on the chat does
not follow the bottom (since 0.198: Chromium drops the rest of a smooth wheel scroll when the page
sets a position). In WebKit outside Chromium (Safari, the macOS app, every browser on an iPhone),
while it goes on, the chat sets no scroll position of its own: it neither follows the bottom nor
renders older blocks, so a scroll up stops at the top of the rendered blocks until the scroll
settles (since 0.136 for a wheel, since 0.198 for the rest). Once it settles, the chat follows the
bottom if the feed still holds it and something moved it meanwhile, and renders the 60 older
blocks if the feed is still within 400 px of its top. Since 0.254, while the feed does not follow
its bottom (a move up that left it 80 px or more above its bottom, or a jump to an event, let go of
it) and the bottom is more than two of the feed's windows down, a button with a chevron down stands
in the middle of the feed's bottom edge, over the feed: the send button's corners, 56 × 28 px (48 ×
24 in Compact on a computer). Its press puts the feed at its bottom and the feed follows it again,
and keeps the focus in the input. Pressed while the user's scroll goes on (a fling coasting under
it), the rest of that scroll does not let go of the bottom, and in WebKit the feed goes there once
the scroll settles; a new input up after the press is a scroll of its own.

Messages between sessions in the feed (since 0.54, T51; mockups `Session`, `AskingSession`,
`MSession2`): violet blocks (`--relay`) with an arrow, ↗ for what left this session and ↙
for what came into it, and the other session's title as a link to it, its address in the
tooltip (since 0.64; plain address text when the user has no such session: deleted or unknown). In the answering session a `peer.message` is
"↙ Question from X" (`mode: ask`) or "↙ Message from X" with its text and files, and the final
`agent.message` whose `in_reply_to` is a question is "↗ Reply to X · delivered <time>"
(`reply_delivered_at`) with the turn's `attachment`s and token line inside the block; a send
of that turn that went `with_reply` (§7.1) follows the text after the separator line "sent
with hqc_send while answering". In the asking session the agent's own `hqc_send` / `hqc_ask`
call is "↗ Sent to X · delivered <time>" with the call's `text` and files: the `delivered_at`
and `artifact_ids` of the `peer.message` in X, which the client reads at `message_seq` of the
result (`GET .../events?after_seq=<message_seq - 1>&limit=1`), else the names in `files`, and
until then "waiting for a reply" (an ask), "queued", "waits for its next turn" (buffered) or
"goes with the reply"; the ask's result is "↙ Reply from X" with `reply` (the parts after the
separator under the same separator line) and `files` (Open / Download by `artifact_id`, the
local `path` under each). Such a send is also a `peer.message` in the asker; the client leaves
it out there, as the reply shows it.

Session object (`GET /api/sessions/{id}`, list, create, `PATCH`, `archive`):
`{id, project_id, owner_id, workspace_id?, worker_id?, cwd, title, title_source, slug, agent: {runtime,
acp_agent?, model?, runtime_session_id?, process_state, system_prompt?,
disallowed_tools[], restricted, start_failures}, auto_approve, wake_on_send, locked_by,
last_seq, archived, archived_at?, system?, held_by?, state, queue_len, last_read_seq, unread, created_at,
updated_at, commands?, command_info?, spawned_by?, permission_mode?, effective_permission_mode?,
permission_capped_by?, subagents?, background_tasks?, output_per_s?, foreground_calls?,
activity?, paused_at?, room_mode?, room_id?}`. `room_mode` (since 0.172): present only on a room
(§7.1.1), whose `worker_id` and `workspace_id` are absent and `agent.runtime` is `none`; `room_id`
(since 0.172): present only on a room's agent's session, the room's id.
`subagents` (since 0.70): the subagents the agent runs now, from `session.state` (§5.4);
absent — 0. The client shows "N agents" ("1 agent") next to the state in the chat header and in
the session's row of the list while it is above 0; a background subagent keeps it up after the
turn that started it has ended. Since 0.114, while it is above 0, the chat also shows the
subagents of the latest `subagents.live` (§4) above the input, outside the feed's scroll, so they
stay in view while the feed scrolls (the VS Code tab writes such lines into the chat, where they
scroll away): a line each, `<task>: <what it does now>` (the task alone before any progress, and
since 0.202 while what it does now is the task itself, which 2.1.312 sends after a call of a tool
that does not describe itself, ToolSearch or an MCP tool;
since 0.179, while its request to the model API waits to be retried, `<task>: Retrying 2/10
(529), next in 4 s`, "no response" in place of a status the attempt did not get) and
at its right `<tokens> tokens · <n> tools · <run time>` (`155.3k tokens · 188 tools · 4m 13s`;
since 0.205 on a phone `155.3k · 4m 13s`, for the room of the task), what was not reported yet left
out, the run time ticking every second from `duration_ms`; a long
line is cut with an ellipsis. Since 0.181 a subagent's line is `<task>: waiting for permission`
while an open `approval.request` of the chat names its `task_id` in `subagent` (§4). A subagent's
line goes when it ends; a dropped socket, and a chat
closed, clear the lines until the next subscribe brings the hub's list. Since 0.127 the list also
holds the agent's background commands, which only `background_tasks` counts, so the chat shows it while
either count is above 0; a command's line is its description and its run time. Since 0.141 a line
starts with "Agent: " (since 0.189 "Subagent: ") or "Command: " dimmed, as its `kind` says; a line without a known `kind`
(from an older worker, or a value this client does not know) has neither. Since 0.161 a line
marked `stoppable`, a subagent's, a command's or (since 0.169) a Monitor's, ends with a small
stop button, as in the VS Code tab: it sends `POST .../tasks/{task_id}/stop` and is disabled until
the hub answers, a failure
shown as a notice; the line goes when the task ends.
Since 0.169 the block holds timers too, and shows while any of its lines would: a Monitor watcher's
line ("Monitor: ", a command's line: its description and run time), the wakeup of the agent
("Wakeup: ", its reason) and its cron jobs ("Cron: ", the job's prompt, then ` · ` and its schedule
in words), each of the last two with `in 12m 34s` on the right in place of the counts, counting down
every second from `due_in_ms` as it was when the list came, `due` at 0 (a cron job whose next fire
is not known has none), and the lines of the session's schedules of the latest `schedules.live`
(§4, §16), after them ("Scheduled: ", the message, `in 12m 34s`), the next one first. A timer's
dot does not pulse: it waits, it does not run. The wakeups and the cron jobs wait while the agent is
idle, so the block shows for them with both counts 0, and so for a schedule; a line of a scheduled
message goes when its one-off is sent or it is paused or deleted (a recurring one then shows its
next run). These lines have the same one-line ellipsis as the other lines, on a computer and on a
phone; a dropped socket clears them too until the next subscribe. Since 0.237 a line of a scheduled
message opens and closes, under the last of them, the list of all the session's schedules (`GET
/api/schedules`, paused and spent ones too), as the task list opens under its row; "Schedules" in
the "More" menu opens the same list. Each schedule there is a line of when it runs and its next run
("paused", "sent …"), wrapped, with a small pause or resume button (while it has a next run) and a
delete button, as a command's stop, and its whole message under it. The list is read again on every
`schedules.live` and stays in place while the lines above it come and go; while it is open and no
schedule waits, the block keeps a line "Scheduled: none waiting", which holds it and closes it.
Since 0.223 the agent's task list (`tasks`, §4, §8.1) is a row of the block, after the goal's
(below) and ahead of the main agent's, while it has a task that is not completed: "Tasks: 3 of 7
completed", the completed tasks of all of them, and, when a task is in progress, ` · ` and its
`active_form` (else its subject), with a ▸ at the right end that turns to ▾ when it is open; a
press opens the list under the row, a mark and the words of each task in the list's order, ✓
completed (dimmed), ◐ in progress (its `active_form`, else its subject, in the accent colour), ○
pending (a status this client does not know is shown as pending), and a second press closes it.
The block shows for the row alone; with no task left to do (the list is empty or every task
completed) there is no row, and a list that comes later is closed. The row is the latest stored
`tasks` event of the session, the one of the highest `seq`: it is not a feed item, and the hub
sends the session's latest one on subscribe also when the client's `after_seq` is past it (§6
`subscribe`), which the client takes as the list and as nothing else: it does not move the
client's `lastSeq` back and leaves no gap in the history. The same on a phone.
Since 0.189 the main agent's row stands in the block, after the goal's and the task list's ("Main
agent: Working", §17.1), and the block shows also while that row does (a turn is on, input waits, or
an approval is awaited that is not an open request of the feed), with no subagent, command or timer;
in a room each agent at work has a row of its own, led by its name in place of "Main agent: ".
Since 0.218 the session's goal (`system goal`, §4: the last of them since the last
`conversation_cleared`, which ends the conversation the goal belonged to, is `set` or `unmet`) has a
row before all others, shown also while the agent is idle: "Goal: " and the condition on one line,
"N checks" after it while unmet checks came since it was set, a chevron that opens the whole
condition and "Last check: " with the last unmet check's reason, and "Clear goal", only where the
input is: it sends `/goal clear`, and while a turn runs (`running`, `waiting`, `queued`) it stops
the turn first, since a slash command waits for the end of the turn and a turn chasing a goal goes
on until the goal is met or hooks have blocked its end 9 times in a row (§8.1). There is no pause of
the goal: the session's Pause stops it with the agent, and Resume goes on with it (the CLI sets it
again on `--resume`).
Since 0.181 a subagent's line (a row whose `kind` is `agent`, or none this client knows,
whatever the feed holds: a chat loads only its latest events, and a subagent's subagent has no
call there; a command's, a Monitor's, a wakeup's and a cron job's line is none) is, but for its
stop button, a button that opens under it what the subagent has done (`GET
.../subagents/{task_id}/history`), drawn with the feed's own rows (thinking, tool calls with their
results, text), newest at the bottom, in a box at most 40 % of the window's height that scrolls,
opens at its bottom and stays there while the user has not scrolled up; "Earlier steps are not
shown." above it when `truncated`. While it is open it is fetched again 2 s after each answer,
not while the page is hidden, and at once when it is shown again, each time with `after` the
`event_id` of the last event it shows (the first time without): a reply with `continues` is
appended to it (an event it shows already is not added again), of which the newest 200 stay, and
it is `truncated` once any was dropped; a reply without `continues` takes its place. An older hub
passes no `after`. A second click closes it, one is open at a time, and it goes with its line
when the subagent ends.
The same on a phone, as wide as the block.
`background_tasks` (since 0.104): the background tasks the runtime lists for the agent now,
from `session.state` (§5.4); absent — 0. A command the agent left running in the background
keeps it up after the turn has ended.
`foreground_calls` (since 0.125): the `call_id`s of the calls the agent runs in the foreground
now and can move to the background (`POST .../background`), from `session.state` (§5.4), kept
in the hub's memory; absent — none. The chat offers "Run in background" for such a call
(§17.1).
`paused_at` (since 0.160): §3 Session, §17.3; absent — not paused. While it is set and the
session is still `running` or `waiting` (the turn the pause stopped has not ended yet), the chat
header and the session's row say "Pausing" (since 0.191; "Pausing after this turn" before) instead
of the state.
`activity` (since 0.179): what the agent waits on now (`retrying`, `compacting`, `thinking`),
from `session.state` (§5.4), kept in the hub's memory; absent — none. The chat's main agent
row (§17.1) shows it in place of "Working" and (since 0.233) of "Input queued"; a client ignores a
`kind` it does not know.
`permission_mode` and `effective_permission_mode` (since 0.42, T38): §3 Session; absent —
null. The client shows the mode in the chat header as a round pill beside the state:
`effective_permission_mode`, else `permission_mode`; "Auto" and (since 0.129) "Allow all" in
amber, "Ask" plain, "<runs> (<asked> asked)" ("Ask (Auto asked)", "Auto (Allow all asked)")
while the session asked for a higher mode than its worker runs (not restarted yet, a process
that cannot switch, `allow_auto = false`, or Allow all on a worker without `allow_all = true`),
"Default" (the worker's default, not reported yet) while both are absent; since 0.43 (T39), while
`permission_capped_by` is set, "<runs> (asked by <address>) · <own> after this turn" ("Ask
(asked by <address>) · Auto after this turn", "Auto (asked by <address>) · Allow all after
this turn"; since 0.129 "the session's own mode" for <own> when `permission_mode` is absent,
since the worker's default is not known to the client): the turn runs in the cap's mode, the
session's own mode comes back when it ends.
Since 0.206 the pill opens a menu with a switch Ask | Auto | Allow all over its items, the
session's own mode pressed (pressing it only closes the menu), and the browser's item under it
(above); a new session's "Permissions" chip has the worker's default, Ask, Auto and Allow all. Going to Ask
asks nothing; going to Auto asks one line: "Switch to Auto? Claude Code then runs tool calls
without asking; the worker's deny list is the only limit."; going to Allow all asks its own:
"Switch to Allow all? Claude Code then runs every tool call without asking, with no classifier
either; the worker's deny list, the ask rules of Claude Code's settings and its own safety
checks are the only limits." `spawned_by` (since 0.37, T34) — `{session_id, address}`
of the session whose agent started this one with `hqc_spawn` (§7), absent otherwise or once
that session is deleted; the client shows "started by <address>" in the chat header as a
link to it. `held_by` (`{entrypoint, status}`): the session is currently held open
by Claude Code outside hqc (§9.3): `state: locked_vscode`, takeover gives `409 vscode_open`
until it is closed there.
`system: true`: the worker's service session (§10.2): input, `stop`, `retry`, `takeover`,
`archive` and `DELETE` give `409 system_session`, `PATCH auto_approve: true` gives `403`.
`state`, `queue_len` (§17.1), `last_read_seq` and `unread` are computed for the requesting
user.
`commands` (since 0.28, T27) — the session's slash commands as the worker last reported them
(`session.state.commands`, §5.4), absent until a process of the session has reported a list. It
is not in `session.summary`: the client fetches the session object when it opens an idle chat
without a list. When the composer text is `/` followed by a name so far, the client lists the
commands starting with that name (ignoring case): arrows move, Tab or Enter insert `/<name> `,
Esc closes, a click or tap inserts. No list — no popup; only commands from the list are offered.
`command_info` (since 0.162) — the same commands with what the runtime says of each,
`[{name, description?, argument_hint?}]` (`session.state.command_info`, §5.4; a list stored
before 0.162 gives the names alone), only in an answer about one session (`GET
/api/sessions/{id}` and the other answers with one session object), not in `GET /api/sessions`
and `GET /api/projects/{id}/sessions`: with descriptions a session's list is kilobytes. The
client fetches the session object when it opens an idle chat without `command_info` (a session
from a list among them) and shows, after each command's name in the list, its argument hint
and then its description, muted, in the same line.

WebSocket `/api/ws` (upgrade only with the hub's `Origin`, §20; messages up to 1 MiB; since 0.230 the query `?deflate=raw` asks for compression, below): the client sends `subscribe {session_id, after_seq}` and receives
events with `seq > after_seq`, then the live stream; `agent.delta` has no `seq`. Since 0.72
the answer being written comes right after those events, before `subscribed`, as one
`agent.delta` with its text so far, and the stream carries only the deltas after it. Since 0.161
a delta with `reset` (the runtime abandoned the attempt that wrote the text, §8.1) ends that
text as an `agent.message` does: the hub drops its copy, so an input after it is not marked
`during_text` (below), and the client drops the text it shows live. Since 0.113
the session's latest `subagents.live` follows it when its list is not empty, and the stream
carries each new one; a client whose part of the hub's event stream fell behind gets it again,
or an empty one when none is kept, with the history it catches up. Since 0.169 the session's
`schedules.live` (§4, §16) follows it the same way, when its list is not empty, and the stream
carries each change of the session's schedules; a client that fell behind gets it, empty or not.
Since 0.223 the session's latest stored `tasks` event (§4) follows them when its `seq` is not above
`after_seq`, as stored and with its own `seq`: a client that loaded only the newest page of the
history, which does not reach back to it, still gets the list, and one whose `after_seq` is
before it has it among the events sent.
The text ends with the `agent.message` stored for it, a `status` other than `running` and (since
0.179) a `retraction`, after which the runtime sends no message for the text it took back. Since
0.208 the thinking being written comes the same way, as one `agent.delta` with `thinking` before
the answer's, and ends with the session's `agent.thinking` and with whatever ends the answer's
text, a delta with `reset` too. The client draws it as the `agent.thinking` it becomes, the
collapsed "Thinking · …" line that opens to the text so far, with the same mark in the one-column
look, as a block of its own after the stored events, above the inputs that stand under it
(below) and before the messages not stored yet. It is never a row of the run of tool calls
before it, folded with the run: it is there to be read while it is written; the stored
`agent.thinking` joins that run as any stored thinking does. Otherwise the stored
`agent.thinking` that ends it keeps its block, so a thinking the user opened stays open. Since
0.108 a `user.message`
or `peer.message` that came while that text was being written stands under it in the feed, live
(after the text, with the messages not stored yet) and once the text
is stored: the `agent.message` goes above the inputs with `during_text` right before it in `seq`
order, never above the input it answers (`in_reply_to`) and, since 0.161, never above one that
waited for a turn of its own and stands after the turns it waited through (below); a final one
takes along its `usage` and, since 0.161, the `system turn_interrupted` or `turn_ended_early`
line after it. Since 0.232 a `side.question` (§17.5) with `during_text` is one of these inputs
for this order, though it is no input: the answer goes above it too. The client takes this from
the hub's `payload.during_text`, never guesses it from times. Since 0.208 the same holds for the thinking: the hub marks an input stored while the
session's thinking is being written with `during_text` too; the thinking being written stands
above the inputs with `during_text` at the end of the feed, but one that waited for a turn of
its own and was delivered (below), and above the inputs that still wait for one (`pending`); the
stored `agent.thinking` goes above the inputs with `during_text` right before it as an
`agent.message` does, taking nothing along, and an `agent.message` after it in the same turn
stays under them. While the answer's text is being
written, the thinking being written right above the inputs under that text goes under it with
them: the worker holds a text until the next block of the response (§8.1), so the text came
before the thinking. An input stored before the session's last `agent.thinking` does not go under
the answer's text being written. Since 0.161 an
input with a `delivery` (`user.message`, `peer.message`) that came while a turn ran (with
`during_text` too, not failed, and not delivered at its own `ts` as a mirrored one is, §9.2)
stands at the bottom of the feed until the agent takes it, under everything live (after the
text being written, before the messages not stored yet), its time
followed by "· queued" while it is `pending` ("· awaiting delivery" stays for an input that came
while no turn ran), as the VS Code tab holds what is typed during a turn. Meanwhile the worker
may write it into the running turn (§17.2: a person's input or, since 0.174, a `send` of another
session, at once or after an answer to a permission request): once the agent takes it after its
current calls (`joined`) it stands where the agent took it (since 0.221; before, at its `seq`,
one with `during_text` under that text as above): right behind the last event of the session
that is no input stored before the hub took the worker's `joined` ack (`payload.joined_after`),
below the text and the calls the agent made before it saw the message, and never above its own
`seq`; the worker sends that ack after the session's own records written before it (§5.2), so
every event the agent made before it took the message is stored by then. Several taken behind
the same event keep their `seq` order. One with `during_text` is placed by `joined_after`, not
by the rule for such an input: it stands below the text it came during and the calls after it,
and the thinking or the text being written stands below it, since the agent took it before they
began. An ack lost while the worker was away (a restart of the hub, a dropped link) comes again
only after what the worker sends on reconnecting, so such a message then stands behind all of
