- Push: the hub POSTs to the subscription's `endpoint`, so only `https://` without
  userinfo and without a non-standard port on push service hosts is accepted: `fcm.googleapis.com`,
  `updates.push.services.mozilla.com`, `*.push.services.mozilla.com`, `*.push.apple.com`,
  `*.notify.windows.com`; redirects are not followed when sending.
- Access JWKS: keys are refreshed outside the cache lock, on a refresh error the previous set
  stays, retries with a growing pause (5 s … 5 min).
- Worker: `hub_url` is `https` only (§5.1), the agent's environment is an allowlist (§8.1) plus
  the `env` of its environment, whose values never leave the worker (§14), the outbox is a 0700
  directory, files 0600. The ssh key store `$HQC_HOME/keys/` is 0700 with 0600 files and the
  agent sockets live in `$HQC_HOME/agents/` (0700); wider modes, links or another owner stop the
  worker at start (since 0.57, T44); a process gets `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` only of its own ssh-agent,
  and only with `ssh_keys` (§14).
- Users' `api_keys` are encrypted with a master key from the hub's env.
- Cloudflare Tunnel: request body limit ~100 MB (matches the artifact limit),
  long-lived connections need heartbeats and reconnects.
- Backup: Postgres and the artifact store; workers' outboxes survive a hub restart.

## 21. Risks

- The Claude Code jsonl format and the stream-json/control protocol are unofficial; keep
  the parser and the adapter tolerant, cover them with fixtures, pin the CLI version.
- Takeover relies on the plugin and the CLI sharing the session file; if the plugin changes
  its storage, the mirror breaks.
- ACP in Hermes is stable, but the ACP v2 methods (`session/resume`, `session/fork`) are still
  a draft; the adapter sticks to v1 plus `session/load` and pins the Hermes commit hash
  (`4787e4d5` on llm-server).
- The boundary between sessions on one machine without a container is soft (§14); for
  ACP agents other than Hermes it is weaker still (§2.1).
- Agent→agent chains are bounded by timeouts and budgets, not by semantics; with
  abuse of `ask` money is spent up to the limit.

## 22. Prior art and borrowings

Checked on 2026-10-22.

- **Codync** (a Rust host on every machine, ACP to 40+ agents, SQLite, iPhone/Electron/TUI,
  Cloudflare relay with E2E). Closest in spirit: bots with a folder and a permission policy,
  group chats with @ and a limit of 3 rounds, a built-in `team` MCP for asking other
  bots. The architecture is the reverse of ours: many hosts, the client connects to each.
  No web or Android, no VS Code mirror, sharing, shared search or offline queue.
- **Paseo** (TS daemon, Expo clients, relay). More mature clients, no Hermes and no
  single hub over many machines.
- **Claude Code Remote Control**: official, Claude Code only, no projects
  and no Hermes.
- **CloudCLI / claudecodeui**: one machine, reads `~/.claude/projects`; the only
  one with a mirror of VS Code sessions.
- **Agent Host Protocol (Microsoft, MIT)**: a protocol for "a host between many clients
  and ACP agents": actions with `serverSeq`, reconnect by `lastSeenServerSeq`,
  write-ahead with an `origin` echo, "the first `toolCallConfirmed` wins", one turn
  per chat. That is exactly our §5–§6 and §17, but without workers, users, grants,
  agent→agent and storage. We do not take it whole; taken: the `client_op_id` echo (§6), the
  first-answer rule for approvals (§10.1), the action vocabulary for naming events.
  An AHP-compatible facade over `/api/ws` is possible later, if third-party clients appear.
- **OpenAB / OpenACP**: bridges from ACP agents to Discord, Telegram, Slack. A fallback UI:
  if the web client is delayed, a service bot in Telegram with forum topics covers
  notifications and approval answers. Not in scope.

### 22.1 Rejected alternative: no hub
The Codync model: every worker is a host itself, the client connects to all of them. Rejected
because `ask`/`send` between machines, shared history and search, sharing with colleagues,
the input queue for an offline worker and a single address for push need shared state;
without a hub each of these would have to be done peer-to-peer.

## 23. Change history

### 0.256 → 0.262 (iteration 9 planned: MCP servers on the machine)
§19: a new iteration 9, MCP servers that run on the machine, declared per environment in
`worker.toml` (the rest of #59); the generic ACP adapter becomes iteration 10, sharing 11, Tauri
12, and the references to them follow. Plan: `docs/ITERATION-9.md`. Found on 2.1.328:
`allow_local_mcp` gives the agent every server the machine's CLI knows, the account's `claude.ai`
connectors included; `--strict-mcp-config` gives none of them. 0.257–0.261 are left to the iOS
client (#171).

Implemented (T70–T71a): §14 `mcp_servers` per environment, checked at load, listed by
`hqc-worker env` and `env which` without values, with a warning on `allow_local_mcp`; §8.1 the
launcher `hqc-worker mcp --local <name>` in `--mcp-config`, `--strict-mcp-config` kept; the
daemon gives a server's spec (Vaultwarden values read then) only to a peer running the worker's
binary; a stdio program gets the child allowlist without `CLAUDE_*`/`ANTHROPIC_*` plus its own
`env`; `http` is relayed with its headers, no redirect followed; the tools pinned in
`$HQC_HOME/mcp-pins.json` unless `pin = false`, `hqc-worker mcp approve` and `mcp pins`; §4
`system mcp_server_failed` and `mcp_tools_changed`.

Implemented (T72, T73): §5.3 `hello.environments[].mcp_servers` (names only), kept by the hub
with the worker's environments (no migration: the column is the JSON of `hello`); §6
`GET /api/mcp/servers` `local[]`; the client's Settings → MCP servers "On machines" and the
project settings' local servers.

### 0.255 → 0.256 (a worker restart: waited for, and told to the agent)
#220: a worker restarted for an update killed a session's background subagents, and nothing told
the agent until the owner wrote again. §17.3: `SIGUSR1` makes the worker stop once no agent works
(at most 30 minutes), so an update waits for turns and background work; after a restart the hub
gives each agent that lost a turn, background work, a wakeup or a cron job a note of the owner
(`user.message.restart`, §4), and the agent goes on at once.

### 0.254 → 0.255 (quick messages for every project)
§3 User `quick_messages` (hub migration `0061_user_quick_messages`), §6 `GET`/`PATCH /api/me`
(`Me.quick_messages`, `PatchMe.quick_messages`; the whole list replaces the stored one, refused
as a project's list is, `400`, before anything of the request is stored), §6 client layout: the
user's own quick messages, edited in Settings after "New session" with the project editor, show in
every project's composer before the project's own (a text in both once); the list's last row links
to Settings and to the project's settings; opening the list re-reads `/api/me` too; the "In quick
messages" check of a message counts the user's list. "Add to quick messages" still adds to the
project's list.

### 0.253 → 0.254 (a button to the bottom of the chat)
§6: scrolled up through a long chat, the only way back to the newest text was to scroll all the
way down by hand. While the feed does not follow its bottom and the bottom is more than two of the
feed's windows down, a button in the middle of the feed's bottom edge now puts the feed at its
bottom, and the feed follows it again. Client only.

### 0.252 → 0.253 (a click on a quote goes to the text it quotes)
§6: the user's `>` lines (what Quote puts in) showed as typed, with nothing that led back to what
they quote. They now show as a quote block in the bubble, and a click on it, as in Telegram, takes
the chat to the quoted text and highlights it: the client looks for it by its letters and digits in
the session's events before the message (the older history loaded until it is found), then after it,
and jumps there as to a search hit. A search hit's jump now also takes the block that draws its
event (a call shown on its permission card), not the last block that starts before it. A swipe of
the user's message leaves out only these quote lines too, not every line that starts with `>`
(a `>>>` line the bubble shows as text is in the swiped quote, so the quote is found). Client only.

### 0.251 → 0.252 (a message swiped left is quoted)
§6: on a phone a message was quoted only by selecting its text and pressing Quote. Now a finger
that swipes a message left quotes its first two sentences, as Telegram does; the message follows
the finger, and a release past 60 px quotes it. Client only.

### 0.250 → 0.251 (a message taken into a turn the runtime began by itself joined it)
§17.2: while Claude Code ran a turn it began by itself (after a background task's notice), the
worker gave the owner's message as a turn of its own; the CLI took it into its running turn, and
the worker sent a plain `ack`. The hub kept no `joined_after`, and the feed showed the message where
it was sent, above the steps the agent made before it took it. The adapter now says whether it took
an input into a turn already running (`AdapterEvent::InputAccepted.joined`: the echo came during the
CLI's own turn), and the worker acks such an input `joined: true` when the hub honours `joined` on
it (a person's, a room's, a `send`, none a schedule's run); an `hqc_ask` or a schedule's run taken
so keeps its plain `ack`. The protocol, the
hub and the client are unchanged.

### 0.249 → 0.250 (a message taken into a turn that was lost is not left waiting at the bottom)
The runtime ran a turn by itself, took the owner's message into it (the worker had written it as
a turn: a plain `ack`, no `joined`) and its process died: `system turn_lost` names no input, so
the client counted the message as waiting through that turn, and as the next turn was another
message's, it and the message joined behind it stood queued under everything that came later,
for good. §6: when the first end after a delivered input is `turn_lost`, the input waited only if
it was delivered after it; delivered before, it stands at its own place, as in the turn it went
into. The hub's `waited_place` (the cut of a fork before such a message) follows the client.

### 0.248 → 0.249 (a sign-in proxy's redirect at sign-out wipes the device's copies)
§6: since 0.240 the client deletes the device's copies of a user when `/api/me` answers `401` or
`403`, but a sign-in proxy (Cloudflare Access, oauth2-proxy) answers a signed-out user with a
redirect to its sign-in page; `fetch` followed it, failed as offline, and the copies stayed. The
client now asks `/api/me` with `redirect: 'manual'` and takes a redirect for `401`. Client only.

### 0.247 → 0.248 (every capped input that waits at the owner's Stop is dropped)
§17.2: since 0.241 the owner's Stop drops an input of another session or a schedule's run capped
below the session's mode (T39), but writes one capped at or above that mode into the agent's
history; when the owner raised the mode to `allow_all` afterwards, the next turn found it there
unhandled in the higher mode. The worker now drops every input with a cap below `allow_all` at the
owner's Stop, with the same note to the agent, the owner's own message capped by the buffered
`send` messages in front of it (T40) included; the reason and the note no longer speak of the
session's mode. §7.1.1 follows. The protocol, the hub, the client and the macOS app are
unchanged.

### 0.245 → 0.246 (Auto on a provider; an MCP server's form answers kept out of the history; `sudo` over ssh)
#194: a session on a model provider in Auto had every call that needs Auto's safety check
refused by the CLI, since the check runs on Anthropic's servers and does not pass through a
provider; the agent spent its turns probing what still ran. §5.3: the worker runs such a session
in `ask` where `auto` is asked; §6: `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` with `permission_mode: auto` for a
session with a provider is `422 auto_needs_anthropic`; the client offers no Auto there and says
why. #129: §4 `clarify.response` of an MCP server's request is stored with `answers: {}`, and
the frame kept for the worker forgets the answers once acknowledged. #162: §14
`[environments.<name>.permissions] remote_unblock`, deny rules lifted only in the adapter's own
check and only for the command `ssh` sends to a named host, with options that run nothing locally.

### 0.244 → 0.245 (iteration 8: skills from the hub)
§19: a new iteration 8, skills the owner uploads once on the hub (#62); the generic ACP adapter
becomes iteration 9, sharing 10, Tauri 11, and the references to them follow. §5.3
`session.start.skills`, `GET /worker/skills/{sha256}`, §6 `/api/skills`, §8.1 `--plugin-dir`, §14
`hub_skills`, §20. A skill travels as names and hashes; the worker fetches each archive once per
hash, builds a plugin folder of its own (`hqc`) and starts the agent with `--plugin-dir`, the
hub's copy winning over a same-named skill of the machine (`skillOverrides`). A skill with
`hooks` is refused by the hub and the worker, since hooks run outside the worker's `deny`.
Migration `0058`.

### 0.243 → 0.244 (the agent is told of its background work that runs long)
A background command or subagent of the agent that ran for hours was known only to the rows above
the input: an agent whose build hung for 40 minutes was told nothing. §5.4, §8.1: the worker sends
the new `session.long_runs` when a background command or subagent of the agent has run for the
worker's new `long_run_note` and for each as long again, counted from its start, all the tasks due
on one tick in one frame, and the hub gives the agent a note naming each with its task id and run
time, as the owner's pending input, so that it checks the task and stops what hangs.
`long_run_note` (§14) is in seconds, 3300 (55 minutes) unless written, `0` for none; with the
1-hour prompt cache the default is below the hour the cache lives from the agent's last request,
so the turn of the note reads the cache and renews it for the next note; a value of an hour or
more makes it miss, and so does the 5-minute cache or a provider at any value. A Monitor, a task
held on the foreground of the turn and a subagent of a subagent that still runs are not watched;
a task first seen past a mark is not told of the marks it has passed. The task descriptions are
the model's words and go into the note as JSON strings, with the marks of a room's and another
session's lines escaped. §4: the hub is a source of `user.message` on that frame. A hub older
than 0.244 answers the frame with `invalid_frame`: update the hub before the workers. No
migration.

### 0.242 → 0.243 (a Vaultwarden secret as T3 Code's 1Password one, and a provider key from Vaultwarden)
§14, §5.3: a locked `rbw` is no longer refused: `rbw list` unlocks it, `rbw-agent` asking for the
master password through the `pinentry` of that machine, so a Touch ID pinentry with a short
`lock_timeout` asks again once the vault locked, as T3 Code's `op` does through the 1Password app
(an agent's own use of `rbw` there restarts that timeout, §14); the owner is
told when it stays locked or is not answered in time, and the card stays open. The reads of a
worker run one at a time, so concurrent ones wait for one prompt; a read's `rbw` calls and that
wait fit in 25 s (was 15 s), inside the hub's 30 s. Any field of the entry can be read, not only
the password: `vault_field` (`hqc_secret`, `secret.put`, `POST /api/sessions/{id}/secrets`, the
card's `secret.vault_field`) names it, and the worker reads `rbw get --raw` and picks the field by
its exact name, as `rbw get --field` matches a custom field by a substring. An entry of type "SSH
key" is given only as `kind: ssh_key`, with a field or without. §3, §4, §6: every `hqc_secret` card
of a worker that reads Vaultwarden and its fields carries `secret.reads_vault` and has "Vaultwarden | Type it",
opening on Vaultwarden only when the agent named an entry, with an optional "Field". §14, §8.1:
the `api_key` of a `[providers.<name>]` in `worker.toml` may be `{ vault, field? }`, read with
`rbw` at every start of the agent into that process only, as T3 Code reads a credential reference
when a provider starts; a key that cannot be read fails that start, naming the provider, and not
retryably (the hub's three retries would stack the prompts a locked `rbw` leaves open). No hub
migration. §5.4: such a worker sends `vault_fields: true`; one before 0.243 would ignore
`vault_field` and give the password, so the hub puts the field and `reads_vault` on a card, and
takes `vault_field`, only for a worker that sends it (else `409 unavailable`).

### 0.241 → 0.242 (every key in Settings; the macOS app keeps only its global shortcut)
§6, the Settings page: the keys of the client — Quote and Search of selected text (0.238), the
project search, the session column — were fixed, and the macOS app had its own shortcuts in its
own Settings for a new session, archiving the open session, the previous and the next session and
project, Back and Forward, which it ran by clicking the page and which a browser did not have. Now
the client has all of them: a "Keys" section of Settings records each anew, puts it back to its
default or clears it, kept on the device, and the client does the actions itself, in a browser
too (where ⌘N and Ctrl+N stay the browser's). The macOS app keeps only the global shortcut of New
Session in Project; its File and Go menu items stay, without keys. The hub goes first: a client
before 0.242 has none of these keys, and the new app no longer takes them. The hub's server and
the worker are unchanged.

### 0.240 → 0.241 (a capped input that waits at the owner's Stop is dropped, and the agent told so)
§17.2: since 0.231 the owner's Stop writes what waited into the agent's history without a turn,
an input of another session or a schedule's run capped below the session's mode (T39) included;
the next turn, in the full mode, found it there unhandled. The worker now fails such an input, not
retryable, and writes in its place a quiet note that names what was dropped (the sending session,
a scheduled message, a message), not its text. §7.1: an ask whose input fails for good (the worker
refuses it, the agent does not start, the session continues in VS Code or is archived) fails at
once with the reason instead of at its timeout. §7.1.1: such a failure of a room's input whose
message is older than the room's last Stop adds no line and ends no round. The protocol, the
client and the macOS app are unchanged.

### 0.239 → 0.240 (the device's copies are cleaned up)
§6, §12, the Settings page: the copies of the history and of attachments that the client keeps on
the device since 0.220 only grew, and stayed after the user signed out. Now both databases of a user
are deleted when the hub answers `/api/me` with `401` or `403`, when another user signs in on the
device, and by "Forget this device" in Settings; at most once an hour the client deletes the copies
of sessions the hub no longer lists, those not used for 30 days, and the least recently used beyond
200 MB. The artifacts database is at version 2, with a store `used` (the last use and size of each
blob); a history range carries `used_at` and `bytes`. Client only.

### 0.238 → 0.239 (a call whose request id is taken ends at once; a `joined_after` that is no integer)
§3 PendingRequest: since 0.225 the hub opens no request whose `request_id` an open request of
another kind of the session holds, but `hqc_publish`, `hqc_move` and `hqc_secret` took the refusal
for a repeat and their call got no result until its timeout, and `hqc_ask` stored and delivered its
message and then opened no request, so no reply could reach it. Such a call is now answered at once
with `unavailable`, the ask before its message is stored; a worker's own request refused this way
is refused to the worker. §6 fork: the fork read `payload.joined_after` of every event with a
bigint cast, and a worker's event payload is stored as sent, so a string or a fraction there made
every fork of the session fail; a value that is not a non-negative JSON integer of at most 18
digits (every `seq` is one) now counts as none. The clients, the worker and the macOS app are unchanged.

### 0.237 → 0.238 (keys for Quote and Search of selected text)
§6: Quote and "Search in …" of text selected in the feed had no keys, only the button over the
input and the menu of a right click. ⌘' (Ctrl+' off a Mac) quotes the selection as the button
does, where there is an input; ⌘E (Ctrl+E) searches it in a new tab. They are taken only while
the chat holds a selection that starts in the feed or in a subagent's history; without one, with
Shift or Alt held, or Ctrl on a Mac, the key stays the browser's. The keys go by the key's place,
not its letter, so they work in any layout. The Quote button's tooltip and the menu's Quote and
Search name them.

### 0.236 → 0.237 (the schedules in the block above the input)
§6, §16: the session's schedules opened in a panel under the chat's header, with its own heading,
Close, and Pause and Delete buttons unlike anything in the block above the input, though their
"Scheduled:" lines stand in that block. The panel is gone: a "Scheduled:" line, as the task list's
row, opens the list under it in the block, a line per schedule with small pause or resume and
delete buttons and the whole message under it; the "More" menu's "Schedules" opens the same list.
It is read again whenever `schedules.live` comes, so a sent one-off shows as sent. Only the client.

### 0.235 → 0.236 (a provider and an MCP server filled from their URL)
§5.3 `provider.probe`, §6 `POST /api/providers/probe`, `POST /api/mcp/probe`. Adding a model
provider asked for its name, model and context window, and an MCP server for its name and how it
signs in, which the endpoint itself can tell. Both forms start with the URL; the hub probes it (a
provider through a worker, which reaches the owner's network) and fills the rest while the owner
has not edited it; every field stays visible and editable.

### 0.234 → 0.235 (iteration 7: remote MCP servers relayed by the hub)
§19: a new iteration 7, remote MCP servers the owner adds once on the hub (#59); the generic ACP
adapter becomes iteration 8, sharing 9, Tauri 10, and the references to them follow. §5.3
`session.start.mcp_servers`, §5.4 `mcp.upstream`, §6 `/api/mcp/servers`, §14 `hub_mcp`, §20.
A server's address and token stay on the hub: the worker gives the CLI a stdio relay per server
under the server's own name (`mcp__<name>__<tool>`), and the hub makes the calls, one MCP session
per hqc session and server, a large result as an artifact, a timeout per server. Migration
`0057`. OAuth sign-in (T65) and the client's screens (T66).

### 0.233 → 0.234 (one Quote button over the input, Copy alone on a message)
§6: a message's buttons were Search, Copy and Quote: Search worked on the selection inside that
message (hidden without one), Quote on it, else on the message's first two sentences; the Quote
pop-up was awkward, the menu of a right click a click more, and the buttons at the message's bottom
right had to be reached in a long message. Search and Quote are gone from the messages: their strip
is Copy (which now copies the whole message, never the selection) and, on the user's own message,
Take back, Send now, Add to quick messages and Fork; a press on the strip no longer takes the focus
from the input. "Quote" is one button, the word itself, over the right end of the input's field
(left of send, taking no room: the field, its wraps and the feed do not move when it comes and
goes), shown while the chat holds a selection that starts in the feed or in a subagent's history,
where there is an input, and it needs a selection; a press appends the selection to the draft as
`> ` lines. The chat follows the selection cheaply (a copy of its range; its text is read at the
press, or from that copy when the press cleared the selection) and renders only when a quotable
selection comes or goes. A range that ends outside the feed it starts in (a triple click on the
last paragraph of the last message ends past it) is cut at the feed's end, for the right-click
menu (Quote, Copy, Search in …), which is otherwise as it was, too. A range that starts in the
line a folded reasoning shows begins with its selected part of that line, as the old Quote of that
reasoning had it; one that only passes through the reasoning leaves the line out, as before.

### 0.232 → 0.233 (a compaction before a waiting input is shown)
§6, §17.1: with the context past its threshold Claude Code runs an auto-compaction before it takes
the next input and echoes that input only after it, so for the whole compaction (93 s on a live
session) the input stayed pending, no turn was open, the session was `queued`, and the main
agent's row said "Input queued" whatever the worker reported. The worker and the hub already
passed "compacting" on; the client dropped it in `queued`. Now an `activity` stands in place of
"Input queued", the row drawn as a running one: "Main agent: Compacting the conversation…". Only
the client changed.

### 0.231 → 0.232 (a side question to a session's agent)
§4: the events `side.question` (the hub's, the owner's) and `side.answer` (the adapter's); §5.3:
`session.side_question`; §6: `POST /api/sessions/{id}/side_question`; §8.1: the `side_question`
control request, which Claude Code answers outside the conversation, without a turn and without a
trace in the agent's context; §17.5: behaviour. `/btw <question>` or `/side <question>` in the
composer asks it, the question and the answer stand as one muted block in the feed, and it
works for an unloaded agent, which the hub starts first, with `session.start.no_wait`: with all
slots busy the session does not queue, the start's settings are kept for the next start, and
the question gets an error. A question the worker answers with an `error` frame, or whose
connection closes before the answer (it drops or a new `hello` replaces it), gets that error as
its `side.answer`. The hub stores only one `side.answer` per question, of a question of the same
session. A question during the agent's text stands under it like a message (`during_text`). A
refused question comes back into the composer. `hqc_read` leaves side events out. Its API cost
is added to the process's running total, so the next turn of the same process shows it, in its
cost and in `session_tokens`. The question reads the conversation's prompt cache and so renews
it, which the header's cache time does not see.
A `model_refusal_fallback` of `scope` `local` no longer retracts events of the conversation.

### 0.230 → 0.231 (the owner's Stop sends what waited without a turn)
§4, §5.2, §5.3, §6, §7.1, §8.1, §17.2: a Stop used to leave the messages that waited to chance: the
CLI cancelled the ones written into the turn and they failed, the worker's queue ran after the Stop
as if nothing had happened. Now the owner's own Stop is "stop the turn, send everything that waited,
stop again". `session.stop` gets `quiet` (omitted when false); the hub sets it in the owner's Stop
route and in a room's Stop, never in a pause's stop, which keeps the waiting messages for the
resume. A worker older than 0.231 ignores the field and stops as before, and only a hub of 0.231
makes a worker send `ack {quiet}`, so the workers need not be updated after the hub. With a turn
running (the runtime's own included) a `quiet` stop sends a `cancel_async_message` for each line of
hqc's the CLI has not taken, then the plain `interrupt` (`cancel_queued` would also dequeue the
CLI's own lines that carry no `uuid`: task notifications, cron, `/loop`), and marks the inputs the
worker holds; when the stopped turn ends it marks the inputs the runtime dropped from it, and writes
the marked ones into the agent's history as quiet lines (`shouldQuery: false`, which Claude Code
records without calling the model), in the hub's creation order (`event_id`), so the agent knows
what was written and does not act on it. Until that end nothing new goes into the turn, and what
comes after the Stop is never marked, so Clear goal (a Stop, then `/goal clear`) still runs `/goal
clear`. A slash command that waited, judged by the text the runtime gets, fails ("cancelled by
Stop"). A Stop with no turn running and a stop without `quiet` mark nothing. The engine takes each
quiet line by the `result` that lists it in `user_message_uuids` (the CLI takes lines written back
to back together: one `result` for several), with one adapter event and no turn, status, `usage` or
end of turn. The worker acks each input with the new `ack {quiet: true}`; the idle unload and a move
wait for those acks, and a quiet line the CLI drops (on 2.1.312 it answers `cancelled` for a line it
failed to process) or a process that ends first (not through `session.kill`) is written again. The
quiet line carries `priority: "later"`: the CLI folds a line of priority "next" or above into a turn
that runs, whatever its `shouldQuery`, a turn it started by itself included, so a "later" line never
joins one and is taken once the CLI is idle, and the worker writes it at once. A normal input
written while quiet lines wait would run before them (the CLI dequeues "next" before "later"), so
the worker hands none until their acks. A Stop never cancels a quiet line. On the `ack {quiet}` the
hub also writes `payload.joined_after` (0.221), so the feed stands a quiet message where Claude Code
recorded it: behind the stopped turn, or behind a turn the CLI ran by itself before it took the
line. The hub marks such an input delivered, keeps `payload.quiet` on it and tells clients with the
`delivery` frame (never as waiting), opens no turn for it, fails an `hqc_ask` it carried ("<address>
was stopped before it took the question"), and lets a room go on as for a joined input. Send now
does not pass the hold of the stopped turn (`not_now`). A `cancelled` for the turn's own first line
that a Stop's cancel reached before the CLI started it (no `result` follows) makes it come back
dropped, and so quiet, except in a turn the runtime started by itself. Take back of a marked input
in the worker's queue leaves it, and of one the CLI already cancelled is answered at once; neither
is written quiet; one already written as a quiet line is `409 already_taken`. A `session.kill` is
not held for the acks: a kill or a worker restart at any time between the Stop and the acks (during
the stopped turn, and while quiet lines wait behind a turn the CLI started by itself) drops the
marked inputs at the worker, and the hub, which holds them pending, sends them to the next process
as plain inputs, which run as before 0.231 (§17.2). A Stop no longer leaves its flag set when no
turn runs or its process ends, which made the end of a later turn treat its dropped inputs as
cancelled. A fork's copy leaves out a message written quiet whose `joined_after` is not below the
`seq` of the record where the copy's conversation is cut (Claude Code recorded it after that record,
so the copied agent never got it); a fork of a copy reads the copy's own `joined_after`.

### 0.229 → 0.230 (a chat catching up draws a few times, the client socket compressed, one session fetched instead of the list)
§6: a chat opened after a long absence took long to show the events it had missed: the hub sent
them at once, but the client drew the chat for each frame. On a chat of 28 000 events with 3000
missed, reopening drew 3000 times and took 2.7 to 6.1 s before this change; with it, it draws 5 to
18 times and takes 0.6 to 2.0 s, about as long as the hub takes to send them (six runs each,
Brave, live hub). The client now applies the events of a subscription without drawing until the
hub's `subscribed` (and again after a socket reset, which subscribes with a backfill), and draws
at most every 100 ms meanwhile, so a long backfill shows as it arrives. A `subscribed` of a
subscription that was left and made again meanwhile (the hub answers each `subscribe`, a refused
one with an `error` naming the session) does not end the new catch-up: the socket counts the
`subscribe` frames it sent and the answers it got. So that an error naming a session answers only
a refused `subscribe`, a failed backfill (on a `subscribe`, on a gap in the live stream, or after
the hub's bus overflowed) now sends its `error` without `session_id`; the hub logs the session. An open chat also builds its
feed only when what it is built from changed: the timeline's `revision` grows with a stored event
(new or changed), the thinking being written, an invalid event and a message not stored yet, and
not with the answer's text, `subagents.live` or `schedules.live`, which the feed does not read;
each hub `session.summary` (1.5 to 3 a second) and each delta of the text redrew the chat and
built the feed again without a change in it. `Timeline.items()` is kept per `revision`.

§6: on a narrow channel the page paid for every byte of `/api/ws`: tungstenite, under axum's
WebSocket, has no permessage-deflate, so the hub answered the upgrade without
`Sec-WebSocket-Extensions` and sent plain text. Measured on the live hub with raw DEFLATE: the full
`summary` 479 KB → 102 KB; a catch-up of 3000 `event` frames 2690 KB → 1498 KB when each frame is
compressed alone, 686 KB when they are one stream, which is why there is one stream per
connection. `/api/ws?deflate=raw` now asks for that stream (the hub uses `flate2` with the
`zlib-rs` backend `zip` already brings, at level 2: level 1 there uses fixed Huffman codes only and
compressed a synthetic summary to 178 KB against 127 KB at level 2, for the same CPU): every frame
goes out as a binary message, its JSON and `\n` compressed and sync-flushed, without it the frames
are text as before. The client asks when `DecompressionStream('deflate-raw')` exists, inflates the
messages in order through one stream, takes each line as a frame, and reconnects when the stream
breaks. The frames reach the listeners a few microtasks after the message, and not at all when the
socket was replaced meanwhile; the client resubscribes from the last `seq` it has seen, so nothing
is lost. The macOS app's page script read only text frames of a socket whose address ends in
`/api/ws`, so on a compressed socket the app would have shown no notification, no Dock badge and
no window bar; it now finds the socket by its path and inflates its binary messages on a stream of
its own. An HQC.app built before 0.230 reads no frame of a hub that serves this client (no
notifications, Dock badge or window bar, and answered permission cards stay): rebuild the app when
the hub is updated. Also §6: a summary of an unknown session in a known project fetched `GET /api/sessions`,
2.2 MB of JSON (243 KB gzipped by the proxy in front), to add one session; the client now fetches
that session when one session's frame names it; the `summary` of every session, sent on each
(re)subscribe, still fetches the lists, as it may name many. What the lists did besides adding it
is not done then: a session deleted elsewhere stays on the page until the next list.

### 0.228 → 0.229 (the session's tokens next to its cost in the chat header)
§4, §6, §8.1: the header showed only the session's cost. The worker now sends the runtime's
running token total on `usage` as `session_tokens` (the sum of the cumulative `modelUsage` token
counts of the `result`, input, output, cache reads and cache writes, carried over `--resume` and
reset by `/clear` like the cost), and the header shows it after the cost, "$2.25 · 3.4M tokens
this session" (a room sums its agents'; a session on a provider shows its tokens, not its made-up
cost). A session whose last `usage` came from an older worker shows no tokens until its next turn.

### 0.227 → 0.228 (a message's buttons at its bottom right, and the right-click menu again)
§6: a message's buttons (Search, Copy, Quote; on the user's message also Add to quick messages,
Fork, Take back, Send now) stood left of its time at the right end of its first line, except a
phone's agent message with a usage line, which had them at that line's end: a long message had to
be scrolled back up to reach them. They now stand at the message's bottom right, on a computer and
a phone alike: at the right end of an agent message's usage line and of the bottom line of "Reply
to"; else floated right at the end of the text's last line, on that line while it has room, on a
line of their own under it when it has none and after a text that ends in a code block, a table, a
rule, a quote or a formula. A message from another session and a room post no longer have them in
their head; an open reasoning has them at the end of its text (a folded one, in its summary line as
before); a message with no text keeps them left of its time. A user's text and a reasoning are shown
without their trailing line breaks. On a computer a right click on text selected in the feed or in a
subagent's history gives the client's menu again (Quote where there is an input, Copy, "Search in
…"), for the selection as it was at the press: a click outside it (which a Mac's browser answers by
selecting the word under the pointer) and a click with nothing selected give the browser's menu, a
click inside a selection that WebKit off a Mac cleared on the press selects it again; a selection
across messages is taken whole, without their times, heads and the hidden text of folded blocks.

### 0.226 → 0.227 (the thinking estimate runs up between reports)
§17.1: "Thinking · ~N tokens" in the main agent's row changed in steps: the worker reports a new
estimate at most once per 2 s, and the client drew each as it came, in whole thousands from 10k
up, so the count stood still for seconds. The VS Code tab runs its own count up to each new
estimate over the time since the one before; the client now does the same (0.3–3 s, redrawn every
100 ms; the first estimate and a smaller one shown at once) and writes it with two decimals from
1k up and without the "~", "Thinking · 12.34k tokens". Only the client changed.

### 0.225 → 0.226 (the publication card: secrets capped, hidden files named, no link into `.git`)
§7, §20: the owner's card of an `hqc_publish` listed every name that looks like a secret in the
archive's order with no cap, so a hundred `a0001.key` pushed an `id_rsa` far down the card and off
the few lines of the macOS app's notification; it showed a hidden folder as one line with its
count, so `.kube/config`, `.aws/config` or `.docker/config.json` went unnamed. The secrets now
come at most 20, the first file of each glob, then the second of each, and so on; every hidden file
is named by its full path, at most 20, the same way round the hidden folders; the rest is counted
in "and N more". More names look like a secret: `*.ppk`, `*.jks`, `*.keystore`, `*.kdbx`,
`*.gpg`, `.netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.git-credentials`, `secrets.*`, `service-account*.json`. The
worker packed a link inside the folder that resolves into `.git` (`repo -> .git`) as `repo/…`;
an entry whose canonical path has a `.git` or `.hqc` component below the folder is now left out.

### 0.224 → 0.225 (a request's id is its session's alone while it is open)
§3 PendingRequest: an answer names its request by the id alone, and the hub looked it up across
kinds; a worker could open an `approval` with the `request_id` of a publication or a move waiting
for the owner, and the owner's Allow on that card could land on the publication instead, as the
owner's own `once` with the `allowed_by` mark. The hub now opens no request whose `request_id` an
open request of another kind of the same session has (the check and the insert under one lock),
and a worker's `approval.request` and `clarify.request` open their row before they are stored,
so one refused is not stored and shows no card. A repeat of the same request after a reconnect is
stored as before. The clients and the macOS app are unchanged.

### 0.223 → 0.224 (no whole-server answer for an ambiguous name; only an offered option)
§8.1, §10.1: the card of an MCP tool offered "all tools of this server" for any tool name, and
the server is the part before the next `__`, as Claude Code reads it; for a server whose name
starts or ends with `_` or has `__` that part is another server's name (`mcp__hqc___x` of a
server `hqc_` reads as `hqc`), so "Allow all hqc tools" stored `mcp__hqc` and allowed the real
`hqc` too. The worker now offers neither answer for a name another server's tool could share
(the tool part starts with `_` or has `__`; as a precaution also a server part that starts or
ends with `_`), and the hub stores no folder rule for `server_always` on one. A rule made from a
card of the real `hqc` still covers `hqc_`, as Claude Code's own does. The worker also took any
option it knows as the answer: `server_session` and `server_always` on a card that offered
neither, `session` on a request only a person may answer, `always` in restricted mode (as
`session`). It now keeps the ids of the options the card offered and refuses any other; the hub
already refused an option that is not in the request it stores.

### 0.222 → 0.223 (the agent's task list above the input)
Backlog item "the agent's task list as a pinned block". §4: a stored event `tasks`
`{items[{subject, status, active_form?}]}`, the whole list after each change, written by the
Claude Code adapter. §8.1: the adapter follows the main agent's `TodoWrite`, `TaskCreate`,
`TaskUpdate` and `TaskList` calls through their results, sends `tasks` only when the list
changed, and `/clear` empties it, and a resumed process starts with the list its transcript makes
(a fork starts empty, as the CLI's). A `tasks` event is cut at 200 tasks of 512 bytes; the hub
indexes the type (migration `0056_events_tasks`); an unknown `status` is tolerated; the adapter
takes the id and subject of a task from the CLI's result text, after the CLI corrected the call.
§14: the worker's `task_tools = true` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` for its agents;
without it CLI 2.1.312 gives the 5.x models no task tools (the older models of its list have them
regardless). §6: "Tasks: 3 of 7 completed" is a row of the block above the input while a task is
not completed, after the goal's row (0.218) and before the main agent's; a press opens the list
with a mark per task, the client keeps the event of the highest `seq` and it is no feed item; on
subscribe the hub also sends the session's latest `tasks` event when it is older than
`after_seq`, so a client that loaded only the newest page has the list.

### 0.221 → 0.222 (the context and the prompt cache in the chat header)
§4 `usage`, §6 chat header, §8.1: the header said what a session cost but not how close its
context is to the auto-compaction, nor how long Claude's prompt cache of the session still lives
(a message after it ends reads the whole context again at the full price). A `usage` that carries
tokens now has `context_tokens`, `context_limit` and `cache_ttl_s`, built by the Claude Code
adapter from the stream: the usage of the main agent's last API response, the model's window in
`result.modelUsage` less the output reserve and the CLI's margin, and the TTL of the cache writes
seen (an hour or five minutes) less the seconds since the response started; after a compaction the
size is the boundary's `post_tokens` until the next response. The limit is the model window's
threshold: an overridden auto-compaction window or a disabled one is not seen. The item is left
out of a room and of a session VS Code holds. The meta row shows "<n>% context" and, while the
session is not Running and not on a provider, " · cache m:ss" counted down, "cache expired" after
the end, on a computer after the cost and on a phone in the state's line; `/clear` empties both.
Like the goal's row, the item comes from the loaded history (0.220). Worker, protocol and client;
the new fields are optional, so an older worker's `usage` shows nothing.

### 0.220 → 0.221 (an input the agent took after its calls stands where it took it)
§4, §6, §17.2: a message typed during a turn that the CLI took only after the running tool call's
result (`joined`) stood at its own `seq`, above the whole turn: above the text and the calls the
agent made before it ever saw the message. The hub now keeps where it was taken: when it honours
the worker's `joined` ack it writes `payload.joined_after`, the `seq` of the last event of the
session that is no input, in the same update, and sends it in the `delivery` frame. The worker
sends that ack after the session's own records written before it, and the hub handles a worker
connection's frames one after another, so every event the agent made before it took the message
is stored by then; the agent events' `ts` is the worker's clock and `delivered_at` the hub's, so
the client cannot compare them. The client moves such a message down to right behind that event
(never up, several behind the same one in `seq` order); one with `during_text` is placed by
`joined_after` too, below the text it came during, and the text or the thinking being written
stands below it. A fork before it cuts at the last `agent.message` up to that event, and a fork's
copy carries `joined_after` into the copy's own `seq`. An ack lost while the worker was away
comes after what the worker sends on reconnecting: the message then stands behind all of that, a
limitation. A message joined before has no `joined_after` and stands as before.

### 0.219 → 0.220 (history and attachments kept on the device, the older history on demand)
§6, §12, §15, §17.2: each open of a chat downloaded its newest page and then the whole older
history again, and each view of an image after its link had expired (10 minutes) downloaded the
image again; on a slow link a long chat took long to open. The client now keeps on the device
(IndexedDB, a database per user) what it received of each session's history, the records of
attachments and the bytes it downloads to show them; a chat opens on its copy, takes the hub's
newest page to check and extend it, and drops the copy when that page does not continue it. The
older history loads a page at a time when the user scrolls to its top, down to a search hit, and
by itself only for the header's cost (a `usage` within the last 1000 events) and the cards of
open requests. An image in the feed is a `data:` URL of its kept bytes, loaded when it comes near
the window; its `<img>` no longer renews a link. A `/clear` older than the loaded history adds the
cost before it to the header only once its line is loaded, and a goal whose last event is older
than the loaded history shows its row only then too. A take-back (0.219) in a chat shown from its
copy waits for that page, which would show the message waiting again, and writes `withdrawn` into
the copy itself; the files it puts back into the input are not kept on the device.

### 0.218 → 0.219 (take a waiting message back, or send it now)
§3 Event, §5.3, §6, §8.1, §17.2: a message of the owner's that waits for the agent shows two buttons,
Take back and (while a turn runs) Send now. Take back withdraws it (`delivery: withdrawn`, a new
value): the hub drops it, a worker that holds it takes it out of its queue or has Claude Code drop
the line with `cancel_async_message`, an agent that has taken it already makes it `409
already_taken`; `hqc_read`, a fork's copy and the search leave it out, the feed pages and a
subscription's backlog return it as `withdrawn` and the client hides it, and puts its text and
files back into the input. Send now writes it
into the running turn with `priority: "now"`, which makes Claude Code move the running Bash, MCP
call or subagent to the background and take the message into the same turn. New frames
`session.withdraw` and `session.input_now`, answered with `result {withdrawn}` / `{sent_now}`
(`error not_now` for a turn that cannot take input), routes `POST .../inputs/{event_id}/withdraw`
and `.../now`; an input the owner typed is written to the CLI with `origin: {kind: "human"}`, which a
message of another session, a room's input, a run of a schedule and a note of the hub's own do not
carry: the hub marks the owner's `user.message` `payload.human` in its input route alone and sets
`session.input.human` from it, unless a peer header, a room's rewrite or buffered `send` messages
make the input something else; Take back and Send now are for such messages only. A worker keeps an
input across a reconnect, so the hub marks `events.handed_at` (migration `0055`) before each
`session.input` and withdraws on its own word only an input never handed; one handed is asked about
at its worker's connection whatever the session's start state (a worker that was killed or paused
holds nothing and says so), with no connection it is `409 worker_offline`; while the question is
open the connection's `withdrawing` keeps the message from being handed and refuses a second
take-back (`409 withdrawing`); the answer is settled also when the owner's request is gone. A
withdrawn input is never sent; a client whose take-back got `409 withdrawn` puts the text back. Two
limitations (§6): a worker's answer after `504 worker_timeout` is dropped, and a message the worker
dropped meanwhile stays queued until the owner takes it back again, the worker reconnects or the
agent's process restarts; a take-back whose `200` the client lost hides the message without
putting its text back. A worker's `error` for the two frames is `502` with its own code. When the
CLI does not answer a cancel in time the input is a written one again, and a session that waited
for a slot for a withdrawn input leaves the line. Hub, worker, protocol and client.

### 0.217 → 0.218 (the agent's goal: a row above the input, its checks in the feed)
§4, §6, §8.1: Claude Code's `/goal <condition>` already reached the CLI, which keeps the agent at
work until a model of its own finds the condition met, but hqc showed nothing of it: the CLI streams
none of the goal's progress and writes it only to the transcript. The adapter now reads those
records and sends each as `system goal`, a check after the text it judged, and the mirror maps the
same records for a session the worker's own process does not run; the client draws the checks as
lines as Claude Code's own UI does ("Goal achieved (55s · 3 checks · 918 tokens)", "Goal not yet
met… continuing", "Goal could not be achieved" with the reason) and, while the goal is set, a row
first above the input with the condition, the number of unmet checks, the last one's reason, and
"Clear goal", which stops a running turn before it sends `/goal clear`. The CLI's reply to a local
slash command, which the adapter sent as a `runtime` message drawn in red as an error, is `system
command_output`, as the mirror's already was.
### 0.216 → 0.217 (the card names the ask rule behind it)
§8.1, §4: a card that a `permissions.ask` rule raised said nothing of why, also in Allow all,
where such a rule still asks: Claude Code sends no `decision_reason` for a rule, only
`decision_reason_type: "rule"` and the rule's source (2.1.329). The adapter now writes `reason`
itself, "An ask rule for Artifact in user settings (~/.claude/settings.json) requires approval
for this call", naming the rule when `matched_ask_rule` comes; the client already shows
`reason` under the card's title.

### 0.215 → 0.216 (a secret from Vaultwarden)
§14: `vault = true` in `worker.toml` (with `session_secrets`) lets an `hqc_secret` card take the
secret from a Vaultwarden (Bitwarden) entry instead of a typed value, as T3 Code's card takes a
1Password reference: the worker reads it with `rbw` on its own machine, as T3 Code reads
1Password with `op` on the agent's machine, so the value passes neither the client nor the hub.
The entry is the one named exactly (found by its id first, since `rbw get` alone also takes a
partial name), an entry of Bitwarden's type "SSH key" gives its private key, and every `rbw`
call of a read fits in 15 s.
§7: `hqc_secret` takes `vault`, the entry the agent names; §3, §4: the card carries it as
`secret.vault`, only for a worker that reads Vaultwarden. §6: the card opens on the entry, which
the owner confirms or changes, or switches to typing the value; `POST
/api/sessions/{id}/secrets` takes `vault` in place of `value`, and the feed line names the entry.
§5.3: `secret.put.vault`; §5.4: `hello.capabilities.vault`, so no hub migration.
### 0.214 → 0.215 (.git and .hqc are never published; the card names secrets first)
§7, §20: the card of a publication could understate what goes public: it named the first 50
files that are not hidden, so an `id_rsa` or a `credentials.json` past them was only in "and N
more", and showed a hidden folder as one line, so a token in `.git/config` went unseen. The
worker no longer packs an entry named `.git` or `.hqc`, at any depth inside a published folder
(the published path itself is not checked); the tool's description says so. The card always
names a file whose last component looks like a secret (`.env*`, `credentials*`, `id_rsa*`,
`id_dsa*`, `id_ecdsa*`, `id_ed25519*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, any case), also past
the first 50 and inside a hidden folder, and lists the files in three groups, each in the
archive's order: the secrets, the other hidden files and the hidden folders, the first 50
others. The macOS app's notification of a publication keeps this order instead of putting the
hidden lines first.

### 0.213 → 0.214 (a move or a publication after a restart only on the owner's mark)
§3 `move`, `publish`: a hub that stopped while it carried out an allowed move or publication
took, on start, any `approval.response` of the session with the call's `request_id` and `once`
as the owner's leave, the hub's own `by: auto` included; a worker that reused the call's request
id for an approval of its own and then cancelled the call had it carried out at the next start.
The owner's `once` now closes the row and puts `allowed_by` (the owner's id) into its `payload`
in one update, and only rows with the mark are carried out after a restart; the feed is not
consulted. A row an older hub closed allowed has no mark and is not carried out after the
upgrade.

### 0.212 → 0.213 (all tools of an MCP server in one answer)
§10.1, §8.1, §4: the card of an MCP tool call offers "Allow all <server> tools for this session"
(`server_session`) and "Always allow all <server> tools in this folder" (`server_always`, which the
hub turns into the folder rule `mcp__<server>` before it forwards the answer); until now the answer
`session` held only for the exact tool, so every other tool of the server asked again. The folder
rule is the one the rules screen already lists, so a later server-wide setting on the hub replaces
it without a change here. §10.1, §14: a tool name in a rule (hqc's and the worker's
`[permissions]`) may have `-`: Claude Code's server names are letters, digits, `_` and `-`
(`claude-in-chrome`), and until now no rule could name such a server. The hub has to be updated
before the workers: an older client labels both answers by their canonical, as "Always in this
session" and "Always allow", and an older hub stores no folder rule for `server_always`.

### 0.211 → 0.212 (Pause while a subagent works after the turn)
§6 client layout: Pause was offered for `running`, `waiting` and `queued` only, so a session
whose turn had ended while its background subagent or task still worked, which the header and
its row show as Running, had neither Pause nor Stop. Pause is now offered there too, in the
header and in the row's menu; it ends the agent's process and that work with it, as a pause of
an idle agent always did (§17.3). Stop stays hidden there: it stops a turn, and a background
subagent or task goes on after it (§8.1); a subagent and a background command have their own
stop on their line above the input. Client only.

### 0.210 → 0.211 (the favorites scroll with the session list)
§6 client layout: a project's favorites were a block pinned over its session list, on a phone
and in the Spacious look at most half of the column, scrolling inside it; a favorite past the
block's fold was out of sight, a session that waits for the user among them while the project
showed it waiting. The Favorites group now stands in the list's one scroll, on a desktop and a
phone alike, first but for a new session's "Draft", which stays above it so that its current
row is in sight however many favorites there are. On a desktop the column is not mounted again
for another project and kept the scroll of the one left, which now would hide the favorites:
another project's list opens at its top.

### 0.209 → 0.210 (the header's Pause says the pause is at once)
§6 client layout: the header's Pause came with 0.206 in the words of the pause before 0.191,
"Pause after this turn" on a phone and "The agent stops when this turn ends; messages wait for
Resume" as the tooltip on a computer, while since 0.191 a pause stops a running turn at once.
They are now "Pause session" and "The agent stops now; messages wait for Resume". The 0.206
record said "More" held Pause before it; it held, besides Schedules and Move to project…, the
mode, the model, Rename and the browser, Pause was only in the row's menu, and Folder rules and
Restart session came into "More" with 0.206. Client only.

### 0.208 → 0.209 (publish a page or a file at a public link)
§7, §7.2: the tool `hqc_publish(path, caption?)` (issue #7). The worker packs a folder with
`index.html`, or one file, into a deterministic zip, every entry inside the folder and
`allowed_roots` (a link pointing out is refused by its name), and uploads it as an artifact of the
new kind `site`; the hub opens it with limits and always asks the session owner with a card in
the session's own chat ("Publish" / "Deny"), whatever the session's mode and `auto_approve`;
`once` publishes it once per call, writes an `attachment` of `kind: site` and answers `{url,
event_id}`, the url a random `public_id` on the publication domain. Without `HQC_PUBLISH_BASE`
the tool is `unavailable`; `INSTRUCTIONS`: only when the user asks, the link is public, give it
in the answer. §3: Artifact `kind: site`, `published_at`, `public_id`, a `site` never one record
with another (migration `0052`); PendingRequest `publish`, published at hub start when the
previous process stopped before it stored the result. §4: `attachment` with `kind: site`. §5.4:
the upload of a `site`. §6: `public_url` in the artifact object, `DELETE
/api/artifacts/{id}/publication`, `POST /api/artifacts` refuses `kind: site`, `publish` in `GET
/api/requests`. §10.1, §11: answered by the session owner only, never by `auto_approve`, nor on
Enter or Esc; the card names every hidden file and each hidden folder with its count. §12: the
publication domain, what it serves and with which headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, so that the page's own fonts, modules, `fetch` and wasm load from its
opaque origin; Web Workers, popups, forms, cookies and `localStorage` do not work), at most 32
files streamed at once (`503` beyond), the feed's card; deleting the publishing session or its
project takes a publication down, which the delete confirmations say, archiving does not; the
cleanup keeps a published `site` while its session exists. §2.1, §20: the domain outside Access,
the limits (the hub walks the archive's central directory itself before the zip reader opens
it).

### 0.207 → 0.208 (the thinking shows while it is written)
§4, §6, §8.1: while the model thought, the feed showed only the activity line, and the "Thinking"
line came when the thinking was done, together with the next step. With `--thinking-display
summarized`, which the worker passes, Claude Code streams the thinking as `thinking_delta` chunks
with text before the finished block; the adapter dropped them. It now sends each as an
`agent.delta` with `thinking: true`. The hub keeps the thinking being written apart from the
answer's text, sends it on `subscribe` as one such delta before the answer's, and ends it on the
session's `agent.thinking` and on whatever ends the answer's text; an input stored meanwhile gets
`during_text`. The client draws it as the collapsed "Thinking" line its `agent.thinking` will be,
a block of its own, not a row of the folded run of tool calls before it; the stored
`agent.thinking` takes its block, so a line the user opened stays open, unless it joins that run.
An input written during the thinking stands under it, live and once it is stored, as under the
answer's text since 0.108; while the answer's text is still being written, the thinking after it
stands under that text. §8.1: a `message_start`, or a response of another `message.id`, after
thinking deltas that no `assistant` thinking or text took up drops the thinking with the text
(`reset`), as after text deltas since 0.161. §4: the hub drops the texts being written of a session
it deletes. §5.2: the hub relies on a delta going before the outbox entries written after it, as
the worker sends them: a thinking delta after its `agent.thinking` would open a second thinking.
The hub has to be updated before the workers: an older hub ignores `thinking`, so it adds a newer
worker's thinking chunks to the answer's text it keeps for subscriptions, which its
`agent.thinking` does not end, marks inputs stored meanwhile with `during_text`, and passes the
deltas on as they came; its client, older too, shows them as answer text until the next
`agent.message` or the end of the turn. Checked on a test install (Claude Code 2.1.312, sonnet
5.5), at 1280 and 390 px: the "Thinking" line stood in the feed about 3 s before its
`agent.thinking`, growing to 543 characters as three bursts of chunks came (45 in all); after a
Bash call it stood under the folded run of that call, growing from 250 to 480 characters, and
joined the run once stored. 0.186–0.205 are taken by other pull requests.

### 0.206 → 0.207 (the permission card says what it asks and what it grants)
§4, §8.1, §10.1: the card showed a multi-line command as its first line when it stood right after
its call and as its last line otherwise (a subagent's request, another session's card, the
Requests list), so a script was allowed unseen; an MCP call showed the first of a list of known
keys (`message` of `{to, message, channel}`) with the rest as JSON in the subtitle or not at all;
"Always allow" and "Always in this session" did not say what they allow. `approval.request` now
carries `args_preview`, the call's arguments as `tool.call` does, and an option may carry a
`grant` (`place` `session` / `local_settings`, `rules`, `exact`); `place` joins the tolerant
enums. The card shows a Bash command whole as it will run (with its line count when its box
scrolls, and the cut mark only when the command itself is cut), its other fields under it, every
argument of another tool (not Edit, MultiEdit, Write) with more than one or with one that the
row's line would cut or run together, a note when the box of the arguments scrolls, and a line per
option with a grant under the buttons, naming `.claude/settings.local.json` at the root of the
session's git repository and the end of the agent's process; a rule of a grant cut to 256 bytes
ends with `…` within them; a request from an older worker, which has no arguments, keeps its
description line.
0.186–0.199 are taken by other open branches.

### 0.205 → 0.206 (the chat header reworked)
§6 client layout and `permission_mode`, §7.1.1, §17.3: the chat header's "More" menu held,
besides Schedules and Move to project…, the mode, the model, Rename and the browser; Pause and
Restart were only in the row's menu, Pause also for an idle session; Folder rules was a button
of its own. The permission mode and the model are now round pills beside the state, each opening
its menu: the mode a switch Ask | Auto | Allow all with the browser's item under it; the model
the Claude families, each with its versions in a submenu, "Another model…", the providers and
the worker's usage limits, the same menu in a new session's model chip and in "Switch model"
under a refusal. The title is renamed in place (a pencil on hover, on a phone a tap). Pause
stands before Stop only while the agent works, also in the row's menu; a paused session has
Resume in its place, and its row shows the pause sign. "More" keeps Schedules and Move to
project… and gains Folder rules and Restart session; Folder rules left the row's menu. The meta
row says "on <worker>". On a phone the header's buttons stand on the title's line, the state has
a line of its own, the pills another with "started by" after them instead of a last line of its
own, and where the session runs is in "More". The session column head's "⋯" took the list's
order, "Reorder…" and "New room…" and dropped Open in new tab and the favorites item, both in
the project's right-click menu (a phone, without the bar, keeps the favorites item); Favorites
has no pin, and the room's icon is two speech bubbles. Client only. 0.186–0.196 are taken by
open branches.

### 0.204 → 0.205 (a subagent's cards and rows on a phone: the task before the counts)
§6, §4: on a phone a subagent's start card cut its task to a few letters, as "Agent started:",
the type and the "background" chip took its first line, and `<tokens> tokens · <n> tools` crowded
what the subagent does now off the second; its row above the input cut the task the same way, and
so did its end card, its label "Agent finished:" and the counts taking the room. On a phone
both cards now say "Agent:", the start card without the chip, and the start card, the end card,
the row above the input and a background task's line show the token count without the word
"tokens" and the run time, without the tool calls (`155.3k · 4m 13s`). A computer is unchanged.
0.186–0.194 are taken by other pull requests.
### 0.203 → 0.204 (a message's Search, Copy and Quote are buttons of its own, and Add to quick messages)
§6: Search, Copy and Quote of selected text were the client's menu of a right click on a computer
and a "Quote" button under the selection on a phone, which a phone's own selection menu covered.
They are now buttons of the message that holds the selection, always shown (no hover), in the line's
flow so that they cover no text: left of the message's time, in the head of a message from another
session and of a room post, at the right end of a phone's agent message's usage line, at the right
end of a reasoning's summary. A phone has no row under the message any more. Search is a slot at the
strip's left end, hidden until the message holds a selection, so the line keeps its width. Quote with
nothing selected takes the message's first two sentences with "…"; Copy with nothing selected copies
the whole message, as before. The buttons are on agent, user and text-answer messages, a message
from another session, a reply to one, what the session sent to another and the reply it got, a room
post, the agent's reasoning and the messages of a subagent's history; Search no longer needs the
input. A right click opens the browser's menu.
§6 client layout, quick messages: a message the user typed has a button right before fork that adds
its text at the end of the project's quick messages (read from the hub first, sent whole in `PATCH
/api/projects/{id}`, nothing sent for a text already there); a text in the list is a check.
### 0.202 → 0.203 (a subagent that ends with its commands still running)
§8.1: a subagent of Claude Code 2.1.329 that stops while commands it started run on (a wait loop
that never ends) sends its `task_notification` with its report as `summary` and no `handback`.
The adapter took every notification without `handback` while the subagent's commands were listed
for 2.1.312's placeholder "This agent has not reported yet…" and held it until they ended, so the
feed had no "Agent finished" card and the line above the input said the subagent was running for
hours. Only the placeholder is held now; any other notification is the subagent's end at once,
and the commands it left get rows of their own (stoppable) instead of its row. A later
notification of the same task gives a line when its text differs, so the real report of a subagent
the CLI resumed after an interim one shows too. §5.4, §8.1: when such commands still run 30
minutes after the end, the worker sends the new `session.subagent_leftovers` once, with how long
ago the subagent ended, and the hub gives the agent a note naming them, as the owner's pending
input, so that it stops the ones no longer needed; the subagent's task and the commands'
descriptions are the model's words and go into the note as JSON strings, with the marks of a
room's and another session's lines escaped. §4: the hub is a source of `user.message` on that
frame. No migration.
### 0.201 → 0.202 (a subagent's line does not repeat its task)
§6 client layout: 2.1.312 sends a subagent's `task_progress` on each of its tool calls, with the
call's activity text as `description` (the row's `activity`), and the subagent's task itself when
the tool has none (ToolSearch, an MCP tool), so the line above the input read "Agent: Review
links, part A: Review links, part A" and the card in the feed had the task on both lines. An `activity` equal to the row's `description` is now shown as
none: the task alone above the input, "Running" on the card.
### 0.200 → 0.201 (a lost transcript write is shown, a quiet CLI exits by itself, Stop ends a hung CLI)
§4, §8.1, §17.3: Claude Code 2.1.317 and later write `system/session_writes_lost` (`error_code`
`ENOSPC` or `EDQUOT`, `lost`: `transcript`, `global_config`) when the disk was full, but only on
exiting with status 0, which a CLI that the worker ended with SIGTERM never did, and the adapter
dropped the line: a full disk lost the transcript without a word. The adapter now writes `system
transcript_not_saved` when `lost` has `transcript` (only the log, when the global config alone was
lost), and ends a process with nothing running (the idle unload, `session.kill` of a quiet
session, a move with no background task) by closing its stdin, so that it can exit and report,
falling back to SIGTERM after 5 s; a process in a turn, with subagents or background tasks, and
the other ends stay as they were. And Stop waited 10 s for the turn's end, SIGINT, 10 s, SIGTERM,
5 s, SIGKILL, 25 s in all, for a CLI that does not even answer the `interrupt`: it now waits 2 s
for that answer, and a CLI that gave none while the turn ran gets SIGTERM, SIGKILL 5 s later; one
that answered goes the way it did. Only the worker changes. 0.186–0.208 are taken by other open
branches.
### 0.199 → 0.200 (a cron job outlives an idle unload; a fork takes its subagents' transcripts; an `off_host` task is no work)
§17.3, §8.1, §5.4: three worker fixes. (1) The deadline of `idle_timeout` is the latest of the
agent's last activity, the time of its armed wakeup and the next fire of each cron job the worker
last listed (`due_in_ms` of the `kind: cron` rows of `subagents.live`), plus the timeout; a stale
wakeup does not let the process go before a later cron fire, a job with no known next fire holds
nothing. Before, only the wakeup was counted and the unload killed the cron job, which then never
fired. (2) A session forked from a message copies the transcripts of the subagents the cut part
names into the new session's `subagents/` folder, so the agent can continue them with
`SendMessage`; the CLI does not bring them on `--fork-session`. (3) A task of the CLI's
`background_tasks_changed` list with `off_host: true` (2.1.325, cloud sessions only) is not
counted in `session.state.background_tasks` and keeps no subagent as `parent_task_id`, as
`ambient` ones. 0.186–0.207 are taken by other open branches.
### 0.198 → 0.199 (previews of a question's options)
§4, §8.1: Claude Code's `AskUserQuestion` lets each option carry a `preview` (a mockup, code, a
diagram as text), and the question card did not show it. `clarify.request` questions now carry
`option_previews?` from `options[].preview`, by the rule of `option_descriptions`; the worker
cuts each to 8 KiB with a truncation mark. The client shows them as plain text in `<pre>`, never
rendered: on a desktop beside the options, the one of the option last under the pointer while
the pointer is over the question, so that it can be scrolled, or of the option with the keyboard
focus, else of the first chosen one, else the first one that has a preview, all of them
in one cell so that the column keeps the height of the tallest; on a phone under each chosen
option that has one. A question without previews looks as before.
Checked on a test install with Claude Code 2.1.312, Sonnet 5.5 asked for a question whose first
two options carry ASCII mockups: the `clarify.request` held both and `""` for the third. At 1280
px the first preview stood beside the options, the pointer on the second option showed its own
and on the third none, the column stayed 166 px tall and the options in place; after a choice the
chosen option's preview stayed when the pointer left. At 390 px the chosen option's preview opened
under it and the page stayed 390 px wide. A `<b>` in a preview showed as text. The answer reached
the agent.
0.186–0.206 are taken by other pull requests.
### 0.197 → 0.198 (a scroll up stays where the user took it)
§6 client layout: while the agent wrote an answer, a scroll up of the feed was taken back to the
new text. A move up let go of the bottom only while the feed's scroll range stayed (0.164), and an
answer being written changes it between any two scroll events; in Chromium the chat also followed
the bottom on every piece of the answer, which drops the rest of a smooth wheel scroll before its
scroll event comes. A move up in the user's own scroll up (a wheel or trackpad, a finger, the
main button pressed on the feed's own element, a scrolling key, and the scroll events that follow
within 400 ms) now lets go of the bottom whatever the range did; a scroll down keeps the range
rule, so the browser's move as images load still does not let go under it. While the user's
scroll goes on, the chat does not follow the bottom. A finger is told by its touch events: a
browser cancels its pointer once the touch turns into a scroll.
On an iPhone a scroll up near the top of the rendered feed also jumped screens up into older
history: 0.136 held positions back only while wheel events came, so under a finger and its fling
the chat rendered 60 older blocks and set the position that keeps the view in the middle of the
scroll, where WebKit loses it. A finger and its fling, and a bounce at the top that comes after
the last wheel event, now hold them back too.
Checked on a test install. Safari of an iOS 26.1 simulator, flicks up with a finger over a
300-turn chat: when the older blocks came in, the block at the top of the window went from event
543 to event 483 before, in 2 of 2 runs, and stayed after, in 2 of 2. Playwright 1.49, an answer
of about 900 words being written, twelve wheel steps of 60 px up: Chromium was back at the bottom

above it before and after. A WKWebView of macOS (Safari 27.2) with trackpad gestures, momentum

0.186–0.204 are taken by other pull requests.
### 0.196 → 0.197 (the agent reads its subagent with hqc_read)

### 0.191 → 0.192 (a turn the runtime starts by itself is not idle)

branches.)
### 0.190 → 0.191 (a pause stops the running turn at once)
§6, §7.1, §17.3 (user decision, 2026-11-20: "pause should come at once; a turn may run for half
an hour"): a pause during a turn let the turn run to its end, and only then the hub ended the
agent's process, so the session could go on working for half an hour under "Pausing after this
turn". `POST /api/sessions/{id}/pause` now stops a running turn as `POST /stop` does
(`session.stop`, the session's open requests cancelled as Stop cancels them) and ends the process
when that turn has ended, on the same `status` `idle` or `error` or turn loss as before. The

worker never got (its link was dead, it was away) is sent after its next `hello` while the turn
still runs, as the kill already was. Resumed before the stopped turn has ended, the agent gets
the note too (before, the turn ran on and needed none). The note now also says that a step the
pause cut, which Claude Code shows the agent as a tool use the user rejected, was the pause, and
to go on: on the test stand a resumed agent without it answered "You declined the run" and
stopped. Only after a pause that stopped a turn: after a pause of an idle agent a rejected step is
the user's own (Stop or "No" on a permission card), and the agent would have repeated it. §7.1: a
final text an interrupt cut off (`interrupted`: Stop, a pause, "No" to a permission request) is
no reply to an `hqc_ask`; the turn's `status idle` fails the ask as a turn without an answer
(before, the asker got the cut text as the answer). The client says "Pausing" until the process
ends. §3: `sessions.pause_cut_turn`, migration `0054_session_pause_cut` (0052 and 0053 are taken
by open branches). No frame or worker change. 0.186–0.196 are taken by open branches.
### 0.189 → 0.190 (the chain limits and the limit bar from the hub's environment)
§7.1, §7.1.1, §20: the two limits of a chain of peer messages were constants of the hub, so a
room that should talk longer than 20 posts without the owner, or a chain that should carry more
than 50 messages, needed a rebuilt hub. `HQC_PEER_HOPS_PER_CHAIN` (default 20, 1–254: `hops`

conversation after the owner's message; `HQC_PEER_MESSAGES_PER_CHAIN` (default 50, from 1) sets
the messages of a chain in all. §6: the share of a usage window from which the chat shows the

the hub serves as `limit_notice_percent` of `/api/me`, and at `0` the chat shows no bar. A value
out of range stops the hub at start.
### 0.188 → 0.189 (the activity line above the input, as "Main agent:")
§6, §17.1: "Agent is working", the grey box at the end of the feed, read as a message of the
dialogue. The main agent's row is now the first row of the live block above the input, as
"Main agent: Working", "Main agent: Running …" or "Command: …" for a shell command, with the run
time as the other rows show it, and "Run in background" is an icon button with a tooltip; the
subagents' rows say "Subagent: " in place of "Agent: ", and the block shows while the main agent's
