### 0.187 → 0.188 (a floating new-session button on a phone)
§3 User, §6, §6 client layout: the project a quick new session opens in is the user's setting,
`users.new_session_project_id` (migration `0053_new_session_project`, `Me` and `PatchMe` in
`hqc-proto`; `PATCH /api/me` stores only one of the user's own projects, else `404`), picked in
Settings → "New session"; it is the personal project until one is picked and when the picked one
is archived or deleted, so there is no "none". The first screen of a phone has one floating
button in that project's color that opens `#/p/<id>/new`, and the page exposes
`window.hqc.newSessionInProject()` for a wrapper's shortcut to do the same.
### 0.186 → 0.187 (a request answered from this client closes at once)
§10.1, §17.1: the card of a request closed only when the `approval.response` or `clarify.response`
event came over the socket, and on our hub that took up to 10 s after the hub had taken the answer;
the person pressed Answer again and got `409 request_closed`. The client now records the answer
when the `POST` returns (also for a secret given), shows the request as answered and drops it from
the Requests list; its chat shows the session as running if the hub still says it waits, and the
activity line counts the call from the answer. The hub's event, or a cancel, takes the record away
when it comes. A `409 request_closed` to a permission or a question makes the client fetch the
newest events, so the card shows what became of the request. A button's action ignores a second
press while its request is in flight. No hub change.
### 0.185 → 0.186 (a background task's output inside its line)
§4, §6, §8.1: every finished background command left a card of its output file standing in the
feed, a block of its own under the "Background task ·" line — since 0.181 the worker uploads
the task's output and follows its notification with an `attachment` (§8.1), and the client
drew it as it draws any attachment. Now the client folds that attachment into the line: once
the line is opened, it stands under the text with the usual Open and Download of an
attachment, and folded, the line looks as it did. Only the client changes.

### 0.184 → 0.185 (the worker's Claude Code signed in from hqc)
§5.3, §6, §4, §3 Worker: an expired sign-in of a worker's Claude Code meant going to the machine
and running `claude` there (a login over ssh does not reach the macOS Keychain). The owner now

sign-in page and the code the page gives, and the tokens stay on the machine (each machine has
its own login, as refresh tokens rotate). Frames `claude.auth`, `claude.login`,
`claude.login_code`, `claude.login_cancel`; `capabilities.claude_code.login`; REST under

### 0.183 → 0.184 (Fable 5.2 in the model menus)
§6 client layout: the versions of the model menus have Fable 5.2 (`claude-fable-5-2`) first of its
family; checked on 2026-11-19 to answer as itself on a subscription, and the `fable` alias
resolves to it.

### 0.182 → 0.183 (a full worker makes a session wait, not fail)
§8.1, §4: with `max_sessions` agents running, a start was `agent_start_failed` (retryable), the
hub tried `max_start_failures` times 2 s apart and failed the input, and the session went to
"Needs you" (#41: two new sessions and an old one in four minutes). The worker now takes the
start, writes `system waiting_for_slot` once, holds the inputs and starts the session as soon as
another agent stops, in the order they began to wait; nothing is stopped to make room. A kill, a
release to VS Code and a restart take the session out of the line.

### 0.181 → 0.182 (`hqc_read` reads a subagent's work)
§5.3, §7, §8.1: an agent knew what its subagent did only from its final report, and nothing while
it worked; the client's history of a subagent (0.181) was for a person. `hqc_read` takes
`subagent` (without `session`, one of the calling session) and answers with the subagent's steps
in pages of at most 100 events and 64 KiB, `agent.thinking` only with `thinking: true`, paged with
`before_event` and `after_event` and the `earlier`, `later` and `gap` of the result; `later` of the
newest page is also what the agent passes to read only the steps that came since. It asks the
worker with the client's `session.subagent_history`, which gets `before`: the newest events before
that one, under the same caps. Only the last 4 MiB of the transcript are read, as for the client.
An older worker ignores `before` and sends its newest page, so paging back from it repeats that
page; the client's history does not change. No migration.

### 0.180 → 0.181 (a background task's end, the CLI's own tasks, a subagent's request and history)
§5.4, §8.1, §17.3: a subagent the CLI marks `ambient: true` (no activity, the SDK says) was counted
in `subagents`, so it kept a session Running and its agent from being idle; it is now left out of

what it spent, the "Background
task ·" line nothing of how the task ended, and its output was only a path the agent could read;
`system` carries `usage {total_tokens, tool_uses, duration_ms}` from the notification, which a
subagent's end card shows as tokens and tool calls before its run time and the "Background task"
line at its end as the row above the input has it, the line says "Background task failed ·" or
"Background task stopped ·" by its `status`, and the worker uploads the task's `output_file` (a
regular, non-empty file at the path the CLI names, its last 2 MB when it is larger, the caption
saying so) as an `attachment` right after the notification. §4, §6, §10.1: a subagent's
permission card said "The agent wants to …", as the main agent's; `approval.request` and
`clarify.request` carry `subagent {task_id, description}` when `agent_id` names a subagent the
adapter knows, the card says "Subagent “<description>” wants to …" ("… asks" on the questions'
card, "Subagent “<description>”: run the command?" on a phone's sheet), and the subagent's line
above the input says "waiting for permission" while the approval is open. All the new fields are
optional.

§5.3, §6, §8.1: what a subagent did was not in the chat at all (the VS Code tab writes its steps
into the feed, where they scroll away). A subagent's line above the input now opens, under it,
its steps drawn with the feed's rows, fetched when asked and again every 2 s while it is open and
the page is not hidden: the
new `GET /api/sessions/{id}/subagents/{task_id}/history` asks the worker with the new frame
`session.subagent_history`, which reads the last 4 MiB of the subagent's transcript (one runs to
100 MB), opened as `hqc_attach` opens a file (no symlink, no FIFO), and answers with its newest
events (`{events[], truncated}`), at most 200 and 512 KiB as JSON, so that the reply never
reaches the hub's 1 MiB per message, past which the hub drops the worker's link; stored nowhere.
A refresh passes `after`, the `event_id` of the last event the client shows, and the worker then
answers only the events after it with `continues: true` when its page still holds it, which the
client appends (an older worker ignores `after` and sends the whole page, which the client takes
in its place; an older hub passes none). §6: every row of `subagents.live` whose `kind` (§4,
since 0.141) is `agent`, or none the client knows, is a subagent's and opens, also when the chat
has not loaded its `Agent` call or it was started by a subagent; a command's, a Monitor's, a
wakeup's and a cron job's (since 0.169) do not. A
worker before 0.181 does not know the frame (`error {invalid_frame}`, `400 invalid_path` to the
client), and one before 0.141 does not mark its commands, whose lines then open to that error
too. No migration.

### 0.179 → 0.180 (the CLI's requests: only a person's, the reason, a withdrawal, an MCP server's; its results)
§8.1: the Claude Code adapter answered a `can_use_tool` from a `session` rule or the folder's hqc
rules, and the hub's `auto_approve` answered it, also when the CLI said that only a person may
(`requires_user_interaction`, `matched_ask_rule`, `suppress_always_allow_rule`), and the card
offered "Allow for this session" and "Always allow" there. Such a request now reaches the card
with `human_only: true` (§4) and only `once` and `deny`, without `rule_suggestions`; §10.1:
`auto_approve` leaves it to the owner. §4, §8.1: `approval.request` carries the CLI's
`decision_reason` as `reason?` (at most 1024 bytes) and `display_name?` (at most 256 bytes); the
card shows the reason under its title and names the tool by `display_name`, an MCP server's tool
as `<tool> (<server>)` as before: the CLI's `display_name` of one drops the server. §4, §8.1, §10.1:
`control_cancel_request` of the CLI was not read, so a card the CLI no longer waited for stayed
open until the turn's end or, for a background subagent, its end; the adapter now closes it with
the new cancel reason `withdrawn` ("Cancelled: withdrawn") and writes no later answer, except
while a Stop or a denial that stops the turn is carried out: the requests of the aborted turn that
its end would cancel are then `stopped`, so a question can be answered by a message. §4,
§5.3, §6, §8.1: an MCP server's request for input (`elicitation`) got `error`, which the CLI
takes as `cancel`, and never reached the person; it is now a `clarify.request` with `server?`,
`message?` and, for a link, `url?`: a form's properties are its questions, its answer goes back
typed as `accept`; `clarify.response` and its frame carry `action?` (`accept`, `decline`), which
`POST …/requests/{request_id}` takes for such a request only, `decline` and a link's Done without
answers; a form with an object or an array is answered `cancel` with `system
elicitation_unsupported`. §6, §10.1, §11: only the worker owner answers such a request, anyone
else gets `403`: the server runs with the owner's credentials. §4, §8.1: what such a request
only shows is cut (`server` to 256 bytes, `message` to 4 KB, a question's text and header to 1024
bytes), and one whose `clarify.request` is over 256 KiB of JSON, which the hub would refuse by
dropping the worker's connection, is answered `cancel` with `system elicitation_unsupported` as
well. §4, §8.1: a form's question carries `required` (from the schema's `required`) and `input`
(`integer`, `number`), and the card's submit button waits for every required field and for an
integer or a number that reads as one, an answer a server on the MCP SDK would refuse; other
constraints of the schema are not checked. The plan of `ExitPlanMode` is not part of this
change. An older
client shows such a card without its reason and an MCP server's request as the agent's
question, a form without "Decline" and a link without its URL; an older hub's `auto_approve`
answers a `human_only` request, and it takes no `action`, so a declined or done request gets
`400`.

The results. §4, §8.1: a tool result over its 4 KB preview was cut there, and "Full result" of the
client never came: the worker set no `artifact_id`. The worker now uploads such a result's text, its
first 2 MiB, as a `text` artifact in `artifact_id` before it sends the event. A result's images were
only `[image]` in the preview; each is now an `image` artifact in the new
`tool.result.artifact_ids[]` (a list, beside `artifact_id`: one result may carry several, and the
hub's cleanup, §12, keeps the artifacts of every event's `artifact_ids` as it does for
`user.message` and `peer.message`). A failed upload, also one that takes over 30 s in all (the
session waits for it), leaves its field out. The result of an `Agent` (`Task`) call that completed
was the `tool_result` text with the CLI's trailer for the model (`agentId: …`, `<usage>`); it is now
the subagent's report from `tool_use_result`. An `assistant` text `(no content)`, the CLI's for a
reply without text, was drawn as the agent's answer; it gives no `agent.message` now, from the
adapter and the mirror (§9.1). §6: the addresses in a result are links, each labelled with the
address it opens (a look-alike host in its punycode form), its images thumbnails that open in the
viewer, and the page address of an `Artifact` call's result a line of its own under the run of
calls, seen while the run is folded. An older client ignores `artifact_ids`; an older hub stores the
field it does not know as part of the payload. §12: the hub keeps those files for good, as
attachments: a choice, not an oversight.

### 0.178 → 0.179 (what the agent is doing now: retries, compaction, thinking, long calls; the CLI's notices)
§8.1, §5.4, §6, §17.1: while Claude Code retried a failed request to the model API, compacted
the context or thought, the chat said only "Agent is working", the same as for a turn that had
stopped answering. The worker now reports what the main agent waits on as
`session.state.activity` — `retrying` from `system` `api_retry` (attempt, retries, delay,
status), `compacting` from `system` `status` `compacting`, `thinking` from `system`
`thinking_tokens` (the CLI's estimate) — until the model's next output, a tool call, another
status or the end of the turn, a new thinking estimate at most once per 2 s (the CLI sends one
about ten times a second, and each `session.state` costs the hub its queries and a
`session.summary`); the hub keeps it in memory (no migration) and drops it at the
end of a turn, at the agent's stop, at its worker's disconnect or `hello` and at a deletion, and
gives it as `activity` of the session object and `session.summary`; the activity line shows
"Retrying 3/10 (529), next in 8 s" ("Retrying 3/10 (no response)" when the next attempt goes at
once), "Compacting the conversation…" or "Thinking · ~12k tokens" in place of "Agent is
working". §4, §8.1: a subagent's retried request
(`tool_progress` with `subagent_retry`) puts `retry` on its row of `subagents.live`, and the
row reads "Retrying 2/10 (no response), next in 4 s" until the CLI says the retry went through.
§4, §8.1: a compaction that failed (`system` `status` with `compact_result: failed`) was
silent; it is now a `system compaction_failed` line with the CLI's error, and
`context_compacted` carries `trigger`, `pre_tokens` and `post_tokens` of `compact_metadata`,
shown as "Context compacted · auto · 153k tokens freed". §17.3: a tool call that ran silent for
longer than the hub's watchdog lost its turn although Claude Code sent a heartbeat for it every
30 s (`tool_progress` with `heartbeat: true`), which the worker dropped; at each heartbeat the
worker now sends the session's `tokens.rate` again, an event the watchdog already counts, so
the watchdog itself does not change (§4 `tokens.rate`). The CLI lines were read in its code
(2.1.312), not checked live; a failed compaction was seen live.
§4, §8.1, the CLI's notices: its and its hooks' messages (`system` `informational` of a level other
than `info`, `notification`) were dropped; they are `system runtime_notice` lines. A fallback to
another model (`model_fallback`, `model_consent_fallback`) was silent and the turn's `usage` named
the model that did not answer; it is a `system model_fallback` line "<model> → <fallback>: …", and
the `usage` names the fallback. A refusal with no other model (`model_refusal_no_fallback`) is a
`system model_refusal` line. A refusal answered by another model left the refused answer in the
feed: the worker reads `supersedes` and `retracted_message_uuids` and sends the new event type
`retraction` with the ids of the events it derived from those records, which the hub stores like any
event and clients do not show, nor the events it names (as the VS Code tab drops those rows); it
also ends the text being written, for which no message comes, and a fork leaves those events out.
Of its ids the hub keeps only the agent's own replies, thinking, calls and results of the session,
at most 1024, so a worker cannot hide a person's message, an answer or another session's event;
search still finds them. A
`system model_refusal_fallback` line says which model answered, and the turn's `usage` names it
unless the fallback's `scope` is `local`. A model switch the CLI refused was only logged while the
header showed the model chosen: it is a `system model_not_switched` line with the reason and
`model`, the model kept, which the worker keeps and the hub makes the session's `agent.model`; an
open chat fetches the session object again on that line, and a refusal of a switch the user has made
again since is only logged, as is one that names the model asked for (the CLI's fixed "set_model
failed" after a switch that applied). MCP servers that did not connect (not the ones the user turned off) and
plugins that did not load were silent: `system mcp_not_connected` and `system plugin_errors`, given
when their list changes, not before every turn. §5.4, §6: `worker.limits` carries `status`,
`rate_limit_type` and `resets_at` of the limit nearest, `GET /api/workers` shows them, and the chat
shows a bar above the input at 70 % of a window or once a limit is hit ("You've hit your 5-hour
limit · resets 18:00"), worded as the VS Code tab words it, though the tab shows the share only once
the status is `allowed_warning`; a limit or a window whose reset time has passed shows none, nor a
session on a provider. A `session.state.activity` of a kind the hub does not know reads as none, so
a newer worker's frame still reads. Before,
the limits showed only in the "More" menu. An older worker sends none of these, older hubs ignore
the new fields (an older hub stores a `retraction` as an event of an unknown type), and an older
client shows the new codes as text and a `retraction` as a collapsed card of an unknown event, next
to the refused answer it still shows.

### 0.177 → 0.178 (a bubble's note as an icon)
§6, §17.2: the note of a user's message, "joined the turn" (§17.2) or "instead of the request"
(§10.1), took a line of its own in a bubble and a run of bold words left of the time on a plate.
It is now an icon right before the time, in the time's line: two arrows merging for "Joined the
turn", a reply arrow for "Instead of the request"; the words are its tooltip and its name for a
screen reader. Client only. 0.173–0.177 are taken by other branches.

### 0.176 → 0.177 (a call's line shows its arguments and its result)
§6, §17.1: a call with none of the keys a line reads, an MCP tool's (`move (probe-bench)` with
`{"x": 90.7, "y": 80.9, "z": 85}`), was a row of just its tool; its line is now its arguments in
the order of `args_preview`, as the opened row shows them, each field as Claude Code 2.1.325 shows
one of an MCP tool's input: `z: 85, x: 90.7, y: 80.9` (§4: the shortest value first). A call's row
and the header of a group of one call showed no result until opened; the result now follows the
line after "→", on the same line: the error (without the CLI's `<tool_use_error>` tags), else the
result, as the opened row shows it (a change that went through shows none), a JSON object as `key:
value, …`, a lone `result` field (what an MCP tool that returns a plain value answers) as that
value, any other text as written (a number written again would lose digits, `1.10` reading
`1.1`). The result is often what the call is for, so when both do not fit it keeps three parts of
the width to the line's one, and the shorter leaves the rest to the other. Other lines that showed
less than they hold: a row's time was never shown, the worker sends no `duration_ms` (Claude Code
reports no time of a call), and now runs from the call to its result, as the group's time does; a
thinking line was cut at 60 characters and now at the end of the line; the "Running" line named
an MCP tool by its raw name (`mcp__probe-bench__move`) and now as the feed does, its paths
relative to the session's folder; an answered request's row showed the argument without the tool
("/Users/me/work/hqc/src/a.rs", an MCP call's would have been its bare arguments) and now names
both as the call's row does, a request card's title an MCP tool as `<tool> (<server>)`. Client
only. 0.173–0.177 are taken by other branches.

### 0.175 → 0.176 (an unrelated task offered its own session)
§7, §7.2: asked for a task that had nothing to do with its session, an agent did it right there;
only the agent could start another session, and the user was not asked. The instructions of the
hqc MCP server now require that on such a task in the user's latest message (not a question, a
quick check or one small edit, and not a message from another session or a room) the agent asks
the user first with its question tool "Start this in its own session?" — "New session" / "Do it
here" — and on "New session" starts it with `hqc_spawn`, whose description says how: the
caller's project, a brief, one line with the new session's address, the end of the turn. As in
the Claude app's Code tab, the agent decides what is unrelated; hqc has no tool, card or setting
of its own for it. A scheduled run reaches the agent as the owner's message, so it may ask there.

### 0.174 → 0.175 (a lookalike of a hub's mark, and the search of a room's agent)
§7, §7.1, §7.1.1, §15: the escape of `[hqc room` (the hub) and `[hqc peer` (the worker) was a
byte match, so `［hqc room` (fullwidth), `[hqc` and `room` with a no-break or ideographic space
or two spaces between them, and a mark with a zero-width or bidi character inside passed and read
to a model as the hub's own line; `clean_name` and the worker's `field` let fullwidth `［］｜＂`
and Cf characters through the same way. Both escapes are now one function in `hqc-proto` that
folds text before comparing it (invisible characters, Cf and the other Default_Ignorable_Code_Points,
dropped, NFKC per character, lowercase, whitespace runs one space; letters of other scripts that
look alike and lookalike brackets are not folded) and replaces the matched span, and names and
header fields drop invisible characters and take every character that
folds to a forbidden one for it. And `hqc_search_history` of an agent of a room left out neither
the room nor another agent of it, so a council agent could read a peer's answer through the
search that `hqc_read` refuses; it now leaves both out for such an agent (the owner's
`GET /api/search` is unchanged). A joined `ack` before the turn's final answer, which a council
agent's direct turn takes from the council, was already handled and is covered by a test.

### 0.173 → 0.174 (a send joins the running turn, and a person's input passes what cannot)
§17.2, §3, §4, §6, §7.1: the worker wrote only the head of the input queue into a running turn,
and a message of another session (`hqc_send`) never fitted, so it waited for the end of the turn
and the person's messages behind it waited too: a session with a 73-minute turn showed a person's
six messages "awaiting delivery" for up to 46 minutes behind one such message. Now the worker
writes into the running turn the first waiting input that may join: a person's input as before,
and a `send` (`peer.mode` `send`, no `schedule_id`) whose cap is not below the session's own
mode, with its peer header. A person's input goes past the waiting inputs in front of it that are
no person's and cannot join (an `hqc_ask`, a run of a schedule, a send with a lower cap), which
keep their places and run after the turn; a person's input that cannot join (a slash command, a
capped one) stops the search, so a person's own inputs keep their order. Nothing joins only a turn
whose own input is an `hqc_ask` (or another `peer` input that is not a `send`); a capped turn and
a turn started by a send take what may join. The hub keeps `joined` also on a `send`'s
`peer.message`, and the client and the fork's cut read a joined `peer.message` as they read a
joined `user.message`. This takes the trade-off §7.1.1 states for a room: agents in the same
mode keep joining, and a mode the owner raises after the input is stored does not hold it down.
A send joins only while the runtime is confirmed at or below its cap, and a send that becomes
the next turn keeps its cap on it and runs in its own mode. A joined input stays behind the last
waiting one delivered before it in the feed and in a fork's cut; if none was, it joined the
running turn and stands at its own `seq`. The hub takes the current turn's input (the chain of
its calls, the ask a lost turn fails) as the last delivered by delivery time, not by `seq`: an
ask that runs after an input that joined past it has the lower `seq`.

### 0.172 → 0.173 (a keep-place frame waits for its session's entries, not the whole outbox)
§5.2: a `session.state` and the answers to a `session.input` keep their place among the outbox
entries (0.171), but the frame waited for the last entry of the whole outbox, the entries of every
session, and each such frame made the connection load every unsent row to send a part of them.
After a mirror import the `ack` of one session's input waited until all the imported entries were
sent (256 un-acked at a time), and the direct frames queued behind it (deltas, replies to
`fs.stat`, the `ack` of a `session.start`) with it; nothing was lost, only late. The order is
needed only within a session and its transcript. The outbox now stores each entry's stream
(`outbox.stream`: the session's id for its events, `mcp.call`s and the worker's log lines, the
transcript's id for a `mirror.event` and a holder report; an outbox from before keeps `''` for its
old entries, which a connection sends in full before any direct frame). A frame that keeps its
place goes after every entry up to the last one of its session's stream or its transcript's (the
transcript: the holder report the mirror wrote just before a `locked_by: vscode` state must come
first, §9.3); one cursor sends the outbox in order, so other sessions' entries before that one
still go first, and a frame of an idle session no longer waits for the rest of the outbox. The
connection reads only the entries up to the frame's. A batch the connection is already sending
still holds the whole direct channel until it is sent, as before 0.171. An `error` answer to a
`session.input` (`locked_vscode`, an attachment or start failure, Stop, `unknown_session`) now
keeps its place like the `ack` and the joined `ack`, which matters for whoever reacts to a failed
delivery relative to a turn's end. Only the worker changes.

### 0.171 → 0.172 (the agents' room)
§7.1.1 (new), §3, §4, §6, §7, §7.1, §15, §16, §17.2: the owner could talk to one agent per chat,
and several agents talked to each other only when one called `hqc_send`. A room is a chat with
several agents, each a session of its own with its own model and system prompt: `POST
/api/projects/{id}/rooms` makes the room, a session with no worker and no agent (`room_mode`), and
its agents' sessions (`room_id`, `spawned_by` the room, titled by an agent's `name` when given;
their agents start with the room's first message). The owner's message in the room goes to its
agents as a `peer.message` from the room (`room {session_id, seq}`) without a peer header, with the
hub's line in front naming the room, the sender (an agent by its name in the room in double quotes
next to the address stored with the input, the name stripped of `|`, `[`, `]`, `"` and control
characters) and the agent's own name; `[hqc room` in the text escaped as `[hqc-room-text`); the
final message of an agent's turn that took such an input, as the turn's own or one that joined it,
is the agent's post in the room, and one that is exactly `NO_REPLY` its pass (`system room_passed`,
a quiet line); an answer an interruption cut off (`interrupted`) posts nothing and counts as a turn
without a post; a post wakes nobody by itself. In `council` the owner's message wakes every agent.
In `conversation` the agents speak one at a time in the room's order: the owner's message wakes the
speaker, else the first agent; the end of the speaker's turn (`status idle` or `error`, a lost
turn), with none of its inputs from the room still pending, moves the circle on: its latest post
since it became the speaker wakes the next agent, until 20 posts follow the owner's last message
(`system room_stopped`), else its pass hands the last post or owner's message on to the next agent
until every agent but its author passed, else the room stops (`room_stopped`, the turn ended
without a post or was lost); an ack for its input that opens no turn and comes after the turn ended
(`joined`, or a plain one sent again after the outbox) decides then; a post of another agent wakes
nobody; a post of a turn the CLI started itself, on an input already answered, is an aside (`aside:
true`), which neither wakes the next agent nor opens again a round every agent passed, and such a
turn's pass or runtime's reply writes nothing; the speaker's runtime's own reply stops the room.
A runtime's own reply is no post (in a `council` a `room_stopped` line too). Each agent's input
carries the other agents' posts since its previous one, in `conversation` the owner's messages too,
each under the hub's line `[hqc room <room> | post from "<its agent's name>" (<its address>)]` or
`[hqc room <room> | message from your owner]` after the line `[hqc room <room> | since your last
turn]`, and their files. An input from the room that fails delivery is a `room_stopped` line in the
room; `POST /stop` of a room stops its agents and leaves their inputs as they are, and a turn on a
message from before its "Stopped" posts nothing unless a later one joined it. The hub decides and
stores what a room does under one lock per room. A room is no target of `hqc_ask` (`invalid_args`),
of `hqc_rename` with `session` or of a schedule (`not_found`), and takes no model, permission mode,
browser or pause (`409 room`); an agent of a room sends or schedules nothing to another agent of it
(`invalid_args`), and the room line tells it that the other agents read its final message in the
room. The session object has `room_mode?` and `room_id?`; `system_prompt` of an agent is written on
creation for the first time, at most 32 KiB (`400`), a NUL in it replaced. A room's input that
reaches a running turn joins it (`joined`, §4, §17.2); an agent's final message pushes nothing, its
post in the room does, named by its agent, and so does a non-member's message there, named by its
sender (§16). The client lists only the room, with its agents' state on the room's icon in place of
the state dot, names the agents in the room's header with Stop and the sum of their costs ("$X this
room"), shows a line per agent at work at the bottom of the room's feed and a post under its
agent's title, has no Restart, Pause or Move for a room, and opens "New room" as a window like a new
session's: chips over the input for each agent (its name, model and prompt), the mode, the
workspace, the folder and the permissions, the first message creating the room. §6: the chat
header's "⋯" starts with Rename, for a room and an agent too. §7, §20: `hqc_room` makes a room as
`hqc_spawn` makes a session, each agent counted as a spawned session, its first message a
`peer.message` from the caller that counts as the owner's message does; `hqc_send` to a room from a
session that is not one of its agents posts into it the same way (an agent of the room sends
nothing to its own room), under the line `[hqc room <room> | message from "<its title>" (<its
address>)]` in front of a later input. Only a person's message starts a chain in a room, the
owner's message joining a running turn too; an input made from a non-member's message or a post
continues its chain, a post is stored whatever its `hops` (only the posts limit stops a
conversation), and it counts once in the chain's messages, the inputs made from it not counted
(§7.1.1). When a round ends, the room sends every session that wrote in it and is none of its
agents how it ended and the room's last two entries since its previous notice or its first message
there (the rest is read with `hqc_read`), under the lowest cap of everything said there since then
(a room's notice, `notice_seq`, §4, §7.1.1); the descriptions of `hqc_room` and `hqc_send` say so.
The agents see each other by their names in the room, quoted, next to their addresses, a name
stripped of `|`, `[`, `]`, `"` and control characters, and each is told its own name. An agent's
session keeps its name in the room (`hqc_rename` without `session` from it is `invalid_args`, and
the room line says so, §7); a post carries the files its turn attached since the input or the
agent's previous final message, whichever came later, so a second post on one input repeats none of
the first's, and in `conversation` they go on with it; a post keeps its agent's cap (T39), decided
when it is stored, and an input made from it carries that cap where it is below the receiving
agent's mode, the owner's message none; the posts in front of an agent's input cap it the same way,
the cap kept in the input's chain when it is stored, so what its turn sends and posts carries it
(T40); an archived room is unarchived although it has no workspace, and its agents' posts wake
nobody while it is archived; deleting a room deletes its agents' sessions; search leaves out an
agent's inputs from the room and finds the rest of its session by its address (§15); an input whose
room the hub does not find keeps the send's header; a repeated `client_op_id` hands the owner's
message again to the agents it did not reach. §4 adds `room_passed` (`from_session_id`,
`event.system.room_passed.json`) and the other `room_stopped` lines. §3 Event, §16 and §17.2 name
the room's input next to a person's message for `joined` and pushes; §7.1.1 says that a turn the
CLI starts by itself after a background task posts too, that agents take `provider_id`, and what
the client shows of the agents: their open requests in the room's feed, their rate and count on the
project bar. Hub migration `0051_rooms` adds both columns.

§7, `hqc_read` (owner's request, 2026-11-18: "make it possible to read a room and a session in
full, from the hub, not only from the same machine"): an agent could find history with
`hqc_search_history` (snippets of 160 characters) or read a Claude Code transcript on its own
machine; a session of another machine had no way to be read, and a room has no transcript at all.
`hqc_read(session, before_seq?, after_seq?)` returns the events of one session of the caller's
owner (archived ones, rooms and the caller itself too) as `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events` does, at
most 100 events and 64 KiB a page, with `earlier` and `later` to page on; no side effects; a room's
notice points at it for the entries it leaves out. An agent of a room cannot read its room or
another agent of it (`invalid_args`): it gets what is said there with its input, and in a `council`
it does not see the others' answers to the message it answers. `hqc_send` and the other tools keep
refusing an archived session and, but for a send, a room (`peers::target`); `hqc_read`'s lookup is
`peers::readable`.

### 0.170 → 0.171 (an input's ack keeps its place)
§5.2, §8.1: the worker sends an input's `ack` past its outbox, and its connection picked between
the outbox and such a frame at random, so the `ack` could reach the hub before events written
before it. The hub opens a turn on an input's `ack` and closes it on a final `agent.message` or
`status idle` (§17.1): the next input's `ack`, ahead of the final answer and `status` of the turn
before it, had its turn closed as it opened, the session not `running` while its agent worked on
that input; and the Claude Code adapter acknowledged an input the CLI takes at a turn's end
without an echo (a local slash command) after that turn's final message, usage and `status idle`,
so its `ack` opened a turn after the turn's end, `running` until the next turn or the turn
watchdog (§17.3). An input's `ack` and `session.state` now keep their place among the outbox
entries, after those written before them and before those written later, so the next input's
`ack` never overtakes the turn before it, and the adapter acknowledges a local slash command
before the events of its turn's `result` (the final message, usage, `status idle`). Only the
worker changes.

### 0.169 → 0.170 (a compaction's usage line shows its tokens)
§4 `usage`, §8.1: a `/compact` ends with a `result` whose `usage` has zeros but which costs, so
the feed drew `0 → 0 tokens · $0.267` under "Context compacted". The tokens were spent: they are
in `result.modelUsage`, which is cumulative over the CLI session, per model (live on 2.1.312). The
`usage` of such a `result` (no tokens, the total grew, a `compact_boundary` came) now carries the
growth of the `modelUsage` token sums over all models. The baseline is the one of the cost: the
sums as of the previous `usage` with a `cost_usd` of the process, or, for the first `result` after
`--resume`, those of the transcript's last `cost-state` (none: zeros), and none again after
`conversation_reset`, where the CLI starts `modelUsage` from 0 with its total; it moves together
with the cost's baseline, never lowered, and a total-only `usage` leaves it. Every other turn
keeps the tokens of `result.usage`.

### 0.168 → 0.169 (timers and scheduled work above the input)
§4, §5.2, §6, §8.1, §16: the block above the input shows more than subagents and commands.
`subagents.live` has `kind` `monitor` (a Monitor watcher, a command's row, `stoppable` as a
command's), `wakeup` (the wakeup the agent armed with `ScheduleWakeup`, the same one that holds
off the idle unload since 0.162) and `cron` (a job of its `CronCreate`) and, on the last two,
`due_in_ms` and no `stoppable`; the worker sends those rows, from what the CLI says (§8.1). A new
event `schedules.live`, written by the hub and transport only, lists the session's enabled
schedules with a next run (§16); it goes to a session's subscribers on subscribe and on every
change of the session's schedules, and a worker sending one is refused. The hub counts the kept
list's `due_in_ms` down as it does `duration_ms` and, when `session.state` counts neither
subagents nor background tasks, keeps the wakeup and the cron jobs in the list (the agent is
idle, they wait) and drops the rest; when it says the agent stopped, it drops the whole list.
The client leads the lines with "Monitor: ", "Wakeup: ", "Cron: " and "Scheduled: ", counts a
timer down to `due`, keeps its dot still, shows the block for a timer or a schedule alone, and
opens the chat's schedules from a "Scheduled" line. On a resume, and on the start of a fork from
the copied part, the worker seeds the cron rows from the transcript by the CLI's rule (§8.1). No
migration.

### 0.167 → 0.168 (model versions in the model menus, and the offer on a refusal)
Claude Code's own catalog of models (`initialize`, 2.1.312) gives a subscription only its
default and the aliases, so a version could only be typed. §6 client layout: the model menus
(the chat's "More", the new session's model chip) list, after the aliases, the versions a
subscription answers as themselves, newest first per family: Opus 5.5, 5, 4.8, 4.7 and 4.6,
Sonnet 5.5, 5 and 4.6, Haiku 5.5 and 4.5, Fable 5.2 (since 0.184), 5.1 and 5 (`claude-opus-4-1` is
left out: it is served by Opus 5.5); a session on one of them shows it chosen, not as a typed name. §4: the
runtime's reply to a model refusal is `agent.message` with `refusal: true` beside `runtime`;
§8.1 and the mirror (§9) take it from `message.stop_reason: "refusal"` of the CLI's synthetic
reply. The client offers "Switch model" under such a line while no message of the user stands
after it and VS Code does not hold the session; its menu has the models of "More" but Claude
Code's default, which a running agent is not switched to; a pick other than the checked one
switches the session as "More" does and the line asks to send the message again.

### 0.166 → 0.167 (quick messages)
§3 Project `quick_messages` (hub migration `0049_project_quick_messages`), §6 `PATCH
/api/projects/{id}` takes `quick_messages` (the whole list; blank, over 10 000 characters or more
than 100 messages is `400`), the project object always carries it (`api.project.json`,
`api.projects.json`, `api.projects.archived.json`), §6 client layout: the quick-message button
and its list in a chat's composer, and the section "Quick messages" of the project settings.
Saved texts the user sends to the agent with one press, per project; pressing sends at once.
0.157 is taken by another branch; migrations 0046 and 0047 by open branches.

### 0.165 → 0.166 (a watcher the CLI keeps by itself is no background work)
§5.4, §8.1, §17.3: Claude Code 2.1.312 lists among the session's background tasks, with
`ambient: true`, tasks that are no activity: its own housekeeping and every live-update watcher,
such as the one that follows the comments on a page the agent published with its Artifact tool,
which stays for the whole process. The worker counted them, so such a session stayed Running
after its last turn and was never unloaded by `idle_timeout`, and a move told its agent it
stopped background work. `session.state.background_tasks` now counts the tasks without `ambient:
true`, and such a task no longer keeps the subagent it names as `parent_task_id` counted: the
watcher of a page a subagent published kept that subagent running for good after it ended. An
idle exit now stops such a watcher with the process, and comments on the page start no turn of
the agent while it is unloaded. Only the worker changes. (0.157–0.160 are taken by open
pull requests.)

### 0.164 → 0.165 (an answer to an earlier connection answers no frame of the new one)
§5: the hub numbered its frames to a worker from `h-1` on each connection, and a worker answers
a frame under its id even after reconnecting: an input it held through a hub restart is
acknowledged when the agent takes it. On a test hub such an `ack` came under the id of a frame
the new connection had given to another session's input, and the hub marked that input
delivered and joined to a turn although its agent never got it; after a restart of that session
the hub did not send it again. The ids are now `h-<connection>-<n>`, `<connection>` the random
low bits of the connection's id; an answer to an earlier connection matches no frame and is
dropped, and the hub re-sends what is still pending, as before. 0.157 and 0.158 are taken by
other pull requests.

### 0.163 → 0.164 (a chat with images opens at its bottom in WebKit)
§6 client layout: in Safari and the macOS app a chat whose newest messages carry images opened
screens above its bottom, at the images. As the images' names gave way to the images not loaded
yet, the feed got shorter and the browser moved its position up; WebKit delivered that scroll
after the images had loaded and the feed had grown again, far from the bottom, and the chat took
it for a scroll up and let go of the bottom. A move up now lets go of the bottom only if the
feed's scroll range (`scrollHeight - clientHeight`) is what it was at the scroll before. On a test
install in WebKit (Playwright 1.49, four 720×1280 images in the newest messages) the chat opened
1372–1432 px above its bottom in 9 of 10 openings before, at its bottom in 10 of 10 after; in
Chromium it opened at its bottom before and after. 0.157–0.163 are taken by other pull requests.

### 0.162 → 0.163 (a SendMessage row says what was sent)
§6 client layout: a SendMessage call (the agent writing to a subagent it runs or to a teammate)
was a row of just "SendMessage": its arguments are `to`, `summary` and `message`, none of them a
key the row reads. Its line (its row, the header of a group of one call, the Running line, an
approval card) is now its `summary`, else its plain-text `message` on one line. Claude Code
2.1.312 previews the call the same way, but by the message's first line ("A 5-10 word summary
shown as a one-line preview in the UI. Defaults to the first line of a plain-text message").
0.157–0.162 are taken by open pull requests.

### 0.161 → 0.162 (`/clear` moves the session to its new transcript; a wakeup outlives an idle unload; a person's title at once, the CLI's during the turn, the slash commands with what they do; the mirror shows the CLI's service lines, command output and compactions)
§4, §5.4, §6, §8.1, §9.2, §9.3: after `/clear` the CLI goes on in a new conversation with a
transcript of its own, and the worker stayed on the old id: the mirror took the new transcript
for another writer's and imported it as a second session that opened with a raw
`<command-name>/clear</command-name>` bubble, the header's session cost fell to the new total,
and after an idle unload, a worker restart or a move the agent went on with the conversation
before `/clear`. `conversation_reset` now gives `system conversation_cleared` "Conversation
cleared" and resets the cost baseline; the first `system/init` after it with another
`session_id` makes that id the session's `runtime_session_id` (`session.state`, stored by the
hub, resumed by the worker's next start, a move and a fork), the process's records and inputs go
to the registry of own records under it, and a holder or another writer of that transcript
releases the session (live run `w1-clear`, 2.1.312); what the process wrote to the old
transcript before the switch stays its own until it ends, so the output of a command run right
before `/clear` is not imported as another session. The CLI writes the new transcript about 70 ms before that `init`: the worker marks the
folder from `conversation_reset` to `init` or the `result` of that turn, and the mirror leaves a
transcript there it has not read yet until then. The hub gives the events the
session has when its `runtime_session_id` changes the old id as `origin_runtime`, so a fork
before a message of the conversation before `/clear` cuts the old transcript, and one before the
first answer after `/clear` starts a new conversation without the source's events. The client's
header adds the last `session_cost_usd` before each `system conversation_cleared` to the latest
one, also when the agent resumed the new transcript later or the chat was opened again.

§8.1, §17.3: an agent that armed a `ScheduleWakeup` and went idle was stopped by `idle_timeout`
before the wakeup was due, and the wakeup died with the process. The adapter now follows the
`scheduledFor` of the main agent's last `ScheduleWakeup` result (0 — none) until the
`command_lifecycle` `started` with `wakeup_source: loop_wakeup` and that `scheduled_for`, and
the worker counts the idle timeout from the later of the agent's last activity and the wakeup's
time (live runs `x6-wake-*`).

§5.4, §6, §8.1: the title came at the end of a turn, from the transcript's last `ai-title`, so a
new session got its title when its first turn ended and a later `ai-title` took back a
`/rename`, and the slash commands came as names with `system/init`. The adapter now sends a
person's title, `system session_title_changed`, at once, reads the transcript's title every 2 s
of the first model turn of a new session or after `/clear` while the process has none (the title
sent before `/clear` is forgotten at the `init` that names the new transcript; a transcript over
4 MiB is not read then) and at the end of every turn, the transcript's last `custom-title`
winning over its `ai-title`, and the commands come from the CLI's answer to `initialize`
(skipped before) and from `system commands_changed` with the first line of each description
and its argument hint, before the first turn. New optional `command_info`
`[{name, description?, argument_hint?}]` in `session.state` and, only in an answer about one session, in the session object (examples
`worker.session.state.json`, `api.session.json`); the client's `/` list shows the argument hint
and the description after each name. An older hub or client ignores the field; from an older
worker the hub keeps the names alone.

§4, §9, §9.1, §9.2, §9.4: the mirror showed the CLI's own lines as a person's bubbles with raw
tags and lost what a command printed, the compactions and a title a person gave. Now
"[Request interrupted by user]" and "[Request interrupted by user for tool use]" give `system
turn_interrupted` "Interrupted", a `<command-name>…<command-args>…` record (also one with
`<command-message>` first) a `user.message` "/x args", `<local-command-stdout>` /
`<local-command-stderr>` and a `system local_command` record the new `system command_output`
with the output cut to 4096 bytes, a `compact_boundary` and the summary after it one `system
context_compacted` with the summary, its id from the boundary's `uuid`; the `title` of
`mirror.event` is the file's last `custom-title`, else its `ai-title`, kept in a new column of
the mirror's state file and copied when a transcript is moved. While the session's hqc process
is alive, a `system local_command` record and a compaction's summary are its own, not another
writer's. 0.150 and 0.151 are taken by other pull requests.

### 0.160 → 0.161 (Stop spares background subagents; an interrupted or early-ended turn says so; a queued input stands after the turn it waited through)
§8.1: Stop killed the agent's background subagents and workflows along with the turn: the worker
sent no `initialize`, and without its `perTaskStopAffordance` the CLI's interrupt stops them. The
worker now writes `control_request` `initialize` with only `perTaskStopAffordance: true` as the
first stdin line of every process, new, resumed or forked, before any input (the CLI applies it only
before the first user message), and skips the answer; the interrupt then stops the turn alone
(checked live on 2.1.312). A subagent is stopped alone from its line (below). §4, §8.1: a reply cut
off by Stop looked finished, and a Stop during a tool call left nothing in the feed: an `assistant`
text with `aborted: true` gives `agent.message` with the new `interrupted: true`, which the client
shows muted with " · interrupted" after its time, and a `result` with a `terminal_reason`
`aborted_*` gives one `system turn_interrupted` "Interrupted" line at the end of the turn, after its
`usage`. A turn that ended early for another reason (an error, `max_turns`, the budget, a hook) just
ended: the reason went into `status idle` `detail`, which the client draws only for `error`. Such a
`result` (an error, or a `terminal_reason` other than `completed`, `background_requested` and
`tool_deferred`) now gives one `system turn_ended_early` line in the same place, "Turn ended early:
" with its `terminal_reason` (the subtype without one), the API's status and its `errors`, cut to
300 bytes, and `status idle` carries no `detail`. A `result` with no tokens gives no `usage` line
whatever its `num_turns` (0.115 kept it for `num_turns` other than 0): a reply interrupted while it
streamed had an empty `0 → 0 tokens` line under it. §5.3, §10.1: `POST /stop` cancelled every open
request of the session, so a background subagent that went on got "No" to its permission request
and empty answers to its questions; with a worker connected it now cancels only the hub's own (a
move, a secret), and the worker cancels the requests of the interrupted turn when it ends, as it
did before.

§4, §5.3, §6, §8.1: with Stop sparing them, nothing in hqc stopped a runaway background subagent
or command but archiving the session. As in the VS Code tab, a subagent's line above the input, and a
background command's, now ends with a small stop button: the adapter marks the rows of
`subagents.live` with the new `stoppable: true` (example `event.subagents.live.json`);
the button sends `POST /api/sessions/{id}/tasks/{task_id}/stop` → `{sent}` (`write` level, as
`/stop`; a `task_id` longer than 128 bytes or with U+0000 → `400`), the hub sends the new frame
`session.stop_task` {session_id, task_id} → `ack` (example `hub.session.stop_task.json`),
fire-and-forget like `session.background`, and the worker writes `control_request` `stop_task`
`{task_id}`, whose answer goes only to its log. The CLI's end of the stopped task removes its
line and gives its "Background task" line, as before. An older worker sends no `stoppable`, so no
button shows for its sessions, and answers `session.stop_task` with `error {invalid_frame}`;
older hubs and clients ignore the new field.

§6: a message written while a turn ran that waited for a turn of its own (one written in the
seconds before the final answer, an answer to a permission request that ended the turn, a
slash command, a run of a schedule, another session's message, a person's input while another
session's question runs) stood in the feed at its `seq`, above the rest of that turn and its
answer, which never saw it, with "· awaiting delivery" as if the worker were off. An input
that came while a turn ran now stands at the bottom of the feed until the agent takes it, "·
queued" while `pending`; one the agent took into that turn (`joined`) then stands at its `seq`
as before, one that waited for a turn of its own where the agent took it: after the turns it
waited through, before the work of its own, a `joined` one behind it right after it. One
written during the agent's text (0.108) and taken only after that turn stood under that text,
above the rest of the turn, though the agent answered it in a turn of its own: it now stands
after that turn too, with the text of its own turn under it; one the agent took into that turn
keeps its place under the text. §6, §7.1 hub: a fork before such an
input cuts after the turns it waited through, and the files of a reply to a question that
waited are those of its own turn, not of the turn it waited through. §6, §17.1: a tool call
without a result stayed "running" for good when its turn was lost (the worker restarted, the
agent died), and the
activity line of a later turn showed "Running $ <that command>" with its time growing until the
agent called a tool. A call with an end of a turn after it is now not finished, marked as a
failed call, and the activity line looks only at the calls after the last end of a turn.

§8.1, §17.2: the last answer of a turn the CLI started by itself (after a background task's
end) was lost now and then: an input that came between that text and the turn's `result` (9–100
ms apart on the stand) dropped the text the adapter held for the `result`. The input now leaves
it held, as an input written into a turn of hqc's does, and the `result` ends it `final: true`.
§4, §6, §8.1: when the CLI abandoned a request whose stream broke and retried it, the live text
showed the start of the abandoned attempt with the retry after it; a retry that came back with a
tool call only left the abandoned text up until the turn ended, and every input of that time was
marked `during_text`. A main agent's `message_start` after text deltas that no `assistant` text
took up now gives `agent.delta` with the new `reset: true` and an empty `text` (example
`event.agent.delta.reset.json`): the hub drops its copy of the text, so a later input is not
marked `during_text` and a later subscriber gets no copy, and the client drops the text it shows
live, as the VS Code tab drops the rows of an abandoned attempt. The same reset comes before a
main agent's `assistant` (not `<synthetic>`) of another `message.id` than the latest
`message_start`'s while such text stands: 2.1.312 mostly retries a broken stream without one,
and that response has no `message_start`. Older hubs and clients ignore
the field and keep the text, as before. §10.1: a question of the agent that a worker restart or
Stop cancelled could not be answered: its card closed with its options grey. Such a card
(`clarify.cancel` `worker_restart` or `stopped`) now stays open while no message of the user
stands after the cancel and the session takes input, and Answer, once every question has an
answer, sends the answers as the user's message in the words of the VS Code tab for an earlier
question, `Answering your earlier question "<question>": <answer>`; the first message of the user
after the cancel, read as the tab reads it, shows the card answered or closes it; a card cancelled
otherwise stays closed.

### 0.156 → 0.160 (a session is paused and resumed)
§3, §4, §6, §7.1, §16, §17.1, §17.3, §17.4 (user decision, 2026-11-15: "wait for the end of the
turn, stop it, and then, on a button, say 'you are unpaused, X time passed' and start it"): a
session could be stopped only for good (archived) or restarted at once; Claude Code has no pause of
its own. A session's menu has "Pause session" next to "Restart session", and for a paused session
"Resume session" in their place. `POST /api/sessions/{id}/pause` sets the session's `paused_at` (hub
migration `0050`); the hub ends the agent's process as a restart does, at once with no turn running,
else when the turn ends, and then sets `paused_at` to that time (a process that ends another way
keeps the time of the pause). While it is set nothing starts the agent or delivers input to it, and
the inputs typed meanwhile wait on the hub: a `cron` run is skipped, an `at` run waits, `hqc_ask` is
refused at once, a running turn still gets its answers; the session's state is `paused`, below
`running` and above `queued`, and while the turn still runs the client says "Pausing after this
turn". `POST .../resume` clears it and, when the process was ended, stores the user's `user.message`
with `resume: true`, `[hqc] You were paused at <HH:MM> UTC on <YYYY-MM-DD> and are resumed now:
<elapsed> passed.`, and starts the agent with the same history; the note goes first, before the held
inputs. The session object and `session.summary` carry `paused_at?`. No frame or worker change.
0.157–0.159 are taken by open pull requests; migrations 0046 and 0049 by open branches.

### 0.149 → 0.156 (a fork is quick, and says so while it is made)
§6, §15: the events a fork copies go in without their search words and the hub writes them
once the copy is in, without the answer waiting for them, into the index but not into
`search_vocab` (migration `0048`:
`search_words` is no longer a generated column but filled by a trigger, `event_search_words`
computes what the column did). Copying 14 545 events of a long session took 9–12 s, most of it
the vocabulary and the words; on a test install the same copy took 5.7 s, without the
vocabulary 2.4 s, without search 0.1–0.2 s. §6 client layout: until the hub answers
`POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork`, the user's message says "· forking…" after its time and its
"Fork from here" is disabled, and the client sends no second request for the same message:
three clicks on a button that showed nothing made three forks.
0.150–0.155 are taken by open pull requests; migrations 0046 and 0047 by open branches.

### 0.149 → 0.155 (a call whose arguments are cut at 4 KB keeps its short fields)
§8.1, §9.1: `args_preview` had the input's keys sorted, so a cut at 4 KB took every field after a
long value with it: a Write's `file_path` after its `content`, a Bash call's `description` and
`timeout` after a long script; the feed showed such a call as just "Write" or "Bash", and so did
the Running line. The fields now go from the shortest value to the longest, values of 3 KB or
more counted as equally long and kept in sorted order (an Edit of two long strings still brings
the start of its `new_string`), an `Agent` or `Task` call's `prompt` still last; the client
reads a cut preview as far as it goes for a call's line (its row, the header of a group of one
call, the Running line, an approval card), so a cut command shows its first line, and a row's
count of the lines that follow reads "+N+ lines" when the preview is cut. 0.150–0.154 are taken
by other pull requests.

### 0.148 → 0.149 (the browser marked in the lists)
§6 client layout: a session given the browser has a ring in the browser's color and a globe in
the session list, and its project a dashed ring of that color on the project bar and on a phone's
list of projects; the browser's color is a status color of its own (`--browser`). Only the client
changes.

### 0.147 → 0.148 (the browser in a session)
§14: `browser = true` in `worker.toml` lets the owner give one session's agent their Chrome on
that machine (Claude Code's `--chrome` with the Claude in Chrome extension): its own tab group in
the user's profile, signed in as the user, plus the tabs the user drags into it; everything but
uploading files, under the session's mode; every other session runs with `--no-chrome`. §5.3
`session.start.browser`, §5.4 `hello.browser`, §3 Worker and Session `browser` (hub migration
`0045`), §6 `PATCH /api/sessions/{id} {browser}` (a change restarts the agent, as a provider's
does) and the chat's "Browser" in "More" and its header; §4 `system browser_refused`; §8.1 the
flags. The owner's case: an agent that looks through listings on eBay, AliExpress and Amazon in
their accounts and reports back.

### 0.146 → 0.147 (secrets in a session, iteration 6)
§19: iteration 6 is secrets in a session, `docs/ITERATION-6.md`; ACP and Hermes move to 7,
sharing to 8, the rest to 9 (the references to them follow). §14: `session_secrets = true` in
`worker.toml` lets the owner give a running agent a secret (the file `$HQC_SECRETS/<name>` of its
process, gone with it) or an ssh key (into the process's own ssh-agent, which every such process
now has, empty at first), and keep a key for the workspace (`$HQC_HOME/workspace-keys/`, apart
from the store of `ssh_keys`, loaded by every later session there); a passphrase is used by the
worker and never kept. §5.3: `secret.put`, `workspace.keys`, `workspace.key_delete`; §5.4
`hello.session_secrets`; §3 Worker `session_secrets` (hub migration `0044`), PendingRequest
`secret`; §6 `POST /api/sessions/{id}/secrets` (the hub keeps nothing: no event, row or log line
has the value; the answer's `note` goes into the user's message), `GET/DELETE
/api/workspaces/{id}/keys`, the composer's Secret form, the `hqc_secret` card, the kept keys on
the rules screen; §7 `hqc_secret` (a card the owner fills, from a password manager too) and
`hqc_ssh_keygen` (the worker makes the key, the agent gets the public half), listed only where
the worker gives secrets; §4 `approval.request.secret`, which the hub drops from a worker's event,
and `system secret_given`; §8.1 `HQC_SECRETS` and the ssh-agent of such a process. The owner's
three cases: a Wi-Fi password written into a device, a router's password once, the key of a
Raspberry Pi set up in the session and kept for its workspace. 1Password's `op` on the worker
is not done: the phone's autofill fills the form.

### 0.144 → 0.146 (a call's arguments as indented JSON)
§10.1: an opened call's row (and a subagent's start card) showed `args_preview` as it came, one
line of JSON with `\n` in its strings, so a subagent's prompt or a long command was a block of
text with escapes. The client now writes it indented, two spaces a level, and a string's lines
each on a line of its own under its key; a preview cut at 4 KB is read as far as it goes and
marked cut; a preview that is not JSON is shown as it is. Only the client changes. 0.145 is
taken by an open pull request.

### 0.144 → 0.145 (a reconnect does not reorder the session lists)
§5.4: the hub set a session's `updated_at` on every `session.state`, and after `hello` the worker
sends one for every session again, so a reconnect gave all of a worker's sessions the same time
and the lists showed them in the order the frames came, not by their last activity (in one hub,
100 sessions of a worker within 1.5 s after a network drop). Its `process_state`,
`runtime_session_id` and `locked_by` now move `updated_at` only when one of them changes; a new
runtime title or holder moves it as before.

### 0.143 → 0.144 (model providers, iteration 5)
§19: iteration 5 is model providers, `docs/ITERATION-5.md`; the ACP adapter and Hermes move to
iteration 6, sharing to 7, the rest to 8. §3 Provider (hub migration `0043`): an
Anthropic-compatible endpoint with one model, a user's, picked per session; §6 `/api/providers`,
`provider_id` on creating and patching a session (a change restarts a running agent), the
session object's `agent.provider`; §5.3 `session.start.provider`, §5.4 `hello.providers`; §14
`[providers.<name>]` of `worker.toml` (`base_url`, `api_key?`): the worker runs a provider only
by its name with the same `base_url` and keeps the key, the hub keeps the description in one
place; §8.1 the CLI's variables for a provider, the worker's own Anthropic credentials left out,
and a session without a provider exactly as before (an owner's gateway in the worker's
environment keeps working); §4 `system provider_refused`; §7 `hqc_spawn(provider?)`, a caller's provider passed on; §6 client layout: "Models" in Settings,
providers in the model menus, the header without cost. Checked end to end on 2026-11-15:
Claude Code over `qwen3.8-27b` through gpu-arbiter's `/v1/messages` (tool calls, streaming, the
prefix cache, auto mode's classifier). The pool of subscriptions of issue #43 is left out:
Anthropic's terms for Claude Code rule out routing requests through consumer subscriptions
against their limits.

### 0.142 → 0.143 (Stop ends a stuck session)
§8.1: Stop sent `interrupt`, then SIGINT to the process group after 10 s, and nothing after
that: a process stuck in a tool call that SIGINT did not end kept its turn, and the session
could not be stopped from the chat. If the turn still runs 10 s after the SIGINT, the group now
gets SIGTERM, and SIGKILL 5 s later, as a kill does; the next input resumes the transcript.

### 0.141 → 0.142 (selected text is searched on the web)
§6 client layout: the menu of text selected in the feed (a right click on a computer) has "Search
in Google" after "Quote" and "Copy": the text's results in a new tab. Settings has a section "Web
search" to pick Google, DuckDuckGo, Bing or Yandex instead; the choice is kept on the device, not
on the hub, so there is no migration and no API change. On a phone the system's own selection menu
has a search already.

### 0.136 → 0.141 (a line above the input and a subagent's cards say what they are)
§4, §6, §8.1: a line of the list above the input did not say whether it was a subagent or a
background command: a subagent before its first progress report and a command both showed a task
and a run time, and the client could not tell them apart either. A row of `subagents.live` now has
`kind`, `agent` or `command`, which the worker sets by the list the row comes from, and the client
starts the line with "Agent: " or "Command: ". A row from an older worker has no `kind` and its line
neither word. §6: a subagent's start and end cards in the feed showed an icon, the task and the
state, and did not say that a subagent had started or finished; their first line now starts with
"Agent started:" and "Agent finished:". On a phone screen 480 px wide or less the start card leaves
out the subagent's type, which the label would leave too little room beside the task. 0.137–0.140
are taken by other pull requests.

### 0.136 → 0.140 (a session dragged onto a project moves there)
§6: a session moved to another project only through "Move to project…", in its row's menu or the
chat's "More" menu, and the form always asked for the project and the folder. A desktop row of
the session list (the favorites too, not in Reorder) can now be dragged onto another project on
the bar; the project's tile, or its row with the name in Compact, is ringed while the row is over
it, and the session's own project does not take it. Dropped there, the session moves into that
project's folder when it has exactly one `ready` folder on the session's worker; with none or
several, "Move to project…" opens over the list with that project chosen; a refusal shows in the
list's notice, "Not moved «…»: …". Only the client changes: the move is `POST
/api/sessions/{id}/move` as before. 0.137–0.139 are taken by pull requests in preparation.

### 0.128 → 0.136 (a chat scrolled with a trackpad stays where the user scrolled it)
§12 Client: in Safari and the macOS app (WebKit) a chat whose rendered feed was short, as a chat
kept in memory often opens, jumped screens up under the first trackpad scroll. The feed was
within its top 400 px, so the gesture's first step made the chat render 60 older blocks and set
the position that kept the view in place, and WebKit, which scrolls on its own thread, applied
the gesture's next step to the position before that one: the feed landed some 3700 px above
where it was, the chat took the jump for a scroll up and let go of the bottom, and a second
render of older blocks went the same way.
There, while the user's own wheel or trackpad gesture goes on, momentum included, until 400 ms
after its last wheel event, the chat now sets no scroll position: following the bottom and
rendering older blocks wait until it settles. Chromium applies the next step to the position the
page set, so there nothing changes. 0.129–0.135 are taken by open pull requests.

### 0.128 → 0.135 (a subagent's start and end cards in the feed)
§6: a subagent the agent started was one row of a folded "N tool calls" group, next to the
thinking, and what it did was seen only in the list above the input. Its `Agent` call is now a card
of its own in the feed, in the project's colour, two lines that never wrap: its task, the subagent's
type and its state, running with what it does now, its counts and run time, in the background, done
with its run time, failed or stopped; and where it ended, at its notification or at the result of
one that ran in the foreground, a lighter card says how it ended, after how long, and the end's
text, which opens as Markdown. §4, §8.1, §9.1: to tie the list's rows and the task's end to the
call, a row of `subagents.live` carries `call_id` (Claude Code: the `tool_use_id` of the subagent's
latest `task_started`), and `system task_notification` carries `call_id` (the notification's
`tool_use_id`, else that of the task's `task_started`; the mirror: the record's `<tool-use-id>`),
`status` (as the runtime says it; the mirror: `<status>`) and `task_id` (the mirror: `<task-id>`),
which ties a subagent cut off by a restart, reported without the call, to the call by the `agentId`
of its background launch. The mirror reads those tags only before `<summary>`: a Monitor's `<event>`
after it holds a command's output. §9.1: the mirror missed a notification that came while a turn
ran, an `attachment` `queued_command` with `commandMode: task-notification`; it now gives the same
`system task_notification`, and like a `user` one it is own while the session's hqc process is alive
(§9.2). §8.1, §9.1: an `Agent` call's `args_preview` had its keys sorted, and a long `prompt` pushed
`subagent_type` and `run_in_background` past the 4 KB cut; the prompt now goes last. §8.1: in Auto a
background subagent delivers its report through `SubagentHandback`, and its line carried the
notification's `summary`, the CLI's note for the model ("This agent's report was delivered to you as
a message from …"), not the report; it now carries `handback_report.text`, its `warning` above it.
All the new fields are optional: under an older worker the card takes the subagent's state from the
call's result alone. The list above the input stays as it was, and so does the "Background task ·"
line of a command's or a Monitor's notification. No frame changes, no migration. 0.129–0.134 are
taken by other pull requests.

### 0.128 → 0.134 (a fork's agent is told it is a copy)
§4 `forked_from`, §5.3 `session.input`, §6 `POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork`: a fork's agent got
the source's conversation and nothing else; `system forked_from` was only in the feed. Asked
to rename itself, an agent of a fork took the source's address from the copied history and
renamed the source. The first input after the cut of a fork with copied history now goes to the
worker with `text` beginning `[hqc fork] <the forked_from text>. The conversation above was
copied from that session; this session is <its address>, separate from it from here on.` and an
empty line; a slash command does not carry it (the next input does), a failed input does not
count, and in a `peer.message` the note stands after the worker's sender header. The address is
the session's at delivery, an input sent again before its `ack` carries the note again, and the

message (no copied history) and other sessions get no note.

### 0.128 → 0.133 (an agent renames its own session without `session`)
§7.2: an agent in a copy of a session, asked to rename itself, called `hqc_rename` with the

and the description of `hqc_rename` now say to rename this session always without `session`,
also when the agent thinks it knows the address, since an address of this session in a fork's
history (an `hqc_rename` result, `current: true` in `hqc_list_sessions`) is the source's.

### 0.128 → 0.132 (a quick call does not swap the activity line)
§17.1: the line at the bottom of the feed turned into "Running <command or tool>" on every

### 0.127 → 0.130 (a session's agent restarted from its menu)
§6, §17.3: `POST /api/sessions/{id}/restart` ends the session's agent process and starts it

### 0.127 → 0.129 (Allow all, a third permission mode)
§2.1, §3, §5.3, §5.4, §6, §7, §7.1, §8.1, §10.1, §14, §17.2 (user decision, 2026-11-12: "a third
mode, Allow all", next to Ask and Auto, per session; Auto stays): `allow_all` is Claude Code's
`bypassPermissions` — no cards and no classifier, the deny rules and the `ask` rules of the
CLI's settings still apply, and the CLI still asks where it asks in every mode (its safety
checks, tools that need a person). It is chosen on a new session's "Permissions" chip and in the
session's "More" menu after its own one-line confirmation, only by the worker owner, and stands
out in the chat header like Auto. The worker runs it only with a setting of its own,
`[permissions] allow_all`, off by default and independent of `allow_auto` (review, 2026-11-12:
`allow_auto` is on by default, and the hub must not get a worker to run without checks, §2.1):
without it a session hqc asks to run in `allow_all` runs in the highest mode the worker allows
(`auto` with `allow_auto`, else `ask`, with a warning in the log) and `mode = "allow_all"` is a
config error; with it the worker starts every process that is not `--restricted` with
`--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`, so that a running session can be switched to it. T39
generalizes to the order `ask` < `auto` < `allow_all`: a chain's cap is the lowest mode of the
sender and everything up the chain, a capped turn runs in the lower of the cap and the session's
own mode (an `auto` cap holds an `allow_all` session down to `auto`), a switch during a capped
turn reaches the runtime as far as the cap allows, and `capped_by` names the first session in
the cap's mode for an `auto` cap too; T40 takes the lowest cap of the buffered messages in the
same order, and an input with an `auto` cap joins no running turn; a runtime below the turn's
mode with nothing asked of it (`plan`) takes a capped input at once. A schedule an agent in
`auto` made before 0.129 stores an `auto` cap that names no session: its runs name the creator.
What a capped turn leaves running (a background subagent or command, a wake-up) goes on in the
session's own mode after it, as it did for `auto` (a known limitation, user decision 2026-11-12,
§7.1). Without a mode of its own the header names none after a capped turn ("the session's own
mode after this turn"). Migration `0042_permission_allow_all` widens the checks of
`sessions.permission_mode` and `effective_permission_mode` and gives `input_caps` the cap's mode
(`ask` for the rows before). A worker older than 0.129 refuses a `session.start` or
`session.permission_mode` with `allow_all`, and a `session.input` with `permission_cap:
"allow_all"`, as an unreadable frame, so the workers go first, then the hub and the client.
0.128 is taken by another pull request.

### 0.127 → 0.128 (the kind of a file uploaded again, and "Open" of a Markdown file)
§3 Artifact, §6, §12: an upload of a file the owner already has under the same name returned

download. Such an upload now gives the record the kind it names; one without `kind` keeps the

`.markdown`, or typed `text/markdown`, up to 2 MB) has "Open", which shows it in the viewer;

### 0.123 → 0.127 (the background commands of the agent in the live list)
§4, §8.1: the agent's own background shell commands, a Bash call run in the background or moved
there, were counted in `session.state.background_tasks` but shown nowhere: the agent said a run
was started in the background, and nothing in the chat showed it running. `subagents.live` now
holds them after the subagents, in the order they became rows: the main agent's `local_bash`
entries of the CLI's `background_tasks_changed` list, not `ambient`, from their `task_started`,
and not of a subagent that counts, whose row stands for them. Monitors are left out: 2.1.312
lists a Monitor's task as `local_bash` without `ambient`, so it is told apart by the call that
started it, a `Monitor` `tool_use` named by its `task_started`. A command's row is its
`task_id`, its `description` from the list (the Bash call's `description`, or the command, cut
to 4096 bytes) and its run time since its `task_started`, with no `activity` or counts;
commands do not change `session.state.subagents`. No frame changes: a command's row is an
ordinary entry of `agents`, which a client reads as a row without counts.
§4 hub: the hub dropped the kept list, and sent the subscribers an empty one, on every
`session.state` with `subagents` 0; a session that runs only a background command reports just
that, so each of its reports would have wiped the rows in open chats and for a new subscriber.
The hub now keeps the list while background tasks run, and drops it when `session.state`
counts neither subagents nor background tasks. §8.1: so that an empty list lost with the link
does not leave rows of ended work while, say, a Monitor runs, the worker sends an empty list
that followed a non-empty one again on every reconnect, until a non-empty list or the
process's stop. The hub goes first, then the workers: under an
older hub a worker's command rows are wiped at the session's next `session.state`; an older
worker under the new hub sends no command rows, and its own empty list still drops its
subagents' rows. 0.124–0.126 are taken by other pull requests.

files rather than give paths. 0.120–0.125 are taken by other pull requests.

### 0.123 → 0.125 (a running command is moved to the background from the chat)
§8.1: the Claude Code adapter follows the Bash calls and foreground subagents of the agent

→ `{sent}` and `foreground_calls` in the session object and `session.summary`, kept in the

### 0.123 → 0.124 (a HEIC is decoded where the browser does not decode it)
§12 Client: a HEIC or HEIF photo attached in Chrome, Firefox or Brave on a computer went out as

### 0.119 → 0.123 (a fork before a later compaction of its source)
§8.1: a fork at a message before the source's last compaction did not start: the CLI resumes a

### 0.118 → 0.122 (a session's token rate)
§4, §5.2, §6, §8.1, §17: a new event `tokens.rate`, transport only like `subagents.live`, carries

the rate every 2 s when it changes, 0 when the process stops, and again after a reconnect. The
hub keeps a session's rate in memory while above 0, drops a worker's rates when it disconnects

### 0.118 → 0.121 (a turn the CLI starts by itself is running)
§4, §8.1, §17.1: the Claude Code adapter sends `status running` on the `system/init` of a turn

while the session's process runs (§17.3: not on one a restarted worker's outbox sends again).

### 0.118 → 0.119 (a search query with a NUL is refused)

### 0.108 → 0.118 (the summary of a compaction)
§4, §8.1: `system context_compacted` carries the summary Claude Code wrote when it compacted

older than 0.118 draws the summary as the divider's text, so the hub goes first, then the
workers. The summary is `system` text, so search indexes it as a message (weight A, §15): a
